The rest of the code in the VC App implements these four methods.
Note that by implementing this VC App using a shared library, it is easy to implement
additional patterns as needed. This can be accomplished by declaring and implementing
the new `extern' function. This new shared library can then be recompiled and distributed
to the design community.

Before examining the code that performs the data mining, it is useful to examine the
Makefile that is used to compile the VC App.

The following figure shows the complete Makefile:
Figure 30

Makefile

The Makefile is similar to a file that is used to compile a shared library. Some of the
specific items are highlighted in the figure. The source code is located in the file called
vcapp_fsdb_data_mining.cpp.
Also, the name of the shared library that is created is called libvcapps.so. Finally, it is
necessary to include the -fPICI and -shared options, which are required while creating a
shared library.
This chapter does not cover the commands used to open and close an FSDB file. Both of
these methods are simple and use the npi_fsdb_open and npi_fsdb_close commands,

This section focuses on the code that detects and reports on the scenarios described
earlier in the chapter.
The most common application of using FSDB model is to query the changes in value. The
following figure shows the general flow of querying value changes.
Figure 31

FSDB Flow

The application introduces some complexity that is not easily handled by this approach. In
particular, this application requires the traversal of multiple signals in a time-based fashion
simultaneously.
While this could be accomplished with the basic functionality that is provided by the baselevel (L0) FSDB reader methods, it would require the addition of `bookkeeping' code, that
could complicate the implementation of the application.
There is a class that is part of the FSDB NPI Library API that eases the traversal of
multiple signals in a time-based fashion, which is ideal for this particular application.
The following code illustrates the methods that are defined for this class:
Figure 32

Method Illustration

Most of the methods that are defined for this class are simple and easy to use. The basic
use model is as follows:
* Declare an instance of the npiFsdbTimeBasedVcIter class.
* Call the add method for each signal whose value changes are to be iterated
(simultaneously).
* Call the set_max_session_load method to limit the number of FSDB `sessions' that
can be loaded at the same time.
This method is used to control how much of FSDB is loaded into memory at a given
time. In other words, this method can be used to balance the performance compared to
memory usage.
In general, this value can be set to six. If the performance or memory issues are
encountered, contact the Synopsys support team.
* Call the start method, with the time range that is to be traversed.
If the entire FSDB file is to be traversed, then the start and end times for the FSDB file
can be retrieved using the npi_fsdb_min_time and npi_fsdb_max_time respectively.
* Call the next method in a while loop. This method returns a handle to the time of the
next value change event and a handle to the signal with which the value change event
is associated.
After calling the next method, call the get_value method to get the value of the signal
at the current time.

Handles in NPI FSDB Model for transaction
A handle is an opaque reference to an object in the FSDB model. The FSDB model
provides functions that operate on objects referred to by handles.
The particular operations that are legal for an object referred to by a handle depend on the
object types.
The NPI FSDB model for transaction contains 10 types of handles:
1. npiFsdbFileHandle: A handle referring to a file object.
2. npiFsdbScopeHandle: A handle referring to a scope object.
3. npiFsdbStreamHandle: A handle referring to a stream object.
4. npiFsdbTrtHandle: A handle referring to a transaction traverse object.
5. npiFsdbAttrHandle: A handle referring to an attribute object.
6. npiFsdbRelationHandle: A handle referring to a relation object.
7. npiFsdbScopeIter: A handle referring to a scope iterator object.
8. npiFsdbStreamIter: A handle referring to a stream iterator object.
9. npiFsdbTrtIter: A handle referring to a trt iterator object.
10. npiFsdbRelationIter: A handle referring to a relation iterator object.

npiFsdbFileHandle
A npiFsdbFileHandle is a handle referring to a file object. The only entry to create a
npiFsdbHandle is using the API "npi_fsdb_open".
When an FSDB file name is given and the file object is created successfully,
npi_fsdb_open returns a file handle directly.
The npiFsdbFileHandle for a specific FSDB file is unique. If you use npi_fsdb_open to get
the handle of a file object that was created previously, the return handle is the same.
Furthermore, you can use the API "npi_fsdb_close" to close an FSDB file and perform the
necessary memory cleaning jobs.
If an FSDB file is opened n times with npi_fsdb_open, you need to call
npi_fsdb_close n times to close it (only the n-th npi_fsdb_close works).
This mechanism is used to avoid unintentionally closing an FSDB file that was
opened and might still be used by other sub routines.
The traverse model of npiFsdbFileHandle is shown as follows:

npiFsdbScopeHandle
A npiFsdbFileHandle is a handle referring to an FSDB scope object. There are many ways
to get a scope handle:
1. npi_fsdb_tr_scope_by_name: Get a scope handle according to the input name.
2. npi_fsdb_iter_top_tr_scope: Get a scope iterator of top scopes and then iterate it to get
scope handles.
3. npi_fsdb_parent_scope: Get the parent scope handle of the input scope.
4. npi_fsdb_stream_scope: Get the scope handle of the input stream.
5. npi_fsdb_iter_child_scope: Get a scope iterator of child scopes and then iterate it to get
scope handles.
The traverse model of npiFsdbScopeHandle is shown as follows:

npiFsdbStreamHandle
A npiFsdbStreamHandle is a handle referring to an FSDB stream object. There are many
ways to get a stream handle:
1. npi_fsdb_stream _by_name: Get a stream handle according to the input name.
2. npi_fsdb_iter_stream: Get a stream iterator from a scope object and then iterate it to
get stream handles.
3. npi_fsdb_trt_stream: Get a stream handle according to the input trt handle.
The traverse model of npiFsdbStreamHandle is shown as follows:

npiFsdbTrtHandle
A npiFsdbTrtHandle is a handle referring to an FSDB trt (transaction traverse) object. It
can be used to traverse the transactions of an FSDB stream.
A stream can have more than 1 npiFsdbTrtHandle. A npiFsdbTrtHandle is used to
represent a transaction which it points to. There are 2 APIs to get npiFsdbTrtHandle:
1. npi_fsdb_create_trt: Create a transaction traverse handle for the specified stream.
2. npi_fsdb_iter_related_trt: Get an iterator of transaction traverse handles (pointing to
related transactions).

npiFsdbAttrHandle
A npiFsdbAttrHandle is a handle referring to an FSDB attribute object. Users can use
npi_fsdb_trt_attr to get npiFsdbAttrHandle which current transaction contains.

npiFsdbRelationHandle
A npiFsdbRelationHandle is a handle referring to an FSDB relation object. A relation
indicates the relationship between 2 transactions.
You can use npi_fsdb_iter_relation to get relation handles defined in the FSDB file.

npiFsdbScopeIter
A npiFsdbScopeIter is a handle referring to an iterator of scope handles. The iterator can
be created by using the following APIs:
1. npi_fsdb_iter_top_tr_scope:get a transaction scope iterator from a file handle
2. npi_fsdb_iter_child_scope:get a scope iterator from a scope handle
When getting a scope iterator, user can use the API "npi_fsdb_iter_scope_next" to
traverse scope handles. After iterating the last scope handle, the iterator becomes invalid
and freed automatically.
In the middle of iterating scopes, users can also use the API "npi_fsdb_iter_scope_stop" to
manually stop and free the iterator.

npiFsdbStreamIter
A npiFsdbStreamIter is a handle referring to an iterator of stream handles. The iterator can
be created by using the following API:
* npi_fsdb_iter_stream: Get a stream iterator from a scope handle
When getting a stream iterator, you can use the API "npi_fsdb_iter_stream_next" to
traverse stream handles.
After iterating the last stream handle, the iterator becomes invalid and freed automatically.
In the middle of iterating streams, you can also use the API "npi_fsdb_iter_stream_stop" to
manually stop and free the iterator.

npiFsdbTrtIter
A npiFsdbTrtIter is a handle referring to an iterator of trt handles. The iterator can be
created by using the following API:
* npi_fsdb_iter_related_trt: Get a trt iterator from a trt handle.
When getting a trt iterator, you can use the API "npi_fsdb_iter_trt_next" to traverse trt
handles.
After iterating the last trt handle, the iterator becomes invalid and freed automatically. In
the middle of iterating trts, users can also use the API "npi_fsdb_iter_trt_stop" to manually
stop and free the iterator.

npiFsdbRelationIter
A npiFsdbRelationIter is a handle referring to an iterator of relation handles. The iterator
can be created by using the following API:
* npi_fsdb_iter_relation: Get a relation iterator from a file handle.

When getting a relation iterator, you can use the API "npi_fsdb_iter_relation_next" to
traverse relation handles.
After iterating the last relation handle, the stream handle becomes invalid and
freed automatically. In the middle of iterating relations, you can also use the API
"npi_fsdb_iter_relation_stop" to manually stop and free the iterator.

Get the attribute value of corresponding

FSDB value struct (used in C/C++).

Generally, an FSDB value can be represented in various formats. npiFsdbValueType is
used to identify the expected value format of "npi_fsdb_trt_attr_value". npiFsdbValueType
has the following literals:
1. npiFsdbBinStrVal: string of binary format (for example, "1111" for 4`d15)
2. npiFsdbOctStrVal: string of octal format (for example, "17" for 4'd15)
3. npiFsdbDecStrVal: string of decimal format (for example, "15" for 4`d15)
4. npiFsdbHexStrVal: string of hex format (for example, "f" for 4`d15)
5. npiFsdbSintVal: signed integer type (for example, -1 for 4'd15)
6. npiFsdbUintVal: unsigned integer type (for example, 15 for 4'd15)
7. npiFsdbRealVal: double type (for example, -1.234E+01)
8. npiFsdbStringVal: ASCII string type (for example, Synopsys)
9. npiFsdbEnumStrVal: string of enum literal (for example,, "R" for 0 in enum {R, G, B})
10. npiFsdbSint64Val: signed 64-bit integer type (for example,, -1 for 64'd15)
11. npiFsdbUint64Val: unsigned 64-bit integer type (for example,, 15 for 64'd15)
12. npiFsdbObjTypeVal: auto set the closest format of the object (currently for transaction
FSDB only)

The details of how npi_fsdb_trt_attr_value gets the FSDB value according to the format
setting are described in "npi_fsdb_trt_attr_value".

FSDB value struct.
npi_fsdb_trt_attr_value

Get the attribute value of corresponding
transaction

The npiFsdbValue structure is defined in npi_fsdb.h.
typedef struct npiFsdbValue {
npiFsdbValType format;
union {
const NPI_BYTE8* str;
NPI_INT32 sint;
NPI_UINT32 uint;
NPI_INT64 sint64;
NPI_UINT64 uint64;
double real;
} npiFsdbValue;

The format of the value is set by the format field of the structure before calling
npi_fsdb_trt_attr_value.
The details of how npi_fsdb_trt_attr_value gets the FSDB value according to the format
setting is described in "npi_fsdb_trt_attr_value".

Flow of Query Transactions in an FSDB File
The most common application using FSDB model is to query transactions. The following
figure shows the general flow of querying transactions:

title: 42 - a - 1
text:
1. Open an FSDB file: The essential step for using the FSDB model is to open an FSDB
You can input a string representing an FSDB file to the API "npi_fsdb_open" to get a
file handle.

2. Get stream handles: An FSDB stream handle can be obtained from traverse APIs
(npi_fsdb_iter_top_tr_scope, npi_fsdb_parent_scope, npi_fsdb_iter_child_scope,
npi_fsdb_iter_stream, npi_fsdb_stream_scope, npi_fsdb_trt_stream) or from a given
name for the API "npi_fsdb_stream _by_name".
3. Create trt (transaction traverse) handles): A stream usually contains many
transactions in an FSDB file. A transaction traverse (trt) handle is used to traverse
those transactions.
A stream can have multiple trt handles at the same time. The APIs to create trt handles
are "npi_fsdb_create_trt"and "npi_fsdb_iter_related_trt".
4. Load transactions: Before traversing trt, users need to load transactions into memory
first.
The related APIs are "npi_fsdb_add_to_stream_list", "npi_fsdb_load_trans",
"npi_fsdb_reset_stream_list", "npi_fsdb_unload_trans".
If transactions of a stream are not loaded, the trt handle cannot perform any
traverse.
5. Traverse trt: With a trt handle, you can use trt traverse APIs (npi_fsdb_goto_time,
npi_fsdb_goto_first, npi_fsdb_goto_next, npi_fsdb_goto_prev) to move the index of the
trt handle.
The time and attribute values of the corresponding transaction can be queried by
"npi_fsdb_trt_time" and "npi_fsdb_trt_time" respectively.
6. Close the FSDB file: The last step of the flow is to close the FSDB file.
The API "npi_fsdb_close" can perform this operation and clean up the memory used for
this FSDB file.

Time Scale Unit
The time scale unit in an FSDB file is fixed. Users can query the scale unit through
"npi_fsdb_file_property_str".
The time value used in npi_fsdb_goto_time and npi_fsdb_vct_time is associated with the
scale unit.

TRT Traversing Behavior
Every time a trt handle is created, you need to call npi_fsdb_goto_time or
npi_fsdb_goto_first to initialize the index to the point of interest.

Although the use of npi_fsdb_goto_time needs to specify an expected time for jumping,
the specified time might or might not have transactions in the FSDB file.
The function changes the index of trt to the last transaction (according to begin time) if
In the following figure, the whole simulation run is from time 0 to time 110, and a stream
has 3 transactions at time 20 and 50:

1. goto_time (19): Failed to set index since there is no transaction before time 20.
2. goto_time (20): trt points to Trans_2.
3. goto_time (20) + goto_prev: trt points to Trans_1.
4. goto_time (20) + goto_next: trt points to Trans_3.
5. goto_time (31): trt points to Trans_2.
6. goto_time (49): trt points to Trans_2.
7. goto_time (50): trt points to Trans_3.
8. goto_time (110): trt points to Trans_3.
9. goto_first: trt points to Trans_1.

Query Related Transactions
An FSDB file often contains four kinds of default relations ("parent-child", "belong-to",
"succ-predecessor", and "annotate-to") and other user-defined relations. They can be
obtained by API"npi_fsdb_iter_relation".
Each relation handle describes the bidirectional relation between 2 transactions. You can
query related transactions from one transaction with API "npi_fsdb_iter_related_trt".

Memory Management
Generally, the API npi_fsdb_close performs the necessary clean up jobs and free memory.
That is, all FSDB objects and trt handles related to the file handle and transactions is freed
from memory.
However, sometimes users might want to clean the memory before calling npi_fsdb_close
for resource issues. The 2 APIs, npi_fsdb_release_trt and npi_fsdb_unload_trans, are
used for this goal.
First, the memory usage in the FSDB model is introduced. The following figure shows the
concept of the memory usage:
Figure 44

Memory Usage in the FSDB Model

The file, scope, and stream objects cannot be freed by the user before calling
npi_fsdb_close. You can free the trt handles and loaded transactions. On the one hand,
the creation of the trt handle is explicit by calling npi_fsdb_create_trt.
On the other hand, the transactions are loaded to memory explicitly by
npi_fsdb_load_trans. Loading transactions to the memory can be seen as decompressing
a session of the FSDB database into memory.
If you know some trt handles and their related transactions are no longer needed, they
can call npi_fsdb_release_trt first to invalidate and free the trt handles and then perform
npi_fsdb_unload_trans to actually remove the transactions.

Support and Limitations

npi_fsdb_unload_trans does not remove transactions that are still pointed to
valid trt handles.

Load Transactions
Before perform transaction traversing, users need to load transactions for the
corresponding stream.
The related APIs for this function are npi_fsdb_add_to_stream_list, npi_fsdb_load_trans,
and npi_fsdb_reset_stream_list. Each FSDB file handle has a dedicated stream list for this
function and the stream list is empty initially.
You can call npi_fsdb_add_to_stream_list to add streams into the list. The API
npi_fsdb_load_trans loads transactions of those streams in the list.
If you want to load a different set of streams, you can call npi_fsdb_reset_stream_list to
clean the stream list and use npi_fsdb_add_to_stream_list to build another stream set.

Support and Limitations
Supported FSDB Files
1. The NPI FSDB model does not support interactive mode for transaction FSDB (that
is, the NPI FSDB model cannot be used to traverse an FSDB file when it is still being
dumped).
2. The NPI FSDB model does not support virtual file for transaction FSDB.

an FSDB file. There exist some common items in the transaction data, such as scopes,

riter Model
* Illegal Cases of Different Handles

NPI FSDB Transaction Writer Model helps the users to dump transaction related data into
an FSDB file. There exist some common items in the transaction data, such as scopes,
streams, and transactions with several attributes. All the essential items can be dumped
into an FSDB file using the corresponding APIs, and it guarantees the FSDB file can
be read successfully through either the FSDB Transaction Reader Model or any of the
Synopsys transaction tools.
Refer to the API Reference to see the entire list of APIs that are used in the FSDB
Transaction Writer model.

The following list of APIs are available in all NPI FSDB Transaction Writer models. Note
that the result of each API example is obtained by running the Transaction Reader
Program. For details, see FSDB Transaction Reader Program Files.

This section summarizes the Verdi transaction data type categories and their definitions,
including Transaction, Stream, Attribute, and Transaction Relation.
Transaction

Transaction is an entry of data input by user code (such as, UVM message) and it contains
attributes of different data types. For maximum flexibility, transactions can be in different
types. The predefined transaction types are:
* Message
Regular transactions for printf-like logging purpose. The transaction in this type is set
as a 0-time transaction automatically, which means the end time of this transaction is
set equal to the begin time of the transaction.
* Action
A 0-time transaction for recording some Actions (such as, read, write, interrupt).
The transaction whose type is action is set as 0-time automatically. Several Action
transactions can be formed into a Group transaction by adding the belong_to relation
between the Action transaction and the Group transaction.
* Transaction
A general transaction with a begin time and an end time. Transaction can be set as 0time manually by setting the end time and the begin time in the same value.
* Group
A group contains several transactions (usually of Action type). The begin time of this
transaction is set as the begin time of its first member transaction. Also, the end time of
this transaction is set as the end time of its last member transaction.
Stream
A Stream is used to organize (or record as a group in the FSDB file) a temporal sequence
of transactions grouped by some criteria, for example, transactions originating from
the same UVM component can be put into one stream. Different streams cannot share
the same transaction. Some streams have hierarchies (such as, following the UVM
component hierarchy), some do not (such as, UVM phases and objections). Streams
might form different hierarchies (such as, UVM component hierarchy and sequence
hierarchy).
An Attribute is a characteristic or property of a specific scope, stream, or transaction.

A Relation is a link between two transactions. It can be defined using the API

Transaction Relation
A Relation is a link between two transactions. It can be defined using the API
npi_fsdbw_add_relation(npiFsdbwRel rel, npiFsdbwTransHandle Master,
npiFsdbwTransHandle Slave).
The parameter rel can be

* npiFsdbwBelongTo
It indicates the belong relation between two transactions, that is, first transaction
Master belongs to second transaction Slave. The transaction Slave can only be in
group type and the transaction Master cannot be in group type. In practical terms,
Master is always in action type and Slave has several transactions belonging to it.
* npiFsdbwAnnotateTo
It indicates the annotative relation between two transactions, that is, first transaction
Master (annotator) annotates to second transaction Slave (annotate). Master can only
be in message type.
* npiFsdbwParentChild
It indicates the layering relation between two transactions, that is, first transaction
Master is a parent and transaction Slave is a child. This relation is valid only if both
Master and Slave are in transaction type. Master (parent) and Slave (child) in different
streams is allowed for this relation.
* npiFsdbwPredSucc
It indicates the ordering/triggering relation between two transactions, that is, first
transaction Master is a predecessor and transaction Slave is a successor. The begin
time of the transaction Master should be less than the begin time of the transaction
Slave.
* npiFsdbwAnyString
It indicates the user can define the relation between two transactions. The provided rel
should be in type of character pointer (char*).

* npiFsdbwHex
Represents the hexadecimal system for attribute value.
* npiFsdbwUnsigned
Represents unsigned for attribute value.

typedef enum npiFsdbwTransType
FSDB Transaction Writer transaction type.
npiFsdbwTransType is used to identify the predefined transaction type.
npiFsdbwTransType has the following literals:
* npiFsdbwTransMessage
Regular transactions for printf-like logging purpose. The transaction in this type is set
as a 0-time transaction automatically, which means the end time of this transaction is
set equal to the begin time of the transaction.
* npiFsdbwTransAction
A 0-time transaction for recording some actions (such as, read, write, interrupt).
The transaction whose type is action is set as 0-time automatically. Several Action
transactions can be formed into a Group transaction by adding the belong_to relation
between the Action transaction and the Group transaction.
* npiFsdbwTransTransaction
A general transaction with a begin time and an end time. Transaction can be set as 0time manually by setting the end time and the begin time in same value.

* npiFsdbwTransGroup
A group contains several transactions (usually of Action type). The begin time of this
transaction is set as the begin time of its first member transaction. Also, the end time of
this transaction is set as the end time of its last member transaction.

Limitations of the NPI FSDB Transaction Writer Model

Limitations of the NPI FSDB Transaction Writer Model
NPI FSDB Transaction Writer model can dump FSDB files in C language and have the
corresponding TCL commands.
The following are the limitations of the NPI FSDB Transaction Writer model:
* This model is not supported in SystemVerilog, SystemC, and VHDL.
* FSDB files with the same file name are not allowed. Each FSDB file created through
this model must have a unique name.

Illegal Cases of Different Handles
Most APIs check handle validation to ensure the provided handle is valid.
If the handle is invalid, the API returns an error message. Several reasons can cause this
* Use the handle which is not created by calling the corresponding API. The APIs for
creating a handle are as follows:
File handle: npi_fsdbw_open
Stream handle: npi_fsdbw_stream_begin
Transaction handle: npi_fsdbw_trans_begin
* Use the handle which has already closed. The APIs for closing a handle are as follows:
File handle: npi_fsdbw_close
Stream handle: npi_fsdbw_stream_end
Transaction handle: npi_fsdbw_trans_end
For some APIs, the given handles must already be closed before use. Otherwise, an error
is issued.
The APIs are listed as follows:
* npi_fsdbw_trans_begin(npiFsdbwStreamHandle stream,): The provided stream
handle stream must be closed in advance.

Data Types of Attributes

Data Types of Attributes
The allowed attribute data types are listed as follows:
* NPI_BYTE8: It represents char type. The size is 8 bits.
* NPI_INT16: It represents short integer type. The size is 16 bits.
* NPI_INT32: It represents integer type. The size is 32 bits.
* NPI_INT64: It represents long long integer type. The size is 64 bits.
* const char*: It represents bit vector and the bit value can be 0, 1, X(x), Z(z).
Also, the bit vector is a signed number, which means that the most significant
bit is a sign bit. For example, '11110' is considered as -2 instead of 30. Only
npi_fsdbw_trans_add_bit_vector_attr supports this type.
* float
* double
* string
If any other data type is provided by users, a compile error is issued. For example, if the
attribute in structure type defined by users is provided, an error message is issued while
compiling the program.
Note that there are four types integer with different size (8bits, 16bits, 32bits, and 64bits).
The given attribute might be shown with different size on representation of Synopsys
transaction tool.

* npiFsdbwFileObj
It is an FSDB file object. You can use the functions of this object for manipulation of
FSDB writing tasks.
* npiFsdbwSigObj
It is an object to indicate a unique signal. You can use this object for writing values.
* npiFsdbwDtObj
It is an object to indicate a data type. You can create your own data types or use predefined data types to create corresponding signals.

General Use Flow in NPI FSDB Writer Model
The general flow of using NPI FSDB writer APIs broadly consists of the following phases:
1. Creating FSDB File: Obtain an FSDB writer object from API npi_fsdbw_create.
2. Creating Hierarchy: Describe the scope and signal hierarchy of the FSDB. This phase
is between the following APIs: npiFsdbwFileObj::begin_hierachy_creation and
npiFsdbwFileObj::end_hierachy_creation.
3. Adding value to signals: After calling npiFsdbwFileObj::end_hierachy_creation,
you can add value to the signals. They can also increase the time using the
npiFsdbwFileObj::incr_time API.
4. Closing the FSDB file: close the FSDB writer object and free up related memory with
the npi_fsdbw_close API.

This document describes APIs for basic behaviors to read/set information from/to CRDB.
Refer to the object diagram and APIs for the possible operations to CRDB. Note that
the objects from this API set are based on how CRDB models, so, there might be some

abstract and simplified than HDL language model.

npiCrdbHandle
npiCrdbHandle is a type for handles returned by APIs. Users should use variables of
this type to hold the handle returned by APIs.
All operations work on handles. A handle can be an object handle or an iterator
handle. Based on their lifetime, an object handle can be a valid handle or a volatile
An iterator handle can be created by npi_crdb_iter_start or npi_crdb_vol_iter_start.
Users must call npi_crdb_iter_stop or npi_crdb_vol_iter_stop to release the handle.
A valid handle is created by all APIs except npi_crdb_vol_iter_next. Users must call
npi_crdb_release_handle to release the handle.
A volatile handle is only created by npi_crdb_vol_iter_next. After a volatile
handle is created, it is automatically released by the iterator handle which
returned it when the iterator handle returns a new volatile handle or is released by
npi_crdb_vol_iter_stop. Users can use volatile handle to do Traversal or Property
operations before it is automatically released.

Users must clone a volatile handle to a valid handle by npi_crdb_clone_handle to
keep it and do other traverse operations.

Example of Volatile Handle
module top ;
reg [7:0] ary [1:0];
npiCrdbHandle c1_vol_hdl = NPI_CRDB_INVALID_HANDLE;
npiCrdbHandle c2_vol_hdl = NPI_CRDB_INVALID_HANDLE;
NPI_INT32 code = 0;
unsigned int size = 0;
// get child iterator from valid ary handle
npiCrdbHandle aryChildIter = npi_crdb_vol_iter_start (npiCrdbVolChild,
ary_hdl);
// iterate next to get ary[1] and ary[0] volatile handles
while (NULL != (c1_vol_hdl = npi_crdb_vol_iter_next(aryChildIter)))
{
// get property of the volatile handle c1_vol_hdl
code = npi_crdb_get ( npiCrdbSize, c1_vol_hdl, &size/*O*/ ) ;
if((0 == code) || (size<=1))
// get child iterator from the volatile handle c1_vol_hdl
npiCrdbHandle c1ChildIter = npi_crdb_vol_iter_start
(npiCrdbVolChild, c1_vol_hdl);
// iterate next to get ary[?][7]ary[?][0] volatile handles
for( int i = 0 ; i < size ; ++i ) {
c2_vol_hdl = npi_crdb_vol_iter_next(c1ChildIter);
// do operations with c2_vol_hdl
} //endfor
// stop ary[1]/ary[0] child iterator => c2_vol_hdl is released
code = npi_crdb_vol_iter_stop(c1ChildIter);
} //endwhile
// stop ary child iterator => c1_vol_hdl is released
code = npi_crdb_vol_iter_stop(aryChildIter);

Handles in NPI Power Model
The power handle is an opaque reference to an object in the power model. The power
model provides functions that operate on objects referred to by handles. The particular
operations that are legal for an object referred to by a handle depend on the type of the
NPI power model contains two types of handles. Data type npiPwHandle represents a
handle referring to a power object. Data type npiPwIter represents a handle referring to an
iterator object.
All of the possible relationships and properties that an object might have are documented
in the form of object diagrams.

Object Type Property
All objects have a npiPwType property, which is not shown in the data model diagrams.
npiPwObjType_elists all object types.
All NPI Power Model Enum properties can be obtained by both npi_pw_property and
npi_pw_property_str.
Use npi_pw_property( npiPwType, <object_handle> ) to get an integer enum value that
represents the type of the object.
Use npi_pw_property_str( npiPwType, <object_handle> ) to get a pointer to a string
containing the enum name.

Keys to Object Diagrams
The keys to the symbols used in the data model diagrams are listed below.

3. Class definition: Bold italic letters in a dotted enclosure indicate a class definition,
where the class groups other objects and classes. Properties of the class are defined in
this location. The class definition can contain an object definition.

4. Class reference: Italic letters in a dotted enclosure indicate a class reference.

5. Unnamed class: A dotted enclosure with no name is an unnamed class. It is sometimes
convenient to group objects although they are not referenced as a group elsewhere;
therefore, a name is not indicated.

6. A single arrow indicates a one-to-one relationship accessed with the routine
npi_pw_handle().
For example: Given npiPwHandle variable ref_h of type ref, access obj_h of type Obj:
obj_h = npi_pw_handle(Obj, ref_h);

7. A tagged one-to-one relationship is traversed similarly, using Tag instead of Obj.
obj_h = npi_pw_handle(Tag, ref_h);

8. A double arrow indicates a one-to-many relationship accessed with the routine
npi_pw_iter_next().
For example: Given npiPwHandle variable ref_h of type ref, iterate objects of type Obj:
itr = npi_pw_iter_start(Obj, ref_h);
while (obj_h = npi_pw_iter_next(itr) )

9. A tagged one-to-many relationship is traversed similarly, using Tag instead of Obj.
itr = npi_pw_iter_start(Tag, ref_h);
while (obj_h = npi_pw_iter_next(itr) )

10. A one-to-many relationship that originates from a circle is traversed using NULL for the
itr = npi_pw_iter_start(Obj, NULL);

while (obj_h = npi_pw_iter_next(itr) )

For object relationships (unless a special tag is shown in the diagram), the type used
for access is listed in column Object Type/Tag of Object Diagram Table.
For example, if an application has a handle to a supply port and wants to go to the
power domain where the supply port is defined, the call would be as follows:
domainH = npi_pw_handle( npiPwPowerDomain, portH );

The property that depends on a particular test is called a test-related property.
For example, a 0 -> 1 toggle bin might be covered in the first simulation run, but not in
another.

int main( int argc, char **argv )
{
// open database
if ( db == NULL )
{
printf( "Failed to load simv.vdb\n" );

}

// Iterate test and merge test
npiCovHandle test_iter = npi_cov_iter_start( npiCovTest, db );
npiCovHandle test;
npiCovHandle merged_test = NULL;
while ( test = npi_cov_iter_next( test_iter ) )
{
printf( "Test: %s\n", npi_cov_get_str( npiCovName, test ) );
if ( merged_test == NULL )
merged_test = test;
{
merged_test = npi_cov_merge_test( merged_test, test );
if ( merged_test == NULL )
{
printf( "Failed to merger test %s\n",
npi_cov_get_str( npiCovName, test ) );
}
}
}
npi_cov_iter_stop( test_iter );
// Dump instance line score from top
dump_instance_line_coverage( db, merged_test );
}

void dump_instance_line_coverage( npiCovHandle scope, npiCovHandle test )
{
npiCovHandle inst_iter = npi_cov_iter_start( npiCovInstance, scope );
npiCovHandle inst = NULL;
float score;
while ( inst = npi_cov_iter_next( inst_iter ) )
{
printf( "%s:\n", npi_cov_get_str( npiCovFullName, inst ) );
score = line_score( inst, test );
if ( score == -1 )
printf( "no score\n" );
printf( "%f\n", score );

}

dump_instance_line_coverage( inst, test );
}
npi_cov_iter_stop( inst_iter );

float line_score( npiCovHandle inst, npiCovHandle test )
{
int total_line = 0;
int total_coverd = 0;
float score;
npiCovHandle line_metric = npi_cov_handle( npiCovLineMetric, inst );
npiCovHandle iter = npi_cov_iter_start( npiCovChild, line_metric );
npiCovHandle block;
while ( block = npi_cov_iter_next( iter ) )
{
total_line = total_line + npi_cov_get( npiCovCoverable, block, NULL );
total_coverd = total_coverd + npi_cov_get( npiCovCovered, block,
test );
}
// No info
if ( total_line == 0 )
return -1;

}

score = ((float) total_coverd / (float)total_line) * 100;
return score;

Class npi_ltr_sig_t
Each npi_ltr_sig_t object represents the signal nodes in trace result.
The signal nodes can be located in either the initial signal specified for trace driver or the
contributors of driver statement. The signal nodes can be a Power object or HDL signal.
1. Use double npi_ltr_sig_t::time() to get the corresponding time values.

2. Use NPI_BYTE8* npi_ltr_sig_t::value() to get the string of value including

npi_end
Perform the ending activities for the NPI process.

The routine npi_end() defined in npi.h is used to perform the ending (reset) activities for
the NPI process. Note that all NPI C-API routines must be enclosed by npi_init() and
npi_end().

int npi_end();

Return 1 (true) if the ending activities complete successfully; otherwise, return 0 (false).
Use npi_init() to perform the initialization activities for the NPI process.

npi_init
Perform the initialization activities for the NPI process.
The routine npi_init() defined in npi.h is used to perform the initialization activities for
the NPI process. It is essential that the npi_init() be called before any C-API routines
provided in this manual, otherwise, all the functions that operate on objects referred to by
npiNlHandle does not work. In addition to initialization, some ending activities for the NPI
process have to be executed after the work is done, refer to the routine npi_end().

npi_compare_objects
Compare two handles to determine whether they refer to the same object.
The NPI routine npi_compare_objects() returns 1 (TRUE) if the two handles refer to the
same object. Otherwise, 0 (FALSE) is returned. The only thing NPI can compare for
variable is whether the variable is a constant. For example,

npi_compare_objects (arr[0], arr[i]); // return 0; NPI cannot get i's
(defined in simulation time)

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------char* get_and_print_value(const npiHandle hdl)
{
static npiValue value;

static NPI_BYTE8 value_str[MAX_STRING_LENGTH];
npiHandle typeHdl = npi_handle(npiVhBaseType, hdl);
if(!typeHdl)
int type = npi_get(npiType, typeHdl);
switch(type) {
case npiVhIntTypeDecl:
case npiVhEnumTypeDecl:
value.format = npiIntVal;
snprintf(value_str, MAX_STRING_LENGTH-1, "%d", value.value.integer);
case npiVhFloatTypeDecl:
value.format = npiRealVal;
snprintf(value_str, MAX_STRING_LENGTH-1, "%f", value.value.real);
case npiVhPhysTypeDecl:
value.format = npiPhysVal;
snprintf(value_str, MAX_STRING_LENGTH-1, "%lld", value.value.phys);
case npiVhArrayTypeDecl:
{
npiHandle elemTypeHdl = npi_handle(npiVhElemType, typeHdl);
if(npi_get(npiType, elemTypeHdl)==npiVhSubTypeDecl)
elemTypeHdl = npi_handle(npiVhBaseType, elemTypeHdl);
const char* typeName = npi_get_str(npiName, elemTypeHdl);
if(strcmp(typeName, "std_ulogic")==0 || strcmp(typeName, "BIT")==0) {
value.format = npiBinStrVal;
snprintf(value_str, MAX_STRING_LENGTH-1, "B\"%s\"",
value.value.str);
}
else if(strcmp(typeName, "CHARACTER")==0) {
value.format = npiStringVal;
snprintf(value_str, MAX_STRING_LENGTH-1, "\"%s\"",
value.value.str);
}
}
}
return value_str;
}

proc get_and_print_value { hdl const_type } {
set size [ npi_get -property npiSize -object $hdl ]
if { [ npi_get -property npiSigned -object $hdl ] == 1 } {
set sign_str "s"
} else { set sign_str "" }
switch -- $const_type {
npiDecConst {
set value [ npi_get_value -format npiDecStrVal -object $hdl ]

}
npiRealConst {
set value [ npi_get_value -format npiRealVal -object $hdl ]
set value_str [format "%s" $value]
}
npiBinaryConst {
set value [ npi_get_value -format npiBinStrVal -object $hdl ]
set value_str [format "%d'%sb%s" $size $sign_str $value]
}

npiOctConst {
set value [ npi_get_value -format npiOctStrVal -object $hdl ]
set value_str [format "%d'%so%s" $size $sign_str $value]
}
npiHexConst {
set value [ npi_get_value -format npiHexStrVal -object $hdl ]
set value_str [format "%d'%sh%s" $size $sign_str $value]
}
npiStringConst {
set value [ npi_get_value -format npiStringVal -object $hdl ]
set value_str [format "\"%s\"" $value]
}
npiIntConst default {
set value [ npi_get_value -format npiIntVal -object $hdl ]
set value_str [format "%s" $value]
}

}
return $value_str
}

no longer needed. This avoids logical memory leaks.

object is automatically freed when npi_scan returns NULL because it has either completed
an object traversal or encountered an error condition. If neither of these conditions occurs
(which can happen if the code breaks out of an iteration loop before it has scanned every
object), npi_release_handle should be called to free any memory allocated for the iterator.

npi_scan
Scan the SystemVerilog hierarchy for objects with a one-to-many relationship.

The NPI routine npi_scan traverses the instantiated SystemVerilog hierarchy and return
handles to objects as directed by the iterator. The iterator handle is obtained by calling
npi_iterate for a specific object type. When npi_scan returns NULL (C/C++) or empty (Tcl),
the iterator handle is no longer valid and cannot be used again.

iterator

Get a handle to an object using its index number within a given object.
The NPI Netlist API npi_nl_handle_by_index returns a handle to an object based on the
index number of the object within the reference object, obj. The reference objects can be
ports, instance ports, or net objects. If the selection represented by the index number does
not lead to the construction of a legal index select expression (that is, the given index is
out of range of the reference object), the routine returns a NULL handle.

NPI_INT32 type = npi_nl_get(npiNlType, hdl);
if ( type == npiNlInst )
NPI_INT32 left = npi_nl_get(npiNlLeft, hdl);
NPI_INT32 right = npi_nl_get(npiNlRight, hdl);

NPI_INT32 max = ((left < right) ? right : left);

}

npi_nl_release_handle
Release the handle and its associated resources allocated by NPI Netlist routines.
The NPI Netlist API npi_nl_release_handle frees memory allocated for NPI Netlist
handles.
The tool might allocate memory when a handle is obtained, although often all required
memory was allocated when the object was first created or elaborated.
You can safely ignore calling npi_nl_release_handle when a handle is no longer needed.

It is always advisable to call it when the handle is valid and will not become invalid
automatically.
This avoids logical memory leaks.
npi_nl_release_handle cannot be called with an invalid handle.
npi_nl_release_handle can free memory created for iterator objects.
The iterator object is automatically freed when npi_nl_scan returns NULL.
This happens when traversal completes or an error condition occurs.
If neither condition occurs, call npi_nl_release_handle to free memory allocated for the
iterator.
This can happen when code breaks out of an iteration loop before scanning every object.
The routine returns 1 (true) on success and 0 (false) on failure.

General Use Flow in NPI FSDB Writer Model
The general flow of using NPI FSDB writer APIs broadly consists of the following phases:
1. Creating FSDB File: Obtain an FSDB writer object from API npi_fsdbw_create.
2. Creating Hierarchy: Describe the scope and signal hierarchy of the FSDB. This phase
is between the following APIs: npiFsdbwFileObj::begin_hierachy_creation and
npiFsdbwFileObj::end_hierachy_creation.
3. Adding value to signals: After calling npiFsdbwFileObj::end_hierachy_creation,
you can add value to the signals. They can also increase the time using the
npiFsdbwFileObj::incr_time API.
4. Closing the FSDB file: close the FSDB writer object and free up related memory with
the npi_fsdbw_close API.

npiCrdbHandle
npiCrdbHandle is a type for handles returned by APIs. Users should use variables of
this type to hold the handle returned by APIs.
All operations work on handles. A handle can be an object handle or an iterator
handle. Based on their lifetime, an object handle can be a valid handle or a volatile
An iterator handle can be created by npi_crdb_iter_start or npi_crdb_vol_iter_start.
Users must call npi_crdb_iter_stop or npi_crdb_vol_iter_stop to release the handle.
A valid handle is created by all APIs except npi_crdb_vol_iter_next. Users must call
npi_crdb_release_handle to release the handle.
A volatile handle is only created by npi_crdb_vol_iter_next. After a volatile
handle is created, it is automatically released by the iterator handle which
returned it when the iterator handle returns a new volatile handle or is released by
npi_crdb_vol_iter_stop. Users can use volatile handle to do Traversal or Property
operations before it is automatically released.

Users must clone a volatile handle to a valid handle by npi_crdb_clone_handle to
keep it and do other traverse operations.

Handles in NPI Power Model
The power handle is an opaque reference to an object in the power model. The power
model provides functions that operate on objects referred to by handles. The particular
operations that are legal for an object referred to by a handle depend on the type of the
NPI power model contains two types of handles. Data type npiPwHandle represents a
handle referring to a power object. Data type npiPwIter represents a handle referring to an
iterator object.
All of the possible relationships and properties that an object might have are documented
in the form of object diagrams.

Object Type Property
All objects have a npiPwType property, which is not shown in the data model diagrams.
npiPwObjType_elists all object types.
All NPI Power Model Enum properties can be obtained by both npi_pw_property and
npi_pw_property_str.
Use npi_pw_property( npiPwType, <object_handle> ) to get an integer enum value that
represents the type of the object.
Use npi_pw_property_str( npiPwType, <object_handle> ) to get a pointer to a string
containing the enum name.

The program performs the following actions:
1. Shows the design top "top" specified for the power model.
2. Gets the power domain "tb/PD_SRC".
3. Gets the instance "tb/SrcA".
4. Iterates all the supply nets from the power domain.
5. Gets isolation supply set handle of the power domain, and then gets the associated
supply set from the isolation supply set handle.

proc npi_pw_dump_obj { hdl } {
set name [ npi_pw_property_str -type npiPwFullName -ref $hdl ]
set type [ npi_pw_property_str -type npiPwType -ref $hdl ]
set lineNo [ npi_pw_property -type npiPwLineNo -ref $hdl ]
puts "$name\($type\) at line $lineNo"
}
proc npi_pw_demo {} {
design top
puts "Design top: [ npi_pw_design_top ]"
get power domain by name
set pdSrc [ npi_pw_power_domain_by_name -name "tb/PD_SRC" ]
npi_pw_dump_obj $pdSrc
get instance by name
set inst [ npi_pw_handle_by_name -name "tb/SrcA" -type
"npiPwInstance" ]
npi_pw_dump_obj $inst
iterate supply nets
set iter [ npi_pw_iter_start -type "npiPwSupplyNet" -ref $pdSrc ]
while { [ set net [ npi_pw_iter_next -iter $iter ] ] != "" } {
npi_pw_dump_obj $net
}
npi_pw_iter_stop -iter $iter
get supply set handle
set isoHandle [ npi_pw_handle -ref $pdSrc -type "npiPwIsoSetHandle" ]
set supplySet [ npi_pw_handle -ref $isoHandle -type
"npiPwAssocSupplySet" ]
npi_pw_dump_obj $supplySet
}

The property that depends on a particular test is called a test-related property.
For example, a 0 -> 1 toggle bin might be covered in the first simulation run, but not in
another.

* npiCovStatus if the npiCovStatusCovered flag is to be checked

proc trace_driver_by_name {sigName}{
set stmtList{}

trace_stmts_driver $stmtList
}

set stmtList{}
npi_ltr_trace_driver -hdl $sigHdl -retList stmtList
trace_stmts_driver $stmtList

proc trace_stmts_driver {stmtList}{
foreach {stmt} $stmtList {
only check active driver
if{[$stmt drive_type] ne "npiLtrDriveActive"}{
}
show active statement
puts "Active statement:[$stmt statement]"
check contributors
if{[$stmt has_contributor] ==1}{
set contriList{}
$stmt contributor -retList contriList
can do further trace sriver with contributors
foreach {contri} $contriList {
trace_driver_by_hdl $contri
}
}
}

npi_end
Perform the ending activities for the NPI process.

The routine npi_end() defined in npi.h is used to perform the ending (reset) activities for
the NPI process. Note that all NPI C-API routines must be enclosed by npi_init() and
npi_end().

int npi_end();

Return 1 (true) if the ending activities complete successfully; otherwise, return 0 (false).
Use npi_init() to perform the initialization activities for the NPI process.

npi_init
Perform the initialization activities for the NPI process.
The routine npi_init() defined in npi.h is used to perform the initialization activities for
the NPI process. It is essential that the npi_init() be called before any C-API routines
provided in this manual, otherwise, all the functions that operate on objects referred to by
npiNlHandle does not work. In addition to initialization, some ending activities for the NPI
process have to be executed after the work is done, refer to the routine npi_end().

npi_get_value
Retrieve the value of the parameter object and literal.
The NPI routine npi_get_value() retrieves the value of NPI objects. Currently, NPI only
supports getting the value for parameter and literal/constant objects.

NPI_INT32 npi_get_value ( npiHandle expr , npiValue & value, bool
isGetDefaultVal=false );

Handle to an expression object.

The reference to a structure containing value information. Conceptually, the value is the
output of the routine.
typedef struct t_npi_vecval
{
/* following fields are repeated enough times to contain vector */
NPI_INT32 aval, bval; /* bit encoding: ab: 00=0, 10=1, 11=X, 01=Z */
} s_npi_vecval, *p_npi_vecval;
struct npiValue
{
NPI_INT32 format; /* npiBinStrVal, npiOctStrVal, npiDecStrVal,
npiHexStrVal,
npiScalarVal, npiIntVal, npiRealVal, npiVectorVal, npiPhysVal */
union
{
char *str; /* string value */
NPI_INT32 scalar; /* npi0, npi1, npiX, npiZ */
NPI_INT32 integer; /* integer value */
double real; /* real value */
struct t_npi_vecval *vector; /* vector value */
NPI_INT64 phys; /* vhdl phys val */
};

The format of the value is set by the format field of the structure.
* For a string, npiBinStrVal or npiOctStrVal or npiDecStrVal or npiHexStrVal
* For an integer, npiIntVal
* For a real, npiRealVal

* For a scalar, npiScalar
* For a vector, npiVectorVal
* For a phys, npiPhysVal

Other details:
1. The string buffer used by npi_get_value() is overwritten with each call. If the value
needs to be kept, it should be saved by the application like npi_get_str(). However, the
string buffer used by this routine is different from the one used by npi_get_str().
2. The ASCII values of UDP table entries is obtained by using the value format

3. If a constant object's npiConstType is npiStringVal, the value is retrieved by using the
value format either npiStringVal or npiVectorVal.

4. For npiStringVal, if each 8-bit group of the value represents a non-printing ASCII
character, it is mapped to space character. Like the following example, applying
npi_get_value() to parameter handle "aa" obtains the string value " B?".
parameter aa = 32'h000f423f;

5. For Tcl, the return value format of npiRealVal is "%f".

within that scope only.

npi_iterate
Obtain an iterator handle to objects with a one-to-many relationship.
The NPI routine npi_iterate is used to traverse one-to-many relationships, which are
indicated as double arrows in the Object Diagrams. Refer to the Object Diagram section
in the NPI Language - SystemVerilog Model chapter for details. The npi_iterate routine
returns a handle to an iterator, whose type (npiType) is "npiIterator", which can used by
npi_scan to traverse all objects of the specific type associated with the reference object.

npiHandle npi_iterate ( NPI_INT32 type , npiHandle refHandle );

An integer constant defined in npi_hdl.h representing the type of object for which to obtain
iterator handles.
refHandle

Return the handle to an iterator for an object. If there are no objects of type associated
with the reference handle refHandle, then the npi_iterate routine returns NULL.

end
end

{
printf("Module: %s\n", npi_get_str(npiFullName, mod_hdl));
//get the scope of the module handle "TEST.dut", by using one-to-one
method npi_handle()
npiHandle scope = npi_handle(npiScope, mod_hdl);
printf(" The module is in scope: %s\n", npi_get_str(npiFullName,
scope));
//iterate the port of "TEST.dut"

npiHandle port_hdl;
int port_size;
char* port_name;
char* port_dir;
npiHandle port_it = npi_iterate(npiPort, mod_hdl);
while( (port_hdl = npi_scan(port_it)) != NULL ) {
//get the int/bool property and string property of port_hdl
port_size = npi_get(npiSize, port_hdl);
port_name = (char*) npi_get_str(npiName, port_hdl);
port_dir = (char*) npi_get_str(npiDirection, port_hdl);
printf(" %d) Port = %s (%s Size=%d)\n", i++, port_name,
port_dir, port_size);
//release port_hdl since it is useless below
npi_release_handle(port_hdl);
}
}

The NPI routine npi_release_handle frees memory allocated for NPI handles. NPI might
allocate memory when a handle to an object is obtained. One might safely ignore calling
npi_release_handle when a handle is no longer needed, but it is always recommended to
do so, provided the handle is valid and does not automatically become invalid in the future.
A guideline for better memory usage is to release the created handles whenever they are
no longer needed. This avoids logical memory leaks.
npi_release_handle might not be called on an invalid handle.
npi_release_handle might be used to free memory created for iterator objects. The iterator
object is automatically freed when npi_scan returns NULL because it has either completed
an object traversal or encountered an error condition. If neither of these conditions occurs
(which can happen if the code breaks out of an iteration loop before it has scanned every
object), npi_release_handle should be called to free any memory allocated for the iterator.

NPI_INT32 npi_release_handle ( npiHandle object );

Returns 1 (true) if the NPI memory management system releases the memory used by the
object. Returns 0 (false) if NPI does not free the memory of the object because there might
be another application program using it.

Get a handle to an object using its index number within a given object.
The NPI Netlist API npi_nl_handle_by_index returns a handle to an object based on the
index number of the object within the reference object, obj. The reference objects can be
ports, instance ports, or net objects. If the selection represented by the index number does
not lead to the construction of a legal index select expression (that is, the given index is
out of range of the reference object), the routine returns a NULL handle.

if { $type == "npiNlInst" } { return }

set
set
set
set

right [ npi_nl_get -property npiNlRight -object $hdl ]
index [ expr { $left < $right } ? $left : $right ]
max [ expr { $left < $right } ? $right : $left ]

for { } { $index <= $max } { incr index } {
set hdlByIndex [ npi_nl_handle_by_index -index $index -object $hdl ]
set fullName [ npi_nl_get_str -property npiNlFullName -object
$hdlByIndex

]

puts "Handle $fullName by index $index is obtained"
npi_nl_release_handle -object $hdlByIndex

}
}

npi_nl_handle_by_name
Get a handle to an object with the specified name.
The NPI Netlist API npi_nl_handle_by_name returns a handle to an object with the
specified name and type. This function can be applied to instance and net objects. The
given hierarchical name is searched for from the top level of hierarchy.

npiNlHandle npi_nl_handle_by_name ( const NPI_BYTE8* name, NPI_INT32 type
= npiNlUndefined );

A character string or pointer to a string containing the full hierarchical name of an object.

An integer constant representing the type of object for which to obtain the handle (default
value: npiNlUndefined).
wire [3:0] a = 4'b1110; // 3-bit net with identifier "a"
wire \b[3:0] = 1'b1; // 1-bit net with escape identifier "\b[3:0] "

demo.list
top.\b[3:0]
top.a[3:0]
top.a[0:100]
top.1'b1

Reads object names to be found from demo.list, and then finds the handle by name.

{

npiNlHandle hdl = NULL;
FILE* fp = NULL;
NPI_BYTE8 hdlNameStr[1024];
NPI_INT32 intVal = npiNlUndefined;
int strLen = 0;
if ((fp = fopen("demo.list", "r")) == NULL)
{
printf("Can not open the file!\n");
}
while (fgets (hdlNameStr, sizeof(hdlNameStr), fp))
{
// remove the last '\n' character
strLen = strlen(hdlNameStr);
if (hdlNameStr[strLen-1] == '\n')
hdlNameStr[strLen-1] = '\0';
// find the handle by name
if ((hdl = npi_nl_handle_by_name(hdlNameStr)) == NULL)
// dump the handle according to its type
switch (npi_nl_get(npiNlType, hdl))
{
case npiNlInst:
printf("Instance object %s is found, ",
npi_nl_get_str(npiNlFullName,
hdl));
printf("instance type is \"%s\".\n", npi_nl_get_str(npiNlInstType,
hdl));
// other actions
case npiNlDeclNet:
printf("Net object \"%s\" is found, ",
npi_nl_get_str(npiNlFullName,
hdl));
printf("size is %d.\n", npi_nl_get(npiNlSize, hdl));
// other actions
}
npi_nl_release_handle(hdl);
}
fclose(fp);

}

Get a handle to an object using the specified range within a given object.
The NPI routine npi_nl_handle_by_range returns a handle to an object based on the
specified range of the object within the reference object, obj. The reference objects can
be ports, instance ports, or net objects. If the selection represented by the left and right
numbers does not lead to the construction of a legal range expression (that is, the given
range is out of range of the reference object), the routine returns a NULL handle.

npi_nl_iterate
Obtain an iterator handle to objects with a one-to-many relationship.

npiNlHandle npi_nl_iterate ( NPI_INT32 type, npiNlHandle ref );

The NPI Netlist API npi_nl_iterate traverses one-to-many relationships indicated as
double arrows in the object diagrams.
The npi_nl_iterate routine returns an npiNlIterator handle.
Use npi_nl_scan to traverse all objects of the specified type associated with object ref.
If no objects of that type are associated with ref, npi_nl_iterate returns NULL.
If the input type is npiNlInst and the input reference handle is NULL,
npi_nl_iterate returns handles to the top instance objects. For all the other
types with a NULL reference handle, npi_nl_iterate returns NULL.
The handles to objects returned by npi_nl_iterate is sorted in ascending
order by their full hierarchical name except for the following cases:
- If the input type is npiNlSliceNet or npiNlConnectivity, and the input reference
handle is a concatenated net.
- If the input type is npiNlSliceNet or npiNlConnectivity, and the input
referencehandle's parent is a concatenated net.

An integer constant representing the type of object for which to obtain iterator handles.
ref

Handle to an iterator for an object.

Use npi_nl_scan() to traverse the NPI Netlist model using the iterator handle returned from

npi_nl_iterate().

Use npi_nl_iterate_with_range() to obtain handles to objects with a one-to-many
relationship under the given range.
Use npi_nl_handle() to obtain handles to object with a one-to-one relationship.

proc traverse_net_hdl_with_range { netHdl } {

get the range of net

set right [ npi_nl_get -property npiNlRight -object $netHdl ]
set low [ expr {$left <= $right} ? $left : $right ]
set high [ expr {$left <= $right} ? $right : $left ]
for { set i $low } { $i <= $high } { incr i 1 } {
find the connectivity for each bit
if { [ set itr [ npi_nl_iterate_with_range -type npiNlConnectivity
-refHandle $netHdl -left $i -right $i] ] != ""} {

-object $netHdl ] with range \[$i:$i\]"
while { [ set subHdl [ npi_nl_scan -iterator $itr ] ] != "" } {
puts " [npi_nl_get_str -property npiNlFullName -object
$subHdl ]"
npi_nl_release_handle -object $subHdl
}
}
}

1. npiNlDriver, npiNlLoad, and npiNlConnectivity relations returns net, port,
and instance port objects that are drivers, loads, and the connected objects
of the given reference object. Otherwise, npi_nl iterate_with_range returns
NULL.
2. Left bound and right bound passed to npi_nl_iterate_with_range is
automatically normalized by the reference object. More specifically,
npi_nl_iterate_with_range automatically changes the range direction and
trace the overlapped part.
For example, in the following C/C++ code for npi_nl_iterate_with_range,
assume a net handle netHdl with range [3:0],
/* [0:3] is treated as [3:0] => overlap [3:0] and [3:0] =>
equivalent
to npi_nl_iterate_with_range(npiNlLoad, netHdl, 3, 0) */
hdl = npi_nl_iterate_with_range(npiNlLoad, netHdl, 0, 3)
/* [1:2] is treated as [2:1] => overlap [2:1] and [3:0] =>
equivalent
to npi_nl_iterate_with_range(npiNlLoad, netHdl, 2, 1) */
hdl = npi_nl_iterate_with_range(npiNlLoad, netHdl, 1, 2)
/* [2:5] is treated as [5:2] => overlap [5:2] and [3:0] =>
equivalent
to npi_nl_iterate_with_range(npiNlLoad, netHdl, 3, 2) */
hdl = npi_nl_iterate_with_range(npiNlLoad, netHdl, 2, 5)
/* overlap [7:3] and [3:0] => equivalent to
npi_nl_iterate_with_range(npiNlLoad, netHdl, 3, 3) */
hdl = npi_nl_iterate_with_range(npiNlLoad, netHdl, 7, 3)

manipulation for the cloned module.

typedef enum { ADD, SUB } ALU_OP;

wire OPERAND op;

output logic carry,

SUB: {carry,out} = op.a - op.b - 1 + op.cin;

npi_dm_create_argument_instance
Create a new argument instance object.
1. The argument instance is used in the tf_call and system tf_call.
2. An argument instance must have an actual object.
3. For a system tf_call, its argument instances have no formal objects.
4. For a tf_call, its argument instance must have formal objects.
This rule does not apply when the tf_call has no argument.
5. To represent no argument or an empty argument in a tf_call/system tf_call,
use an argument instance has no formal handle but has an actual handle of
npiDmOperation with npiDmOpNull optype.

npiDmHandle npi_dm_create_argument_instance( npiDmHandle formal,
npiDmHandle actual );

formal

This argument specifies the formal object of the created argument instance.
actual

This argument specifies the actual object of the created argument instance.
On success, the created argument instance handle is returned.
Refer to npi_dm_create_function_call.

dump task call info
proc dump_task_call { target_hdl } {
set fd [open result.log a]
set scope_hdl [npi_dm_handle -type "npiDmScope" -ref $target_hdl]
set scope_name [npi_dm_property_str -type "npiDmName" -ref $scope_hdl]
puts $fd "scope = $scope_name"
set task_call_type [npi_dm_property_str -type "npiDmType" -ref
$target_hdl]
puts $fd "type = $task_call_type"
set task_call_name [npi_dm_property_str -type "npiDmName" -ref
$target_hdl]
puts $fd "name = $task_call_name"
if { $task_call_type == "npiDmTaskCall" } {
set task [npi_dm_handle -type "npiDmTask" -ref $target_hdl]
set task_name [npi_dm_property_str -type "npiDmName" -ref $task]
puts $fd "full task name = $task_name"
}
set arg_iter [npi_dm_iter_start -type "npiDmArgInst" -ref $target_hdl]
set arg_counter 1
while { "" != [set arg [npi_dm_iter_next -iter $arg_iter]] } {
puts $fd " argument $arg_counter"
if { $task_call_type == "npiDmTaskCall" } {
set formal [npi_dm_handle -type "npiDmFormal" -ref $arg]
set formal_name ""

if { "" != $formal } {
set formal_name [npi_dm_property_str -type "npiDmName" -ref
$formal]
}
puts -nonewline $fd "
formal_arg = $formal_name"
}
set actual [npi_dm_handle -type "npiDmActual" -ref $arg]
set actual_name [npi_dm_property_str -type "npiDmName" -ref $actual]
puts $fd "
actual_arg = $actual_name"
set arg_counter [expr $arg_counter+1]
}
npi_dm_iter_stop -iter $arg_iter
}

close $fd

end of dumping task call info

}

npi_fsdbw_open
Opens an FSDB file with the provided file name in the current working directory.
The opened FSDB file has to be closed by calling npi_fsdbw_close() if it does
not need to be modified anymore; otherwise there might be some issues while
reading this FSDB file.

npiFsdbwFileHandle npi_fsdbw_open
( const char* name,
const char* unit,
npiFsdbTime time);

Name of the FSDB file.
If it is NULL, an error is issued and this API fails.
Each FSDB file must have a unique name. If it is equal to the name of any existing FSDB
file, this API fails and returns a NULL pointer.
unit (C-based)

The scale unit of the FSDB file.
For example, if the scale unit needs to be set as 10 ns, user can provide a string "10 ns"
as a unit for this API. The legal scale unit should be as [1, 10, 100] [s, ms, us, ns, ps, fs]
(these are case sensitive and only lower cases are allowed). An error is issued and it is set
as 1 ns if any other value is provided.
time (C-based)

The begin time of simulation for the FSDB file.
If the provided time is a negative value, a warning is issued and it is set as 0.

On success, returns a file handle; otherwise, returns an empty string.
Use npi_fsdbw_close to close an FSDB file and use npi_fsdbw_flush to flush data into an
FSDB file without closing it.

Adds an attribute to a scope with a given scope full name.

char* scopeName, const char* attrName, T attr, npiFsdbwRadix radix =
npiFsdbwDec);

The specified file handle. If this handle is invalid, an error is issued. (For the illegal case,

Specifies the full hierarchy name of the scope. Must use `.' as delimiter. If it is NULL, an
error is issued and this API fails.

Specifies the value of the attribute being added.
The allowed data types are listed in Data Types of Attributes. The conversion rule is:
For the C-API:
* If the value is an integer type, an integer attribute is created.
* If the value is a float, double, or string type, an attribute with the same type is created.

radix, refer typedef enum npiFsdbwRadix.

use npi_fsdbw_stream_add_attr to add an attribute to a stream, and use

text:
trans_hdl

The handle of transaction which is specified to add this attribute. If this handle is invalid,
an error is issued. (For details on the illegal case, see Illegal Cases of Different Handles)
attr_name

The name of the attribute.

The attribute type.
To specify the data type in this command, the argument can be
* "INT8", which is char type in C language.
* "INT16", which is short integer in C language.
* "INT32", which is integer type in C language.
* "INT64", which is long long integer in C language.
* "FLOAT", which is float type in C language.
* "DOUBLE", which is double type in C language.
* "STRING", which is string type in C language.
All the arguments mentioned above must be in capital case.
For any other arguments, an error is issued and this attribute is added.

Value of the attribute being added. The data type is set by the argument -type.
expect_attr

The expected attribute value. The data type of expect attribute is same as the data type of
attribute, which is set through the argument -type.

Specifies the radix of the integer data type being used. The usable radix values are as
follows:
* npiFsdbwBin (binary)
* npiFsdbwOct (octal)
* npiFsdbwDec (decimal)
* npiFsdbwUnsigned (unsigned)
If this parameter is provided and the data type of attr is determined as non-integer type
(such as float, double, string), an error is issued.

arrows in the object diagrams.

Sets mapping between input RTL and gate level object.
The input object of RTL and gate level should be both scopes or both signals.
Besides, they should be in the same CRDB.
The parameter inverse is ignored when input objects of RTL and gate level are
scopes.
If the input RTL or gate level object already has correlated objects, this API
adds mapping instead of replacing the existing mapping. To replace the existing
mapping, you should use npi_crdb_unset_correlation to break existing mapping
first.

In the NPI Language model, location objects provide detailed location information,
including file name, begin line number, and end line number. Location is a general object
type for both SystemVerilog and VHDL.

top.v
module top (clk, rst_n, addr, din, dout);
include "ip.v"

ip.v
parameter WIDTH = 64;
input rst_n;
input [WIDTH-1 : 0] addr;
input [WIDTH-1 : 0] din;
output [WIDTH-1 : 0] dout;
ip ip_inst (.clk ( clk),
.rst_n ( rst_n),
.addr ( addr),
.din ( din),
.dout ( dout)
);

In example above, the module definition "top" distributes into two files "top.v" and "ip.v".
Applying method "npiDefLocation" on the instance handle "top", two location handles
are returned, and the detail location information including file name, begin line number,
and end line number can be retrieved by querying properties of the location handles.

1. npiFile returns the file name of the location handle.
2. npiBeginLine and npiEndLine returns the line number where the object begins and
ends in the file, respectively.

Lang Interface

* Appendix A: Supported List

In the NPI Language Model, the language interface is a boundary of different languages
for mixed language design. The language interface can describe its connection
relationship for port and parameter or generic.
The language interface can also be treated as a terminal or an entry point of other
languages. The actual object of the language interface is obtained by applying method
npiActual.

svTop.v
logic [31:0] a;
logic [31:0] b;
logic [31:0] c;
add32 (.width(cv)) a0(a, b, c);
add16 (.width(cv/2)) a1(a[31:16], b[31:16], null);

add.vhd
use STD.textio.all;

begin -- circuits of add32
end architecture circuits; -- of add32
entity add16 is
port(ea : in std_logic_vector(15 downto 0);
eb : in std_logic_vector(15 downto 0);
esum : out std_logic_vector(15 downto 0));
end entity add16;
architecture circuits of add16 is
begin -- circuits of add16
end architecture circuits; -- of add16

In svTop.v, SystemVerilog module "top" obtains two language interfaces "a0" and "a1" by
applying method npiInternalScope.
For language interfaces "a0" and "a1", they get three ports (ea, eb and esum) by applying
one-to-many method npiPort and one param assign by applying one-to-many method
npiParamMap.
Finally, their actual VHDL component objects "top.a0" and "top.a1" is obtained by applying
one-to-one method npiActual respectively.
Similarly, port "ea" under "top.a0" also gets a language interface "a0" by applying method
npiScope because "a0" is a language boundary like the description in the paragraph
above.

Alias Statement
An alias statement declares multiple names for the same physical net, or bits within a net.

module top (inout wire [15:0] bus16,
inout wire [7:0] data_mst,
inout wire [7:0] data_slv
);
alias bus16 = {data_mst, data_slv}; /* alias statement */
wire [3:0] addr, addr_s1, addr_s2;
alias addr = addr_s1 = addr_s2; /* alias statement */

In example.v, the module "top" contains two alias statement "alias bus16 =
{data_mst, data_slv};" and "alias addr = addr_s1 = addr_s2;".
The alias statements can be retrieved by the 1-m relationship "npiAliasStmt".
For an alias statement, the 1-m relationship "npiNetAlias" can retrieve all expressions
declared by net alias.
For example, a net handle "bus16" and an operation handle "{data_mst, data_slv}"
would be returned by applying "npiNetAlias" on the first alias statement.
The three net handles "addr", "addr_s1", and "addr_s2", are returned on the second alias

The 1-m relationship "npiNetAlias" iterates the alias statement and returns all expressions
that are declared by net alias.

Assertion
In the NPI language model, assertion is a class that contains several objects. The object is
one of the following kinds:
* assert: A concurrent assert statement that is used to enforce a property. The
corresponding object type is "npiAssert".
* assume: A concurrent assume statement that is to allowed properties to be considered
as assumptions for formal analysis as well as for dynamic simulation tools. The
corresponding object type is "npiAssume".
* cover: A concurrent cover statement with object type "npiCover". There exist two
categories of cover statement, cover sequence and cover property.
The cover sequence statement specifies sequence coverage, while the cover
property statement specifies property coverage.
NPI provides a property named "npiIsCoverSequence" to distinguish if a cover object
is a cover sequence or not.
* restrict, a concurrent restrict statement with object type "npiRestrict".
* immediate assert, that is an immediate assert statement with object type
"npiImmediateAssert".
* immediate assume, that is an immediate assume statement with object type
"npiImmediateAssume".
* immediate cover, that is an immediate cover statement with object type
"npiImmediateCover".

* sequence inst, that is an instance of a named sequence with object type
"npiSequenceInst".
* property inst, that is an instance of a named property with object type
"npiPropertyInst".
There are two kinds of assertion statement: immediate and concurrent.
* Immediate assertions follow simulation event semantics for their execution and are
executed like a statement in a procedural block. Immediate assertions are primarily
intended to be used with simulation.
There are three kinds belonged to immediate assertion as follows:
Immediate assert (npiImmediateAssert)
Immediate assume (npiImmediateAssume)
Immediate cover (npiImmediateCover).
Immediate assertions can be divided into simple immediate assertions and deferred
immediate assertions.
NPI provides a property named "npiIsDeferred" to distinguish if the immediate
assertion is a deferred immediate assertion or a simple immediate assertion.
* Concurrent assertions are based on a clock semantics and use sample values
of variables. The keyword property distinguishes a concurrent assertion from an
immediate assertion.
There are four kinds belonged to concurrent assertion as follows:
Assert (npiAssert)
Assume (npiAssume)
Cover (npiCover)
Restrict (npiRestrict)

example.sv
timescale 1ns/1ps
//==========================================================
// Testbench
//==========================================================
reg rst_n;
reg inc;
reg dec;
wire [3:0] data;
time t;
// Assert ---------------------------------------/* immediate assert */
always@(*)
ASSERT1: assert (data >= 0) else $error("Error: data < 0");
/* immediate assert, is deferred */
ASSERT2: assert 0 (data <= 9) else $error("Error: data > 9");
/* concurrent assert */
ASSERT3: assert property ( @(posedge clk) !(data[3]&&data[1]) );
// Assume ---------------------------------------/* immediate assume */
ASSUME1: assume (!(inc && dec)) $info("Info: keep assumption");
$warning("Warning: inc == 1 &&
dec == 1");
/* concurrent assume */
ASSUME2: assume property ( @(posedge clk) !(inc && dec) );
// Cover ----------------------------------------always @(posedge clk) begin
/* immediate cover */
COVER1: cover (!inc && dec);
/* immediate cover, is deferred */
COVER2: cover 0 (inc && !dec);
end
/* concurrent cover */
COVER3: cover property ( @(posedge clk) (!(inc || dec)) );
// Restrict -------------------------------------Verdi(R) VC Apps Native Programming Interface (NPI)

/* concurrent restrict */
RESTRICT1: restrict property ( @(posedge clk) (data > 9) );
// Design instantiation --------------------------cnt_0to9 cnt ( .clk ( clk),
.rst_n ( rst_n),
.inc ( inc),
.dec ( dec),
.odata ( data)
);
//==========================================================
// Counter: 0 to 9
//==========================================================
module cnt_0to9 ( input
clk,
rst_n,
inc,
dec,
output reg [3:0] odata
);
reg [3:0] res;
always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n)
if (!rst_n)
odata <= 4'h0;
odata <= res;
always @(*)
if (inc)
if (odata == 4'h9)
res = 4'h0;
res = odata + 1'b1;
else if (dec)
if (odata == 4'h0)
res = 4'h9;
res = odata - 1'b1;
res = odata;
end

The example demonstrates the several types of assertions:
1. Immediate assert (npiImmediateAssert): ASSERT1 and ASSERT2.
ASSERT1 is a simple immediate assertion and ASSERT2 is a deferred immediate
assertion.

2. Concurrent assert (npiAssert): ASSERT3.
3. Immediate assume (npiImmediateAssume): Assume1.
4. Concurrent assume (npiAssume): Assume2.
5. Immediate cover (npiImmediateCover): Cover1 and Cover2.
Cover1 is a simple immediate assertion and Cover2 is a deferred immediate assertion.
6. Concurrent cover (npiCover): Cover3.
7. Concurrent restrict (npiRestrict): Restrict1.
For an immediate assertion, NPI provides methods for obtaining checking expression
and action block.
For example, ASSUME1 is an immediate assume statement. The corresponding
expression of ASSUME1 is "!(inc && dec)" that is checked.
If the expression is satisfied, the action block "$info("Info: keep assumption")"
is executed. Otherwise, the else statement "$warning("Warning: inc == 1 && dec
== 1")" is executed.
ASSUME1: assume (!(inc&& dec)) $info("Info: keep assumption");
else $warning("Warning: inc == 1 && dec == 1");

For a concurrent assertion, NPI provides methods for obtaining clocking event, property,
and action block.
For example, Assert3 is a concurrent assert statement. The evaluation of ASSERT3 is
based on the clocking event "@(posedge clk)".
The corresponding property "@(posedge clk) !(data[3]&&data[1])" is evaluated
when the clocking event occurs. In this case, both if-statement and else-statement are null
ASSERT3: assert property ( @(posedge clk) !(data[3]&&data[1]) );

1. There are nine kinds of assertions: sequence inst (npiSequenceInst), assert
(npiAssert), assume (npiAssume), cover (npiCover), restrict (npiRestrict), property
inst (npiPropertyInst), immediate assert (npiImmediateAssert), immediate assume
(npiImmdiateAssume), and immediate cover (npiImmediateCover).
For an assertion object, NPI provides an 1-1 method "npiScope" for querying scope.
2. There are two types of immediate assertions, simple immediate assertions and
deferred immediate assertions. In a simple immediate assertion, pass and fail actions
take place immediately upon assertion evaluation.

In a deferred immediate assertion, the actions are delayed until later in the time step,
providing some level of protection against unintended multiple executions on transient
or "glitch" values.
Deferred assertions use #0 after the verification directive. Querying property
"npiIsDeferred" on an immediate assertion can distinguish if the immediate assertion
is deferred or not.
If the returned value is 1, the assertion is a deferred immediate assertion. Otherwise,
the assertion is a simple immediate assertion.
3. For an immediate assertion, applying 1-1 method "npiExpr" returns the expression that
is required to check.
Applying 1-1 method "npiStmt" returns the action block when the required expression
is satisfied.
For an immediate assert statement whose object type is npiImmediateAssert and
an immediate assume statement whose object type is npiImmediateAssume, NPI
supports 1-1 method "npiElseStmt" to retrieve the action block when the required
expression is violated.
The example of simplified syntax is shown below,
assert (expression) if_stmt else else_stmt

The statement can be a null statement.
4. There are four kinds of concurrent assertions: cover (npiCover), assert (npiAssume),
assume (npiAssume), and restrict (npiRestrict).
The evaluation of a concurrent assertion is based on a clocking event so that the
property of a concurrent assertion is evaluated only at occurrence of the clocking
event.
You can obtain the corresponding clocking event and property by applying 1-1 method
"npiClockingEvent" and "npiProperty", respectively.
As same as immediate assertions, NPI also supports 1-1 method "npiStmt" on
immediate assertions for retrieving the action block when the property is satisfied.
In addition, NPI supports 1-1 method "npiElseStmt" on a concurrent assert statement
(npiAssert) for retrieving action block when the property is violated.
5. There exist two categories of concurrent cover statement, cover sequence and cover
property. The cover sequence statement specifies sequence coverage, while the cover
property statement specifies property coverage.

NPI provides a property named "npiIsCoverSequence" to distinguish if a cover object
is a cover sequence or not.
If the returned value is 1 that means the statement is a sequence coverage. Otherwise,
the statement is a property coverage.

Assignment
Procedural assignments that occur within processes such as always, initial (refer to
Process), task, and function (refer to Task and Function Calls) are treated as assignment
objects in the NPI Language model.

reg LHS, RHS, clk;
LHS = RHS; /*assignment_1*/
LHS = 10 RHS; /*assignment_2*/
LHS <= @(posedge clk) RHS; /*assignment_3*/
LHS <= repeat(5) @(posedge clk) RHS; /*assignment_4*/
end

In the example code above, there are four assignment objects in the initial process,
assignment_1 and assignment_2 are blocking assignments (the property npiBlocking
returns 1), while assignment_3 and assignment_4 are nonblocking assignments (the
property npiBlocking returns 0).
The object assignment_1 has no event control statement, delay control statement, or
repeat control statement.
The object assignment_2 has delay control statement "#10" (npiDelayControl) whose
statement is NULL.
The object assignment_3 has event control statement "@(posedge
clk)" (npiEventControl) whose statement is NULL.
The object assignment_4 has repeat control statement "repeat(5) @(posedge
clk)" (npiRepeatControl) whose event control is "@(posedge clk)" (npiEventControl).

npiOpType returns npiAssignmentOp for normal assignments (both blocking `=' and
nonblocking `<='). For assignment operators, npiOpType returns a value that corresponds
to the operator that is combined with the assignment.
For example, the assignment a += 2; returns npiAddAssignOp for the npiOpType
property.
