Case
"Case" belongs to the class "atomic statement".

module TOP(a, b, c);
input a, b, c;
reg [15:0] result;
reg [3:0] select;
always @ (a or b or c) begin
case(select) /* case statement */
4'd1, 4'd2, 4'd3: result = 16'h1111; /*case item 1*/
4'd4, 4'd5: result = 16'h2222; /*case item 2*/
default : result = 16'h0000; /*case item 3*/

end

In the example code above, for the case statement, applying npi_handle(npiCondition,
case_handle) returns the expression "select". Applying npi_iterate(npiCaseItem,
case_handle) and then the iterator gives the case item #1, #2, and #3.
The property npiCaseType is npiCaseExact for "case", npiCaseX for "casex", and
npiCaseZ for "casez".
For case item #1, applying npi_iterate(npiExpr, case_item_handle) and then the
iterator gives the expression "4'd1", "4'd2", and "4'd3". Applying npi_handle(npiStmt,
case_item_handle) returns the atomic statement "result = 16'h1111".
For case item #3, applying npi_iterate(npiExpr, case_item_handle) and then the iterator
gives NULL (empty) since it is the default case item.

* The case item groups all case conditions that branch to the same statement.
* npi_iterate() returns NULL for the default case item because there is no expression
with the default case.

Class Access Objects
Class access objects denote an expression indicating the way to access class members.

parameter integer tp = 0;
interface class PutImp(type PUT_T = logic);
pure virtual function integer put(PUT_T a);
class Packet (parameter pkp = 0);
integer pki;
pki = val1 + val2;
class LinkedPacket (parameter lpkp = 0)
extends Packet (lpkp)
implements PutImp (integer);
put = a + super.pkp; /* super.pkp is a kind of class access obj and
means accessing super class's member pkp */

class LinkedPacket2 (parameter lpkp = 0)
extends Packet (tp)
implements PutImp (integer);
super.new(tp, tp+1);
virtual class BasePacket;
pure virtual function integer send(bit[31:0] data);
class EtherPacket extends BasePacket;
virtual function integer send(bit[31:0] data);
Packet
p0 = new (0, 0);
LinkedPacket (1)
lp1 = new (1, 2);
LinkedPacket (1)
lpv1 = lp1;
LinkedPacket2 (2)
lp2 = new;
LinkedPacket2 (2)
lp3 = new lp2;
LinkedPacket2 (2)
lpv2 = null;
EtherPacket ep = new;
typedef LinkedPacket tdlp [1:0];
tdlp (0) lpArr = new (0, 1);
$display("lp1.pki: %d", lp1.pki); /* lp1.pki is a kind of class
access obj and means accessing the member of class var "lp1": pki */
$display("lpv1.pki: %d", lpv1.pki); /* lpv1.pki is a kind of class
access obj and means accessing the member of class var "lpv1": pki */
end

In the preceding example, super.pkp under LinkedPacket class definition is a class
access object.
* Applying npiPrefix one-to-one method displays the left-hand-side: super class
typespec Packet(lpkp).
* Applying npiActual one-to-one method displays the actual object: parameter pkp
under the typespec Packet(lpkp) super class.

Besides, for lp1.pki under the initial process,
* Applying npiPrefix one-to-one method displays the left-hand-side: class var top.lp1.
* Applying npiActual one-to-one method displays the actual object: integer pki under
the top.lp1 class object.
Similarly, for lpv1.pki under the initial process,
* Applying npiPrefix one-to-one method displays the left-hand-side: class var
"top.lpv1".
* Applying npiActual one-to-one method displays the actual object: integer pki under
the top.lp1 class object.

The following kinds of access types are present for a class access object:
* npiThisAccess denotes accessing the member of the current class.
* npiSuperAccess denotes accessing the member of the super class.
* npiVarAccess denotes accessing the member of the class var.
* npiDefnAccess denotes accessing the member of class definition by class scope
resolution operator (::).

Class variable is a type of variable that points to a class object only when it is assigned by
a class object created by the "new" keyword.

parameter integer tp = 0;
interface class PutImp(type PUT_T = logic);
pure virtual function integer put(PUT_T a);
class Packet (parameter pkp = 0);
integer pki;
pki = val1 + val2;
class LinkedPacket (parameter lpkp = 0)
extends Packet (lpkp)
implements PutImp (integer);
class LinkedPacket2 (parameter lpkp = 0)
extends Packet (tp)

implements PutImp (integer);
super.new(tp, tp+1);
Packet
p0 = new (0, 0);
LinkedPacket (1) lp1 = new (1, 2); /* class var lp1 has class object
named lp1 created by method func call new */
LinkedPacket (1) lpv1 = lp1; /* class var lpv1 has class object named
lp1 */
LinkedPacket2 (2) lp2 = new; /* class var lp2 has class object named
lp2 created by method func call new */
LinkedPacket2 (2) lp3 = new lp2; /* class var lp3 has class object
named lp3 that is shallow copied from lp2 */
LinkedPacket2 (2) lpv2 = null; /* class var lpv2 has no class object
*/
typedef LinkedPacket tdlp [1:0];
tdlp (1) lpArr = '{lp1, lpv1}; /* array var lpArr whose element is
class var */
$display("lp1.pki: %d", lp1.pki);
$display("lp2.pki: %d", lp2.pki);
end

In the preceding example,
* lp1 is a class var (npiClassVar), and it obtains a class object (npiClassObj) lp1 by
applying npiClassObj one-to-one method.
The class object is created by new method function call with arguments "1" and "2".
Applying one-to-one method npiTypespec to lp1 obtains a class typespec defined by
class definition LinkedPacket with parameter "1".
* lpv1 is also a class var (npiClassVar), but it obtains the class object (npiClassObj)
lp1 by applying npiClassObjone-to-one method.
The class object is assigned by right-hand-side class variable lp1. So, class variables
"lp1" and "lpv1" points to the same class object named lp1.
* lp3 is a class variable (npiClassVar), and it obtains a class object (npiClassObj) lp3
by applying npiClassObj one-to-one method.

lp3 is shallow copied from lp2, and this information can be obtained by applying
npiClassObj method to the new right-hand-side method function call.

* lpv2 is a class variable (npiClassVar), and no class object is returned when applying
npiClassObj one-to-one method.

* NPI language model does not contain simulation information now. So, the creation of
class object only shows the status before simulation.
For example, consider that a class variable is assigned a class object at tenth time unit,
this class variable would not obtain a class object by applying npiClassObj one-to-one
method.
* For a class variable, npiClassTypespec returns the class typespec with which the
class variable is declared in the SystemVerilog source text.
If the class variable has the value as NULL, the npiClassObj relationship applied to
the class variable returns a null handle.
For a class object handle, npiClassTypespec returns the class typespec with which
the class object is created.
The difference between the two usages of npiClassTypespec can be seen in the
following example:
class Packet;

endclass : Packet
class LinkedPacket extends Packet;

endclass : LinkedPacket
LinkedPacket l = new;
Packet p = l;

In this example, the npiClassTypespec of variable "p" is "Packet", but the
npiClassTypespec of the class object associated with variable "p" is "LinkedPacket".
When a class variable is obtained as a data member of a class typespec, the
application must use npiScope rather than npiClassTypespec to obtain the
enclosing scope.
* From a class object, the iterations over npiVariables, npiMethods, npiNamedEvent,
and npiNamedEventArray return both static and automatic properties or methods.
However, the iteration over npiMethods do not include built-in methods for which there
is no explicit declaration.

* The npiParameter iteration returns parameters corresponding to the following:
Parameters declared in the parameter port list of the class declaration.
Parameters declared within the body of the class declaration as class items.
The npiLocalParam property returns TRUE for parameters declared with the body.
The value of a parameter derived from a class object is same as that of the same
parameter derived from the corresponding class typespec.
* If a class variable and a class object have the same full name, applying this full name
to npi_handle_by_name always returns the class variable handle.

input 3 output 3 ce = top.ce;
sequence my_seq;
we 1 (dout==0);
endsequence

my_seq;

Constraint
SystemVerilog allows users to specify constraints to automatically generate tests for
functional verification. A constraint block contains some expressions, that is denoted as
constraint item in NPI and used to specify limitation of random variables.
The constraint item can be bracketed into two categories: constraint ordering and
constraint expr.
The constraint expris a class that contains implication, constr if, constr if else, constr
foreach, and an expression class composed by distribution and general expression
class.

class CLS_EXT; /* CLS_EXT contains one constraint: proto */
rand int x;
extern constraint proto;
constraint CLS_EXT::proto { /* external constraint block */
x >= 0;
}
class CLS_IMPL; /* CLS_IMPL contains one constraint: C1 */
rand bit [15:0] addr;
rand bit align_mode;
constraint C1 {
(align_mode==0) -> addr[3:0] == 0; /* implication */
(align_mode==1) -> addr[7:0] == 0;
}
class CLS_ORDER; /* CLS_ORDER contains two constraints: C2 and C3 */
rand bit s;

rand bit [31:0] d;
constraint C2 {
if (!s) d==1;
/* constr if */
}
constraint C3 {
solve s before d; /* constraint ordering */
}
class CLS_FOREACH; /* CLS_FOREACH contains one constrain: C4 */
rand byte A[] ;
constraint C4 {
foreach (A[i]) /* constr foreach */
A[i] > 2*i;
}

In the aforementioned example, the class "CLS_EXT" contains one constraint object named
"proto", that can be obtained by the npiConstraint iteration.
"proto" is an external constraint block that means the constraint is declared outside its
enclosing class declaration when its constraint prototype appears in the enclosing class
declaration.
The npiExtern property of "proto" is 1 and the npiExternLineNo and npiExternFile
property returns the location of its external declaration. Applying npiConstraintItem
iteration on "proto" returns a constraint expression "x >= 0".
The constraint "C1" contains two constraint expression, both are implication
(npiImplication). Applying npiCondition relation on an implication expression returns the
expression before the syntax "->".
In addition, the npiConstraintExpr iteration returns the constraint expressions after the
syntax "->".
The constraint "C2" and "C3" contains a constr if expression (npiConstrIf) and constraint
ordering (npiConstraintOrdering), respectively.
For the constraint ordering "solve s before d", npiSolveBefore iteration returns the
expression "s" and npiSolveAfter iteration returns the expression "d".
The constraint "C4" contains a constr foreach (npiConstrForeach). Applying npiVariables
relation on this constr foreach, the array "A" is returned.
The loop variable "i" can be obtained by the npiLoopVars iteration from the constr
foreach.

* For a constraint, npiExtern property shows whether it is an external constraint block or
not.

Covergroup
The coverage group (covergroup) construct encapsulates the specification of a coverage
model. Each covergroup specification can include the following components:
* A set of coverage points (cover point).
* Cross coverage between coverage points (cover cross).
* Coverage options (coverage option).
A covergroup can be defined in a package, module, program, interface, or class.
A cover point specifies an integral expression that is to be covered. Each cover point
includes a set of bins associated with the sample values or value transitions of the
covered expression.
A cover cross can be specified between two or more cover point objects or variables.
Any combination of more than two variables or previously declared coverage points is
allowed.
SystemVerilog implicitly creates a cover point for the variable defined by a cover cross
A coverage option controls the behavior of the covergroup, coverpoint, and cross. A
covergroup object can specify one or more coverage option objects.

module mod;
wire clk;
enum { red, green, blue } color;
bit [3:0] pixel_adr, pixel_offset, pixel_hue;
covergroup cv (ref int ra, input int low, int high) @(posedge clk); /*
covergroup */
option.at_least = low; /* coverage option */

Hue: coverpoint pixel_hue; /* cover point */
Offset: coverpoint pixel_offset; /* cover point */
AxC: cross color, pixel_adr; /* cover cross, cover point */
all: cross color, Hue, Offset; /* cover cross, cover point */
coverpoint ra { /* cover point */
bins good = { [low : high] };
bins bad[] = default;
}
endgroup

In the aforementioned example, the coverage group "cv" is declared inside the module
"mod" so the npiCovergroup object "cv" can be retrieved from "mod" by applying the
method npiCovergroup.
The coverage group "cv" includes one coverage option (npiCoverageOption), three
coverage points (npiCoverPoint), and two cross coverage items (npiCoverCross).
According to the syntax, explicit coverage points labeled "Hue" and "Offset" are defined for
variables pixel_hueand "pixel_offset", and an implicit coverage point is defined for "ra".
Besides, SystemVerilog implicitly declares coverage points for variables "color" and
"pixel_adr" since the variables are defined in cross coverage items "AxC" and "all".
Therefore, five npiCoverPoint objects are returned by the 1-n method npiCoverPoint:
"Hue", "Offset", "ra", "color", and "pixel_adr". Two npiCoverCross objects are returned by
the 1-n method npiCoverCross: "AxC" and "all".
There is one coverage option specified to control the coverage data by the syntax
"option.at_least = low;".
The option named "at_least" can be retrieved by the 1-n method npiCoverageOption from
the coverage group. Since the coverage option is defined as "option.member_identifier",
the property npiCovoptType returns npiOptionCovopt.
Apply the 1-n method npiBins on the coverage points "ra", two bins objects are returned.
The bins object can be specified by keywords bins, ignore_bins, or illegal_bins. In the
example, the bins objects are declared by keyword "bins" so the property npiBinsType
returns npiNormalBins.
The 1-1 method npiBinsSpec is used to retrieve the definition expression for coverage
bins, for example, a range operation "[low : high]" is returned for the npiBins object "bins
good = { [low : high] };".

* Coverage groups can be retrieved from instance handles by the 1-n method
npiCovergroup.
* For a coverage group, the 1-n methods npiCoverageOption returns the coverage
options declared inside the coverage group.
The 1-n methods npiCoverPoint and npiCoverCross returns the coverage point and
cover cross objects, respectively.
The 1-n method npiCoverageEvent is used to retrieve coverage events. The coverage
event is expression, event control, or events.
* For a coverage option, the property npiCovoptType describes member type. If
the coverage option is declared as option.member_identifier, the property returns
npiOptionCovopt.
If the coverage option is declared as type_option.member_identifier, the property
returns npiTypeOptCovopt. Otherwise, it returns npiIllegalCovopt.
* The class "coverage spec" (npiCoverageSpec) contains two object types: coverage
point (npiCoverPoint) and cover cross (npiCoverCross).
For a coverage point, the 1-1 method npiExpr and npiIff are used to retrieve coverpoint
expression and iff expression, respectively.
The 1-n method npiBins returns bins objects if there exists any bins object inside the
coverage point. For a cover cross, the 1-1 method npiIff can retrieve the iff expression
and the 1-n method npiCorssItems returns cross item objects. The cross items could
be coverage points or variables.
* For a bins object, the property npiBinsType is npiNormalBins, npiIgnoreBins, or
npiIllegalBins according to different bins keywords.
If the bins keyword is illegal_bins or ignore_bins, the property returns npiIllegalBins or
npiIgnoreBins, respectively. Otherwise, it returns npiNormalBins.
The bins construct allows creating a separate bin for each value in the given range list
or a single bin for the entire range of values, the 1-1 method npiBinsSpec returns an
expression described the range of variables.

Distribution, Dist Item
A distribution (npiDistribution) is a set of weighted value. The distribution set is a commaseparated list of integral expressions and ranges.
Each term in the list is named dist item (npiDistItem). Optionally, each dist item can have
a weight, which is specified using the ":=" (npiEqualDist) or ":/" (npiDivDist) operators.

class CLS_DIST;
rand int x, y, z;
constraint CX {
x dist { 100 := 1, 200 := 2, 300 := 5 }; /* distribution with
three dist items, each dist item contains range value and weight with
npiEqualDist type */
}
constraint CY {
y dist { [100:102] :/ 1, 200 := 2, 300 := 5 }; /* distribution with
three dist items, each dist item contains range value and weight. Range
[100:102] uses npiDivDist operator, the rest items use npiEqualDist
}
constraint CZ {
z dist { 100, 200, 300 }; /* distribution with three dist items. No
weight is specified so each dist item uses default weight ":=1" */
}

In the aforementioned example, "y dist { [100:102] :/ 1, 200 := 2, 300 := 5}" is a distribution
expression (npiDistribution) with an integral expression "y" and three dist items. Each
dist item (npiDistItem) contains a range value and a weight.
For example, the first dist item "[100:102]:/ 1" is constructed by a range value "[100:102]"
and a weight "1" that is specified by a divided operator ":/" (npiDivDist).
The rest two dist items contain weight value that are specified by equal operators
"=/" (npiEqualDist).
When no weight is specified for dist item, default weight ":=1" is used and the property
npiDistType returns "-1".

1. The npiDistType property of a dist item (npiDistItem) returns npiEqualDist,
npiDivDist, or npiUndefined. npiEqualDist implies the weight is specified by equal
operator ":=1". npiDivDist implies the weight is specified by a divided operator ":/".
If no weight is specified, npiDistType is npiUndefined.
2. The npiWeight method of a dist item (npiDistItem) returns a weight expression. If no
weight is specified, npiWeight returns NULL.

Expression is a group that contains simple-expression, part-select, indexed-part-select,
operation, constant, function-call, sys-function-call, ref-obj, method-func-call, gen-var and
class-access-obj.
Part-select or indexed-part-select is a kind of slicing by specified range. Operation is a
combination of expressions. Constant is the constant value in a design.

typedef bit [1:0] TD;
module mm(a);
bit [3:0] r; /* bit var */
parameter p = 3;
/* Rhs: npiOperation with op-type npiAssignmentPatternOp */

TD
/*
TD
/*

t0 [1:0] = '{{0, 0}, {0, 0}};
Rhs: npiOperation with op-type npiMultiAssignmentPatternOp */
t1 [1:0] = '{2{'{0, 0}}};
Rhs: npiOperation with op-type npiConcatOp; TD'{0, 1}:
npiOperation with op-type npiAssignmentPatternExprOp */
TD t2 [1:0] = {TD'{0, 1}, TD'{default:0}};
mm m0(r[0]);
r[1:0] /* part select */ = 0; /* assignment */
r[2-:3] /* indexed part select */ = 0; /* assignment */
r[p-:4] /* indexed part select */ = 0; /* assignment */
if (r[0] == 0/* operation with npiOpType: npiEqOp */)
r[3] = 0;
end

In the example code above, part-select "top.r[1:0]" (size is equal to 2) gets constant "1"
and "0" by applying method npiLeftRange and npiRightRange, respectively, and gets bitvar "top.r" by applying method npiParent.
Similarly, indexed-part-select "top.r[2-:3]" (size is equal to 3) gets constant "2" and "3" by
applying method npiBaseExpr and npiWidthExpr, respectively, and gets bit-var "top.r" by
applying method npiParent.
Besides, the default expression of t0, t1 and t2 are operations with npiOpType:
npiAssignmentPatternOp, npiMultiAssignmentPatternOp and npiConcatOp respectively.
For t0's default expression, applying 1-to-many method npiOperand gets two npiConcatOp
operations.
For t1's default expression, applying 1-to-many method npiOperand get a npiConstant 2
and a npiAssignmentPatternOp operation. For t2's default expression, applying 1-to-many
method npiOperand gets two npiAssignmentPatternExprOp operations.
npiAssignmentPatternExprOp operation TD'{default:0} get a npiBitTypespec named "TD"
and a npiAssignmentPatternOp operation by applying 1-to-many method npiOperand.

* For an operator whose type is npiMultiConcatOp, the first operand is the multiplier
expression. The remaining operands are the expressions within the concatenation.

expression being the type to which the argument is being cast.

In the following example, the first RHS operation's npiOptype is npiTypeCastOp so it
can get the typespec by applying npiTypespec.
The second RHS operation's npiOptype is npiSigningCastOp, and its signed property
returns 1. The third RHS operation's npiOptype is npiSizeCastOp, and its size property

Generate constructs are used to either conditionally or multiply instantiate generate blocks
into a model. A generate block is a collection of one or more module items.

"Generate scope" belongs to the class "scope".

parameter p = 4;
wire [7:0] a;
wire [7:0] aa;
if(p > 0)
begin: B
/* gen scope, top.B */
and u0 (a[0], a[1],b);
end
for (i=0; i<p; i=i+1)
begin: BB /* gen scope, top.BB[0] ~ top.BB[3] */
assign a[i] = ^a[p-1:i];
end
for (i=0; i<p; i=i+1)
begin /* unamed gen scope, top.gblk1[0] ~ top.gblk1[3] */
assign aa[i] = ^aa[p-1:i];

end

In the example code above, for the first generate description, the gen scope "top.B" is
generated. For the second generate description, four gen scopes, "top.BB[0]", "top.BB[1]",
"top.BB[2]", and "top.BB[3]" are generated.
For the third generate description, four unnamed gen scope, "top.gblk1[0]", "top.gblk1[1]",
"top.gblk1[2]", and "top.gblk1[3]" are generated. Refer SystemVerilog LRM Chapter 27.for
details of the unnamed gen scope.
The property npiArrayMember for the gen scope "top.B" is "0" (FALSE). The property
npiArrayMember for the gen scope "top.BB[0]", "top.BB[1]", "top.BB[2]" and "top.BB[3]" is
"1" (TRUE).
The property npiArrayMember for the gen scope "top.gblk1[0]", "top.gblk1[1]",
"top.gblk1[2]" and "top.gblk1[3]" is "1" (TRUE).
The property npiImplicitDecl for the gen scope "top.B" is "0" (FALSE). The property
npiImplicitDecl for the gen scope "top.BB[0]", "top.BB[1]", "top.BB[2]" and "top.BB[3]" is
"0" (FALSE). The property npiImplicitDecl for the gen scope "top.gblk1[0]", "top.gblk1[1]",
"top.gblk1[2]" and "top.gblk1[3]" is "1" (TRUE).

1. For an unnamed generate, an implicit scope is created. Its npiImplicitDecl property
returns TRUE.
2. References to gen vars within the gen scope is treated as local parameters.
3. Parameters within the gen scope must be local parameters.

The instantiations of modules/interfaces/primitives/programs can contain a range
specification. This allows an array of instances to be created.
In the NPI Language model, there are five kinds of instances array objects - module array,
interface array, gate array, switch array and UDP array.
The later three instance array objects belong to the class "primitive array".

module top; /* module */
mm u1 /* module */(w1, w2[0]);
mm u2[3:0] /* module array */ (w1, w2);
initial begin : INIT_BLK

end

In the example code above, "top.u2" is an object with type "module
array" (npiModuleArray).
Applying method "npiExpr" to the handle "top.u2", an operation handle (npiOperation) with
two operands w1, w2 is returned (operands w1 and w2 are the objects with type npiNet
and npiArrayNet, separately).
Applying method "npiRange" to the handle "top.u2", an iterator handle that contains
one range object (npiRange) is returned. Applying methods "npiLeftRange" and
"npiRightRange" to the range object, constant handles (npiConstant) "3" and "0" is
returned, separately.

* Traversing from the instance array to expr returns a simple expression object of type
npiOperation with a npiOpType of npiListOp. This expression is used to access the
actual list of connections to the instance array in the SystemVerilog source code.

In the NPI Language model, IO declaration is a kind of object that represents the

module m_task();
task convert;
input [7:0] data; /*IO declaration*/
output [7:0] result; /*IO declaration*/
result = (9/5)*(result+32);
end
task automatic counter(ref int cnt); /*IO declaration*/
cnt = cnt + 1;

In the example code above, "input [7:0] data", "output [7:0] result", and "ref int cnt" are
objects with type "IO declaration" (npiIODecl).
Applying method "npiExpr" to the first IO declaration of task "convert" (npiTask) returns a
reg var (npiReg) named "data".
Applying method "npiExpr" to the second IO declaration of task "convert" (npiTask) returns
a reg var (npiReg) named "result".
Applying method "npiExpr" to IO declaration of task "counter" (npiTask) returns a ref obj
named "cnt".

Alias Statement
An alias statement declares multiple names for the same physical net, or bits within a net.

module top (inout wire [15:0] bus16,
inout wire [7:0] data_mst,
inout wire [7:0] data_slv
);
alias bus16 = {data_mst, data_slv}; /* alias statement */
wire [3:0] addr, addr_s1, addr_s2;
alias addr = addr_s1 = addr_s2; /* alias statement */

In example.v, the module "top" contains two alias statement "alias bus16 =
{data_mst, data_slv};" and "alias addr = addr_s1 = addr_s2;".
The alias statements can be retrieved by the 1-m relationship "npiAliasStmt".
For an alias statement, the 1-m relationship "npiNetAlias" can retrieve all expressions
declared by net alias.
For example, a net handle "bus16" and an operation handle "{data_mst, data_slv}"
would be returned by applying "npiNetAlias" on the first alias statement.
The three net handles "addr", "addr_s1", and "addr_s2", are returned on the second alias

The 1-m relationship "npiNetAlias" iterates the alias statement and returns all expressions
that are declared by net alias.

Assertion
In the NPI language model, assertion is a class that contains several objects. The object is
one of the following kinds:
* assert: A concurrent assert statement that is used to enforce a property. The
corresponding object type is "npiAssert".
* assume: A concurrent assume statement that is to allowed properties to be considered
as assumptions for formal analysis as well as for dynamic simulation tools. The
corresponding object type is "npiAssume".
* cover: A concurrent cover statement with object type "npiCover". There exist two
categories of cover statement, cover sequence and cover property.
The cover sequence statement specifies sequence coverage, while the cover
property statement specifies property coverage.
NPI provides a property named "npiIsCoverSequence" to distinguish if a cover object
is a cover sequence or not.
* restrict, a concurrent restrict statement with object type "npiRestrict".
* immediate assert, that is an immediate assert statement with object type
"npiImmediateAssert".
* immediate assume, that is an immediate assume statement with object type
"npiImmediateAssume".
* immediate cover, that is an immediate cover statement with object type
"npiImmediateCover".

* sequence inst, that is an instance of a named sequence with object type
"npiSequenceInst".
* property inst, that is an instance of a named property with object type
"npiPropertyInst".
There are two kinds of assertion statement: immediate and concurrent.
* Immediate assertions follow simulation event semantics for their execution and are
executed like a statement in a procedural block. Immediate assertions are primarily
intended to be used with simulation.
There are three kinds belonged to immediate assertion as follows:
Immediate assert (npiImmediateAssert)
Immediate assume (npiImmediateAssume)
Immediate cover (npiImmediateCover).
Immediate assertions can be divided into simple immediate assertions and deferred
immediate assertions.
NPI provides a property named "npiIsDeferred" to distinguish if the immediate
assertion is a deferred immediate assertion or a simple immediate assertion.
* Concurrent assertions are based on a clock semantics and use sample values
of variables. The keyword property distinguishes a concurrent assertion from an
immediate assertion.
There are four kinds belonged to concurrent assertion as follows:
Assert (npiAssert)
Assume (npiAssume)
Cover (npiCover)
Restrict (npiRestrict)

/* concurrent restrict */
RESTRICT1: restrict property ( @(posedge clk) (data > 9) );
// Design instantiation --------------------------cnt_0to9 cnt ( .clk ( clk),
.rst_n ( rst_n),

);
//==========================================================
// Counter: 0 to 9
//==========================================================
module cnt_0to9 ( input
clk,
rst_n,
inc,
dec,
output reg [3:0] odata
);
reg [3:0] res;
always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n)
if (!rst_n)
odata <= 4'h0;
odata <= res;
always @(*)
if (inc)
if (odata == 4'h9)
res = 4'h0;
res = odata + 1'b1;
else if (dec)
if (odata == 4'h0)
res = 4'h9;
res = odata - 1'b1;
res = odata;
end

The example demonstrates the several types of assertions:
1. Immediate assert (npiImmediateAssert): ASSERT1 and ASSERT2.
ASSERT1 is a simple immediate assertion and ASSERT2 is a deferred immediate
assertion.

2. Concurrent assert (npiAssert): ASSERT3.
3. Immediate assume (npiImmediateAssume): Assume1.
4. Concurrent assume (npiAssume): Assume2.
5. Immediate cover (npiImmediateCover): Cover1 and Cover2.
Cover1 is a simple immediate assertion and Cover2 is a deferred immediate assertion.
6. Concurrent cover (npiCover): Cover3.
7. Concurrent restrict (npiRestrict): Restrict1.
For an immediate assertion, NPI provides methods for obtaining checking expression
and action block.
For example, ASSUME1 is an immediate assume statement. The corresponding
expression of ASSUME1 is "!(inc && dec)" that is checked.
If the expression is satisfied, the action block "$info("Info: keep assumption")"
is executed. Otherwise, the else statement "$warning("Warning: inc == 1 && dec
== 1")" is executed.
ASSUME1: assume (!(inc&& dec)) $info("Info: keep assumption");
else $warning("Warning: inc == 1 && dec == 1");

For a concurrent assertion, NPI provides methods for obtaining clocking event, property,
and action block.
For example, Assert3 is a concurrent assert statement. The evaluation of ASSERT3 is
based on the clocking event "@(posedge clk)".
The corresponding property "@(posedge clk) !(data[3]&&data[1])" is evaluated
when the clocking event occurs. In this case, both if-statement and else-statement are null
ASSERT3: assert property ( @(posedge clk) !(data[3]&&data[1]) );

1. There are nine kinds of assertions: sequence inst (npiSequenceInst), assert
(npiAssert), assume (npiAssume), cover (npiCover), restrict (npiRestrict), property
inst (npiPropertyInst), immediate assert (npiImmediateAssert), immediate assume
(npiImmdiateAssume), and immediate cover (npiImmediateCover).
For an assertion object, NPI provides an 1-1 method "npiScope" for querying scope.
2. There are two types of immediate assertions, simple immediate assertions and
deferred immediate assertions. In a simple immediate assertion, pass and fail actions
take place immediately upon assertion evaluation.

In a deferred immediate assertion, the actions are delayed until later in the time step,
providing some level of protection against unintended multiple executions on transient
or "glitch" values.
Deferred assertions use #0 after the verification directive. Querying property
"npiIsDeferred" on an immediate assertion can distinguish if the immediate assertion
is deferred or not.
If the returned value is 1, the assertion is a deferred immediate assertion. Otherwise,
the assertion is a simple immediate assertion.
3. For an immediate assertion, applying 1-1 method "npiExpr" returns the expression that
is required to check.
Applying 1-1 method "npiStmt" returns the action block when the required expression
is satisfied.
For an immediate assert statement whose object type is npiImmediateAssert and
an immediate assume statement whose object type is npiImmediateAssume, NPI
supports 1-1 method "npiElseStmt" to retrieve the action block when the required
expression is violated.
The example of simplified syntax is shown below,
assert (expression) if_stmt else else_stmt

The statement can be a null statement.
4. There are four kinds of concurrent assertions: cover (npiCover), assert (npiAssume),
assume (npiAssume), and restrict (npiRestrict).
The evaluation of a concurrent assertion is based on a clocking event so that the
property of a concurrent assertion is evaluated only at occurrence of the clocking
event.
You can obtain the corresponding clocking event and property by applying 1-1 method
"npiClockingEvent" and "npiProperty", respectively.
As same as immediate assertions, NPI also supports 1-1 method "npiStmt" on
immediate assertions for retrieving the action block when the property is satisfied.
In addition, NPI supports 1-1 method "npiElseStmt" on a concurrent assert statement
(npiAssert) for retrieving action block when the property is violated.
5. There exist two categories of concurrent cover statement, cover sequence and cover
property. The cover sequence statement specifies sequence coverage, while the cover
property statement specifies property coverage.

NPI provides a property named "npiIsCoverSequence" to distinguish if a cover object
is a cover sequence or not.
If the returned value is 1 that means the statement is a sequence coverage. Otherwise,
the statement is a property coverage.

Bit Select
"Bit select" selects a single bit of the parameter (npiParameter), integer var
(npiIntegerVar), time var (npiTimeVar), byte var (npiByteVar), short int var (npiShortIntVar),
int var (npiIntVar) and long int var (npiLongIntVar).
"Bit select" belongs to the class "simple expression".

time t;
parameter p = 3;

integer i;

In the example code above, "t[0]", "p[0]", "i[0]" are bit-select (npiBitSelect).

For bit-selects, the npiUse relationship accesses any specific use of that bit, any use of the
parent vector, and any part-select that contains the bit.

Refer to the npiBitSelect section in the Language Model - Complete Supported List section

Case
"Case" belongs to the class "atomic statement".

module TOP(a, b, c);
input a, b, c;
reg [15:0] result;
reg [3:0] select;
always @ (a or b or c) begin
case(select) /* case statement */
4'd1, 4'd2, 4'd3: result = 16'h1111; /*case item 1*/
4'd4, 4'd5: result = 16'h2222; /*case item 2*/
default : result = 16'h0000; /*case item 3*/

end

In the example code above, for the case statement, applying npi_handle(npiCondition,
case_handle) returns the expression "select". Applying npi_iterate(npiCaseItem,
case_handle) and then the iterator gives the case item #1, #2, and #3.
The property npiCaseType is npiCaseExact for "case", npiCaseX for "casex", and
npiCaseZ for "casez".
For case item #1, applying npi_iterate(npiExpr, case_item_handle) and then the
iterator gives the expression "4'd1", "4'd2", and "4'd3". Applying npi_handle(npiStmt,
case_item_handle) returns the atomic statement "result = 16'h1111".
For case item #3, applying npi_iterate(npiExpr, case_item_handle) and then the iterator
gives NULL (empty) since it is the default case item.

* The case item groups all case conditions that branch to the same statement.
* npi_iterate() returns NULL for the default case item because there is no expression
with the default case.

Class Access Objects
Class access objects denote an expression indicating the way to access class members.

parameter integer tp = 0;
interface class PutImp(type PUT_T = logic);
pure virtual function integer put(PUT_T a);
class Packet (parameter pkp = 0);
integer pki;
pki = val1 + val2;
class LinkedPacket (parameter lpkp = 0)
extends Packet (lpkp)
implements PutImp (integer);
put = a + super.pkp; /* super.pkp is a kind of class access obj and
means accessing super class's member pkp */

class LinkedPacket2 (parameter lpkp = 0)
extends Packet (tp)
implements PutImp (integer);
super.new(tp, tp+1);
virtual class BasePacket;
pure virtual function integer send(bit[31:0] data);
class EtherPacket extends BasePacket;
virtual function integer send(bit[31:0] data);
Packet
p0 = new (0, 0);
LinkedPacket (1)
lp1 = new (1, 2);
LinkedPacket (1)
lpv1 = lp1;
LinkedPacket2 (2)
lp2 = new;
LinkedPacket2 (2)
lp3 = new lp2;
LinkedPacket2 (2)
lpv2 = null;
EtherPacket ep = new;
typedef LinkedPacket tdlp [1:0];
tdlp (0) lpArr = new (0, 1);
$display("lp1.pki: %d", lp1.pki); /* lp1.pki is a kind of class
access obj and means accessing the member of class var "lp1": pki */
$display("lpv1.pki: %d", lpv1.pki); /* lpv1.pki is a kind of class
access obj and means accessing the member of class var "lpv1": pki */
end

In the preceding example, super.pkp under LinkedPacket class definition is a class
access object.
* Applying npiPrefix one-to-one method displays the left-hand-side: super class
typespec Packet(lpkp).
* Applying npiActual one-to-one method displays the actual object: parameter pkp
under the typespec Packet(lpkp) super class.

Besides, for lp1.pki under the initial process,
* Applying npiPrefix one-to-one method displays the left-hand-side: class var top.lp1.

title: 05 endmodule

piActual one-to-one method displays the actual object: parameter pkp
under the typespec Packet(lpkp) super class.

Besides, for lp1.pki under the initial process,
* Applying npiPrefix one-to-one method displays the left-hand-side: class var top.lp1.
* Applying npiActual one-to-one method displays the actual object: integer pki under
the top.lp1 class object.
Similarly, for lpv1.pki under the initial process,
* Applying npiPrefix one-to-one method displays the left-hand-side: class var
"top.lpv1".
* Applying npiActual one-to-one method displays the actual object: integer pki under
the top.lp1 class object.

The following kinds of access types are present for a class access object:
* npiThisAccess denotes accessing the member of the current class.
* npiSuperAccess denotes accessing the member of the super class.
* npiVarAccess denotes accessing the member of the class var.
* npiDefnAccess denotes accessing the member of class definition by class scope
resolution operator (::).

class LinkedPacket (parameter lpkp = 0) /* class defn "LinkedPacket"
with parameter lpkp */
extends Packet (lpkp) /* extend class typespec: "Packet#(lpkp)"
based on class defn: "Packet" */
implements PutImp (integer); /* implement class typespec:
"PutImp#(integer)" based on class defn "PutImp" */
class LinkedPacket2 (parameter lpkp = 0) /* class defn "LinkedPacket2"
with parameter lpkp */
extends Packet (tp) /* extend class typespec: "Packet#(tp)" based on
class defn: "Packet" */
implements PutImp (integer); /* implement class typespec:
"PutImp#(integer)" based on class defn "PutImp" */
super.new(tp, tp+1);
virtual class BasePacket; /* virtual class defn "BasePacket" */
pure virtual function integer send(bit[31:0] data); /* virtual class
method "send" */
class EtherPacket extends BasePacket; /* class defn "EtherPacket"
extends class typespec "BasePacket"
based on clas defn "BasePacket" */
virtual function integer send(bit[31:0] data); /* implementation of
virtual method from in base class */
Packet
p0 = new (0, 0);
LinkedPacket (1) lp1 = new (1, 2);
LinkedPacket (1) lpv1 = lp1;
LinkedPacket2 (2) lp2 = new;
LinkedPacket2 (2) lp3 = new lp2;
LinkedPacket2 (2) lpv2 = null;
EtherPacket ep = new;
typedef LinkedPacket tdlp [1:0];

tdlp (0) lpArr = new (0, 1);
$display("lp1.pki: %d", lp1.pki);
$display("lp2.pki: %d", lp2.pki);
end

In the preceding example, Packet is a class definition (npiClassDefn), and it obtains
subclass definition classes LinkedPacket and LinkedPacket2 by applying the
npiDerivedClasses 1-to-many method.
The LinkedPacket class definition obtains class typespec (npiClassTypespec) Packet
and class typespec PutImp by applying one-to-one method npiExtends and 1-to-many
method npiImplements respectively.
The class typespec information shows the base class information for class definition
LinkedPacket.

* The npiDerivedClasses iterator returns all the class definitions derived from the given
class definition.
* The relation to npiExtends exists whenever one class is derived from another class.
The relation extends to class typespec and provides the base class.
* The npiParameter iteration returns parameters corresponding to,
Parameters declared in the parameter port list of the class declaration.
Parameters declared within the body of the class declaration as class items.
The npiLocalParam property returns TRUE for parameters declared with the body.
The value of a parameter derived from a class object is the same as that of the same
parameter derived from the corresponding class typespec.

Refer to the npiClassDefn section in the Language Model - Complete Supported List

Class typespec
Class typespec denotes the actual definition of a class object and its parameter values
that have been determined.

parameter integer tp = 0;
interface class PutImp(type PUT_T = logic);
pure virtual function integer put(PUT_T a);
class Packet (parameter pkp = 0);
integer pki;
pki = val1 + val2;
class LinkedPacket (parameter lpkp = 0)
extends Packet (lpkp) /* extend class typespec: "Packet#(lpkp)"
based on class defn: "Packet" */
implements PutImp (integer); /* implement class typespec:
"PutImp#(integer)" based on class defn "PutImp" */

class LinkedPacket2 (parameter lpkp = 0)
extends Packet (tp) /* extend class typespec: "Packet#(tp)" based on
class defn: "Packet" */
implements PutImp (integer); /* implement class typespec:
"PutImp#(integer)" based on class defn "PutImp" */
super.new(tp, tp+1);
virtual class BasePacket;
pure virtual function integer send(bit[31:0] data);
class EtherPacket extends BasePacket; /* class defn "EtherPacket"
extends class typespec "BasePacket"
based on clas defn "BasePacket" */
virtual function integer send(bit[31:0] data);
Packet
p0 = new (0, 0);
LinkedPacket (1) lp1 = new (1, 2); /* class var "lp1" with class
typespec "LinkedPacket#(1)";
class obj "lp1" with class typespec "LinkedPacket(1)" */
LinkedPacket (1) lpv1 = lp1; /* class var "lpv1" with class typespec
"LinkedPacket#(1)" */
LinkedPacket2 (2) lp2 = new;
LinkedPacket2 (2) lp3 = new lp2;
LinkedPacket2 (2) lpv2 = null;
EtherPacket ep = new;
typedef LinkedPacket tdlp [1:0];
tdlp (0) lpArr = new (0, 1);
$display("lp1.pki: %d", lp1.pki);
$display("lp2.pki: %d", lp2.pki);
end

In the preceding example, top.lp1 is a class variable with class typespec
(npiClassTypespec) LinkedPacket(1). This typespec means the specialization of class
definition LinkedPacket with the parameter assignment lpkp = 5.

The LinkedPacket class definition obtains class typespec (npiClassTypespec) Packet
and class typespec PutImp by applying one-to-one method npiExtends and 1-to-many
method npiImplements respectively.
The class typespec information shows the base class information for class definition
LinkedPacket.

* Sub objects generated by class typespec get nothing by applying npiFullName.
* The npiExtends relation returns the base class typespec, if any, from which a given
class typespec is derived. The base class typespec of a class specialization is also a
specialization.
* The npiParameter iteration returns parameters corresponding to the following:
Parameters declared in the parameter port list of the class declaration.
Parameters declared within the body of the class declaration as class items.
The npiLocalParam property returns TRUE for parameters declared within the body.
* The npiClassDefn relation returns NULL for built-in classes.

Refer to the npiClassTypespec section in the Language Model - Complete Supported List

Class Variables and Class Objects
Class variable is a type of variable that points to a class object only when it is assigned by
a class object created by the "new" keyword.

text:
implements PutImp (integer);
super.new(tp, tp+1);
Packet
p0 = new (0, 0);
LinkedPacket (1) lp1 = new (1, 2); /* class var lp1 has class object
named lp1 created by method func call new */
LinkedPacket (1) lpv1 = lp1; /* class var lpv1 has class object named
lp1 */
LinkedPacket2 (2) lp2 = new; /* class var lp2 has class object named
lp2 created by method func call new */
LinkedPacket2 (2) lp3 = new lp2; /* class var lp3 has class object
named lp3 that is shallow copied from lp2 */
LinkedPacket2 (2) lpv2 = null; /* class var lpv2 has no class object
*/
typedef LinkedPacket tdlp [1:0];
tdlp (1) lpArr = '{lp1, lpv1}; /* array var lpArr whose element is
class var */
$display("lp1.pki: %d", lp1.pki);
$display("lp2.pki: %d", lp2.pki);
end

In the preceding example,
* lp1 is a class var (npiClassVar), and it obtains a class object (npiClassObj) lp1 by
applying npiClassObj one-to-one method.
The class object is created by new method function call with arguments "1" and "2".
Applying one-to-one method npiTypespec to lp1 obtains a class typespec defined by
class definition LinkedPacket with parameter "1".
* lpv1 is also a class var (npiClassVar), but it obtains the class object (npiClassObj)
lp1 by applying npiClassObjone-to-one method.
The class object is assigned by right-hand-side class variable lp1. So, class variables
"lp1" and "lpv1" points to the same class object named lp1.
* lp3 is a class variable (npiClassVar), and it obtains a class object (npiClassObj) lp3
by applying npiClassObj one-to-one method.

lp3 is shallow copied from lp2, and this information can be obtained by applying
npiClassObj method to the new right-hand-side method function call.

* lpv2 is a class variable (npiClassVar), and no class object is returned when applying
npiClassObj one-to-one method.

* NPI language model does not contain simulation information now. So, the creation of
class object only shows the status before simulation.
For example, consider that a class variable is assigned a class object at tenth time unit,
this class variable would not obtain a class object by applying npiClassObj one-to-one
method.
* For a class variable, npiClassTypespec returns the class typespec with which the
class variable is declared in the SystemVerilog source text.
If the class variable has the value as NULL, the npiClassObj relationship applied to
the class variable returns a null handle.
For a class object handle, npiClassTypespec returns the class typespec with which
the class object is created.
The difference between the two usages of npiClassTypespec can be seen in the
following example:
class Packet;

endclass : Packet
class LinkedPacket extends Packet;

title: 05 endmodule
text:
endclass : LinkedPacket
LinkedPacket l = new;
Packet p = l;

In this example, the npiClassTypespec of variable "p" is "Packet", but the
npiClassTypespec of the class object associated with variable "p" is "LinkedPacket".
When a class variable is obtained as a data member of a class typespec, the
application must use npiScope rather than npiClassTypespec to obtain the
enclosing scope.
* From a class object, the iterations over npiVariables, npiMethods, npiNamedEvent,
and npiNamedEventArray return both static and automatic properties or methods.
However, the iteration over npiMethods do not include built-in methods for which there
is no explicit declaration.

* The npiParameter iteration returns parameters corresponding to the following:
Parameters declared in the parameter port list of the class declaration.
Parameters declared within the body of the class declaration as class items.
The npiLocalParam property returns TRUE for parameters declared with the body.
The value of a parameter derived from a class object is same as that of the same
parameter derived from the corresponding class typespec.
* If a class variable and a class object have the same full name, applying this full name
to npi_handle_by_name always returns the class variable handle.

Refer to the npiClassVar and npiClassObjsections in the Language Model - Complete
Supported List section of Appendix A.

Clocking Block, Clocking IO declaration
The clocking block construct identifies clock signals and captures the timing and
synchronization requirements of the blocks being modeled.
A clocking block assembles signals that are synchronous to a particular clock and makes
their timing explicit.
In NPI Language model, a clocking block (npiClockingBlock) represents a kind of
scope object that is assembled by clocking event, default skew setting, and clocking io
declaration (npiClockingIODecl).

interface in tf_bus ( input clk );
wire [7:0] din;
wire [7:0] addr;
wire [7:0] dout;
wire ce, we;
clocking cb @(posedge clk);
input 1 output negedge 2;
input 3 din;
output 3 dout;
input 3 output 2 we;
input 3 output 3 ce = top.ce;
sequence my_seq;
we 1 (dout==0);
endsequence
property my_prop;
my_seq;
endproperty
endclocking;

modport mst (input dout, output din, addr, ce, we, clocking cb);
modport slv (input din, addr, ce, we, output dout, clocking cb);

In example.v above, "cb" is an object with "clocking block" (npiClockingBlock).
And "din", "dout", "we", and "ce" are objects with type "clocking io
decl" (npiClockingIODecl).
For a given clocking block object "cb",
* Applying method "npiClockingIODecl" returns four clocking io decl objects, named
"din", "dout", "we", and "ce".
* Applying method "npiClockingEvent" returns the event control object "@(posedge
clk)".
Methods "npiInputSkew" and "npiOutputSkew", and properties "npiInputEdge" and
"npiOutputEdge", on the clocking block apply to the default constructs.
* Applying methods "npiInputSkew" and "npiOutputSkew" returns delay control objects
"#1" and "#2", respectively.
Properties "npiInputEdge" and "npiOutputEdge" returns 0 (npiNoEdge) and 50
(npiNegedge), respectively.
* Applying method "npiSequenceDecl" returns sequence declaration "my_seq" whose
object type is npiSequenceDecl.
* Applying method "npiPropertyDecl" returns property declaration "my_prop" whose
object type is npiPropertyDecl.
For a given clocking io decl object "we",
Methods "npiInputSkew" and "npiOutputSkew", and properties "npiInputEdge" and
"npiOutputEdge" on the clocking io decl apply to the clocking io decl itself.
* Applying methods "npiInputSkew" and "npiOutputSkew" returns delay control objects
"#3" and "#2", respectively.
Properties "npiInputEdge" and "npiOutputEdge" returns 0 (npiNoEdge).

* npiClockingBlock returns the clocking objects that belong to the given instance
* npiClockingIODecl returns the clocking io decl objects that belong to the given
clocking block object.

* The methods, npiInputSkew and npiOutputSkew, and properties npiInputEdge
and npiOutputEdge, on the clocking block apply to the default constructs. The same
methods and properties on the clocking io decl apply to the clocking io decl itself.
* npiExpr returns the expression or ref obj referenced by the clocking io decl.
Consider input ce = top.ce. Here, "ce" is represented by a clocking io decl, and the
npiExpr relation returns a handle to "top.ce".
* Method "npiSequenceDecl" iterates all sequence declarations of the given clocking
block. And method "npiPropertyDecl" iterates all property declarations of the given
clocking block.

npiClockingBlock

Constraint
SystemVerilog allows users to specify constraints to automatically generate tests for
functional verification. A constraint block contains some expressions, that is denoted as
constraint item in NPI and used to specify limitation of random variables.
The constraint item can be bracketed into two categories: constraint ordering and
constraint expr.
The constraint expris a class that contains implication, constr if, constr if else, constr
foreach, and an expression class composed by distribution and general expression
class.

title: 05 endmodule
05 endmodule
05 endmodule
text:
In the aforementioned example, the class "CLS_EXT" contains one constraint object named
"proto", that can be obtained by the npiConstraint iteration.
"proto" is an external constraint block that means the constraint is declared outside its
enclosing class declaration when its constraint prototype appears in the enclosing class
declaration.
The npiExtern property of "proto" is 1 and the npiExternLineNo and npiExternFile
property returns the location of its external declaration. Applying npiConstraintItem
iteration on "proto" returns a constraint expression "x >= 0".
The constraint "C1" contains two constraint expression, both are implication
(npiImplication). Applying npiCondition relation on an implication expression returns the
expression before the syntax "->".
In addition, the npiConstraintExpr iteration returns the constraint expressions after the
syntax "->".
The constraint "C2" and "C3" contains a constr if expression (npiConstrIf) and constraint
ordering (npiConstraintOrdering), respectively.
For the constraint ordering "solve s before d", npiSolveBefore iteration returns the
expression "s" and npiSolveAfter iteration returns the expression "d".
The constraint "C4" contains a constr foreach (npiConstrForeach). Applying npiVariables
relation on this constr foreach, the array "A" is returned.
The loop variable "i" can be obtained by the npiLoopVars iteration from the constr
foreach.

title: 05 endmodule
text:
* For a constraint, npiExtern property shows whether it is an external constraint block or
not.
If a constraint is an external constraint block, that means the constraint is declared
outside its enclosing class declaration. Then npiExternLineNo and npiExternFile
property returns location of the external constraint.
* For a constraint, npiAutomatic property does not mean lifetime, but reflects the
keyword used in constraint declaration. npiAutomatic==0 implies the constraint was
declared static.
* An abstract class that is declared using the syntax "virtual class" might contain
pure constraints. A pure constraint represents an obligation on any non-abstract
derived class to provide a constraint of the same name. npiVirtual property determines
if the constraint is virtual.
* The npiConstraint iteration returns the constraints in syntactic declaration order.
The position within this order of a constraint declared as "extern" is determined by the
position of its prototype.
* The npiConstraintItem iteration returns the constraint items in the order in which they
occur within the constraint.
Constraint Items contains two kinds of objects, constraint ordering
(npiConstraintOrdering) and constraint expression.
* For a constraint ordering object declared using the "solve before" syntax,
the npiSolveBefore iteration returns the expressions between the "solve" keyword and
the "before" keyword, and the npiSolveAfter iteration returns the expressions after
the "before" keyword.
* The constraint expression class contains six kinds of object types as follows:
Implication (npiImplication).
Constr if (npiConstrIf)
Constr if else (npiConstrIfElse)
Constr foreach (npiConstrForeach)
Distribution (npiDistribution)
General expression class.
* Constraints provide two constructs for declaring conditional relations such as
implication and if-else. For an implication, constr if, or constr if else expression,
npiCondition relation returns the predicated expression.

* Each npiConstraintExpr iteration returns the expressions in the order in which they
occur in the containing implication, constr if, constr if-else, or constr foreach.
* For a constr if else expression, npiElseConst iteration returns the expressions in the
order in which they occur in the else condition block.
* The variable obtained through the npiVariables relation from a npiConstrForeach
represents the array being indexed.
* The npiLoopVars iteration returns the index variables of the constr foreach in left-toright order.

npiConstraintOrdering
npiImplication
npiConstrIf
npiConstrIfElse
npiConstrForeach

Continuous Assignment
Continuous assignments drive values onto nets or variables, both vector (packed) and
scalar.
"cont assign" belongs to the class "use".

wire w;
wire w3 = 1; /* Net declaration assign */
reg a, b, select;
assign 5 w = select ? b : a; /* continuous assignment */

In the example code above, the net declaration assign "wire w3 = 1" implies a continuous
assignment "assign w3 = 1" whose npiNetDeclAssign property is "1" (TRUE).
For the continuous assignment "assign #5 w = select ? b : a", the npiDelay of is the
expression "5". The npiLhs of the continuous assignment is the simple expression "w", and
the npiRhs of the continuous assignment is expression "select ? b : a".

N/A

Covergroup
The coverage group (covergroup) construct encapsulates the specification of a coverage
model. Each covergroup specification can include the following components:
* A set of coverage points (cover point).
* Cross coverage between coverage points (cover cross).
* Coverage options (coverage option).
A covergroup can be defined in a package, module, program, interface, or class.
A cover point specifies an integral expression that is to be covered. Each cover point
includes a set of bins associated with the sample values or value transitions of the
covered expression.
A cover cross can be specified between two or more cover point objects or variables.
Any combination of more than two variables or previously declared coverage points is
allowed.
SystemVerilog implicitly creates a cover point for the variable defined by a cover cross
A coverage option controls the behavior of the covergroup, coverpoint, and cross. A
covergroup object can specify one or more coverage option objects.

module mod;
wire clk;
enum { red, green, blue } color;
bit [3:0] pixel_adr, pixel_offset, pixel_hue;
covergroup cv (ref int ra, input int low, int high) @(posedge clk); /*
covergroup */
option.at_least = low; /* coverage option */

Hue: coverpoint pixel_hue; /* cover point */
Offset: coverpoint pixel_offset; /* cover point */
AxC: cross color, pixel_adr; /* cover cross, cover point */
all: cross color, Hue, Offset; /* cover cross, cover point */
coverpoint ra { /* cover point */
bins good = { [low : high] };
bins bad[] = default;
}
endgroup

In the aforementioned example, the coverage group "cv" is declared inside the module
"mod" so the npiCovergroup object "cv" can be retrieved from "mod" by applying the
method npiCovergroup.
The coverage group "cv" includes one coverage option (npiCoverageOption), three
coverage points (npiCoverPoint), and two cross coverage items (npiCoverCross).
According to the syntax, explicit coverage points labeled "Hue" and "Offset" are defined for
variables pixel_hueand "pixel_offset", and an implicit coverage point is defined for "ra".
Besides, SystemVerilog implicitly declares coverage points for variables "color" and
"pixel_adr" since the variables are defined in cross coverage items "AxC" and "all".
Therefore, five npiCoverPoint objects are returned by the 1-n method npiCoverPoint:
"Hue", "Offset", "ra", "color", and "pixel_adr". Two npiCoverCross objects are returned by
the 1-n method npiCoverCross: "AxC" and "all".
There is one coverage option specified to control the coverage data by the syntax
"option.at_least = low;".

the 1-n method npiCoverCross: "AxC" and "all".
There is one coverage option specified to control the coverage data by the syntax
"option.at_least = low;".
The option named "at_least" can be retrieved by the 1-n method npiCoverageOption from
the coverage group. Since the coverage option is defined as "option.member_identifier",
the property npiCovoptType returns npiOptionCovopt.
Apply the 1-n method npiBins on the coverage points "ra", two bins objects are returned.
The bins object can be specified by keywords bins, ignore_bins, or illegal_bins. In the
example, the bins objects are declared by keyword "bins" so the property npiBinsType
returns npiNormalBins.
The 1-1 method npiBinsSpec is used to retrieve the definition expression for coverage
bins, for example, a range operation "[low : high]" is returned for the npiBins object "bins
good = { [low : high] };".

* Coverage groups can be retrieved from instance handles by the 1-n method
npiCovergroup.
* For a coverage group, the 1-n methods npiCoverageOption returns the coverage
options declared inside the coverage group.
The 1-n methods npiCoverPoint and npiCoverCross returns the coverage point and
cover cross objects, respectively.
The 1-n method npiCoverageEvent is used to retrieve coverage events. The coverage
event is expression, event control, or events.
* For a coverage option, the property npiCovoptType describes member type. If
the coverage option is declared as option.member_identifier, the property returns
npiOptionCovopt.
If the coverage option is declared as type_option.member_identifier, the property
returns npiTypeOptCovopt. Otherwise, it returns npiIllegalCovopt.
* The class "coverage spec" (npiCoverageSpec) contains two object types: coverage
point (npiCoverPoint) and cover cross (npiCoverCross).
For a coverage point, the 1-1 method npiExpr and npiIff are used to retrieve coverpoint
expression and iff expression, respectively.
The 1-n method npiBins returns bins objects if there exists any bins object inside the
coverage point. For a cover cross, the 1-1 method npiIff can retrieve the iff expression
and the 1-n method npiCorssItems returns cross item objects. The cross items could
be coverage points or variables.
* For a bins object, the property npiBinsType is npiNormalBins, npiIgnoreBins, or
npiIllegalBins according to different bins keywords.
If the bins keyword is illegal_bins or ignore_bins, the property returns npiIllegalBins or
npiIgnoreBins, respectively. Otherwise, it returns npiNormalBins.
The bins construct allows creating a separate bin for each value in the given range list
or a single bin for the entire range of values, the 1-1 method npiBinsSpec returns an
expression described the range of variables.

In the NPI Language model, port objects provide a means of interconnecting a hardware
description. Port is a general object type for both SystemVerilog and VHDL.
For describing the connection relation, SystemVerilog port (located at SystemVerilog
instance) uses the method npiHighConn and npiLowConn, and VHDL port (located at
VHDL instance) uses the method npiVhMapElem.

(* dont_touch = "1", is_top = "no", x_cnt = 3 *)
(* second_attr = 1 *) /* above items are def attributes of instance
"top.x0" */
module xxx (
(* iso=1 *) input foo, /* port "foo" has an attribute named "iso" with
int value 1 */
(* iso=0 *) output bar /* port "bar" has an attribute named "iso" with
int value 0 */
);
(* iso=1 *) wire foo_iso; /* net "foo_iso" has an attribute named "iso"
with int value 1 */
(* iso=0 *) wire bar_iso; /* net "bar_iso" has an attribute named "iso"
with int value 0 */
(* is_top, float_test = 2.5 *) /* def attributes of instance "top" */
(* inst_attr *) /* attribute of instance "top.x0" */
xxx x0(a, b);

In the aforementioned example, the module instance "top.x0" acquires five attribute
handles by applying npiAttribute method.
The npiName property of these handles corresponds to the following attribute names:
* inst_attr
* dont_touch
* is_top
* x_cnt
* second_attr
Among these, the last four attributes (dont_touch, is_top, x_cnt, and second_attr)
originate from the module definition.
Consequently, querying the npiDefAttribute property for these handles returns a value of
1.
Each attribute handle provides access to its name via the npiName property and its value
through the npi_get_value() method. Additionally, the npiConstType property indicates
the data type of the attribute value.

Delay Control
"Delay control" belongs to the class "atomic statement".

reg reset, r1;
/* process always */
/* delay control statement*/
begin: BLK
/* scope: named begin */
if(reset)
r1 = 0;
r1 = 1 1;
end

In the example code above, for the delay control statement, applying npi_handle(npiDelay,
delay_ctrl_handle) returns expression "100". Applying npi_handle(npiStmt,
delay_ctrl_handle) returns the named begin scope "BLK".

For delay control associated with assignment, the statement is always NULL.

Refer to the npiDelayControl section in the Language Model - Complete Supported List

disable blk_n; /* disable */
end

In the example code above, for the disable statement, applying npi_handle(npiExpr,

Distribution, Dist Item
A distribution (npiDistribution) is a set of weighted value. The distribution set is a commaseparated list of integral expressions and ranges.
Each term in the list is named dist item (npiDistItem). Optionally, each dist item can have
a weight, which is specified using the ":=" (npiEqualDist) or ":/" (npiDivDist) operators.

class CLS_DIST;
rand int x, y, z;
constraint CX {
x dist { 100 := 1, 200 := 2, 300 := 5 }; /* distribution with
three dist items, each dist item contains range value and weight with
npiEqualDist type */
}
constraint CY {
y dist { [100:102] :/ 1, 200 := 2, 300 := 5 }; /* distribution with
three dist items, each dist item contains range value and weight. Range
[100:102] uses npiDivDist operator, the rest items use npiEqualDist
}
constraint CZ {
z dist { 100, 200, 300 }; /* distribution with three dist items. No
weight is specified so each dist item uses default weight ":=1" */
}

In the aforementioned example, "y dist { [100:102] :/ 1, 200 := 2, 300 := 5}" is a distribution
expression (npiDistribution) with an integral expression "y" and three dist items. Each
dist item (npiDistItem) contains a range value and a weight.
For example, the first dist item "[100:102]:/ 1" is constructed by a range value "[100:102]"
and a weight "1" that is specified by a divided operator ":/" (npiDivDist).
The rest two dist items contain weight value that are specified by equal operators
"=/" (npiEqualDist).
When no weight is specified for dist item, default weight ":=1" is used and the property
npiDistType returns "-1".

1. The npiDistType property of a dist item (npiDistItem) returns npiEqualDist,
npiDivDist, or npiUndefined. npiEqualDist implies the weight is specified by equal
operator ":=1". npiDivDist implies the weight is specified by a divided operator ":/".
If no weight is specified, npiDistType is npiUndefined.
2. The npiWeight method of a dist item (npiDistItem) returns a weight expression. If no
weight is specified, npiWeight returns NULL.

Refer to the npiDistType section in the Language Model - List of All Return Types section

"Do while" belongs to the class "atomic statement".

do
// do while statement
begin : fff
x = x - 1;
if (x > 5) begin
end
end
while (x > 0);
return x + 10;
end

In the example code above, for the do-while statement, applying npi_handle(npiCondition,
dowhile_handle) returns the expression "x > 0". Applying npi_handle(npiStmt,
dowhile_handle) returns the named scope "fff".

N/A

Foreach Stmt
"Foreach" belongs to the class "scope".

int prod [1:8] [1:3];
initial begin:INIT
foreach(prod[x,]) /* npiForeachStmt */
prod[x] = {0, 0, 0};
end

In example.v, for the foreach stmt, applying one-to-one method npiVariables obtains
npiArrayVar "top.prod", and applying one-to-many method npiLoopVars obtains
npiIntVar "x" whose scope is foreach stmt and npiOperation whose npiOpType is
npiNullOp.

* The variable obtained through the npiVariables relation from a foreach stmt represents
packed array, unpacked array, or string var being indexed.
* The npiLoopVars iteration returns the index variables of the foreach stmt in left-to-right
order.
If an index variable is skipped, its place is represented as a npiOperation for which the
npiOpType is npiNullOp.
* The scope of each loop control variable in a foreach stmt is the foreach stmt.

Refer to the npiForeachStmt section in the Language Model - Complete Supported List

Event Control
The execution of a procedural statement that is synchronized with a value change on a net
or variable or the occurrence of a declared event is treated as an event control object in
NPI Language model.

reg clk, reset, r1;
always @(posedge clk or negedge reset) /* event control */
begin: BLK
if(!reset)
r1 = 0;
r1 = 1 1;
end

In the example code above, the npiCondition transition for event control statement returns
an operation object (npiOperation) that represents "posedge clk or negedge reset", while
the npiStmt transition returns the named begin object (npiNamedBegin) named "BLK".

N/A

Refer to the npiEventControl section in the Language Model - Complete Supported List

Rhs: npiOperation with op-type npiConcatOp; TD'{0, 1}:
npiOperation with op-type npiAssignmentPatternExprOp */
TD t2 [1:0] = {TD'{0, 1}, TD'{default:0}};
mm m0(r[0]);
r[1:0] /* part select */ = 0; /* assignment */
r[2-:3] /* indexed part select */ = 0; /* assignment */
r[p-:4] /* indexed part select */ = 0; /* assignment */
if (r[0] == 0/* operation with npiOpType: npiEqOp */)
r[3] = 0;
end

In the example code above, part-select "top.r[1:0]" (size is equal to 2) gets constant "1"
and "0" by applying method npiLeftRange and npiRightRange, respectively, and gets bitvar "top.r" by applying method npiParent.
Similarly, indexed-part-select "top.r[2-:3]" (size is equal to 3) gets constant "2" and "3" by
applying method npiBaseExpr and npiWidthExpr, respectively, and gets bit-var "top.r" by
applying method npiParent.
Besides, the default expression of t0, t1 and t2 are operations with npiOpType:
npiAssignmentPatternOp, npiMultiAssignmentPatternOp and npiConcatOp respectively.
For t0's default expression, applying 1-to-many method npiOperand gets two npiConcatOp
operations.
For t1's default expression, applying 1-to-many method npiOperand get a npiConstant 2
and a npiAssignmentPatternOp operation. For t2's default expression, applying 1-to-many
method npiOperand gets two npiAssignmentPatternExprOp operations.
npiAssignmentPatternExprOp operation TD'{default:0} get a npiBitTypespec named "TD"
and a npiAssignmentPatternOp operation by applying 1-to-many method npiOperand.

* For an operator whose type is npiMultiConcatOp, the first operand is the multiplier
expression. The remaining operands are the expressions within the concatenation.
* The cast operation, for which npiOpType returns npiTypeCastOp, npiSigningCastOp,
npiSizeCastOp or npiConstCastOp, is represented as a unary operation, with its sole
argument being the expression being cast.
Only for cast operation of npiTypeCastOp, it can obtain the typespec of the cast
expression being the type to which the argument is being cast.

In the following example, the first RHS operation's npiOptype is npiTypeCastOp so it
can get the typespec by applying npiTypespec.
The second RHS operation's npiOptype is npiSigningCastOp, and its signed property
returns 1. The third RHS operation's npiOptype is npiSizeCastOp, and its size property
returns 8. The last RHS operation's npiOptype is npiConstCastOp.
int cast_int = int'(2.0 * 3.0);
integer cast_signed = signed'(2'b11);
byte cast_size = 8'(1234);
logic [31:0] cast_const = const'(cast_int);

* The operation with npiOpType: npiAssignmentPatternOp could get expr, typespec or
pattern item by applying 1-to-many method npiOperand. This is discussed in detail in
the section "pattern item".
* For a part-select or indexed part-select, the npiParent object is correspond to the
expression formed by removing the part-select range from the expression represented
by the part-select or indexed part-select itself.
For example, given the following declaration:
logic [0:3][7:0] r [1:4];

The parents of various part-selects or indexed part-selects is as shown in the following
table:
part-select or indexed part-select
expression

parent expression

r[4][3][1:0]

r[4][3]

r[i+1][3][j+:2]

r[i+1][3]

r[0][j-:4]

r[0]

r[0:2]

r

* npiSize for part select or indexed part select always returns the number of the flatten
bits. For example, a is declared as below, and npiSize of a[1:0] is 16.
reg [7:0] a [7:0];

* npiSize for constant whose npiConstType property is npiNullConst always returns -1
(npiUndefined).

* For an operation, npi_get_value() gets the value of calculation if:
its npiOpType is not npiAssignmentPatternOp, npiMultiAssignmentPatternOp,
npiAssignmentPatternExprOp or npiListOp.
all its operands can get the value by npi_get_value().
* For npiTypeCastOp and npiAssignmentPatternExprOp, if the cast type is type operator
(example as follows), the size and signed property should be -1.
int i1 = type(ia+ib)'{default:0}; // size and signed of this operation
should be -1

(example as follow), the size and signed property should be -1. (unsupported now)
int i1 = type(ia+ib)'{default:0}; // size and signed of this operation should be -1

For
"For" belongs to the class "atomic statement" and "scope".

parameter int SIZE = 256;
integer index=0;
function myfunc;
for(index=0; index<SIZE; index=index+1) /* for statement */
begin: ggg
$display("aaa");
end
myfunc = 1;

In the example code above, for the for statement, applying npi_iterate(npiForInitStmt,
for_handle), the atomic statement "index=0" is returned from the iterator.
Applying npi_iterate(npiForIncStmt, for_handle), the atomic statement "index=index+2" is
returned from the iterator. Applying npi_handle(npiCondition, for_handle), the expression
"index < SIZE" is returned. Applying npi_handle(npiStmt, for_handle), the named begin
scope "ggg" is returned.

N/A

forever CYCLE clk = ~clk;

. A generate block is a collection of one or more module items.

"Generate scope" belongs to the class "scope".

parameter p = 4;
wire [7:0] a;
wire [7:0] aa;
if(p > 0)
begin: B
/* gen scope, top.B */
and u0 (a[0], a[1],b);
end
for (i=0; i<p; i=i+1)
begin: BB /* gen scope, top.BB[0] ~ top.BB[3] */
assign a[i] = ^a[p-1:i];
end
for (i=0; i<p; i=i+1)
begin /* unamed gen scope, top.gblk1[0] ~ top.gblk1[3] */
assign aa[i] = ^aa[p-1:i];

end

In the example code above, for the first generate description, the gen scope "top.B" is
generated. For the second generate description, four gen scopes, "top.BB[0]", "top.BB[1]",
"top.BB[2]", and "top.BB[3]" are generated.
For the third generate description, four unnamed gen scope, "top.gblk1[0]", "top.gblk1[1]",
"top.gblk1[2]", and "top.gblk1[3]" are generated. Refer SystemVerilog LRM Chapter 27.for
details of the unnamed gen scope.
The property npiArrayMember for the gen scope "top.B" is "0" (FALSE). The property
npiArrayMember for the gen scope "top.BB[0]", "top.BB[1]", "top.BB[2]" and "top.BB[3]" is
"1" (TRUE).
The property npiArrayMember for the gen scope "top.gblk1[0]", "top.gblk1[1]",
"top.gblk1[2]" and "top.gblk1[3]" is "1" (TRUE).
The property npiImplicitDecl for the gen scope "top.B" is "0" (FALSE). The property
npiImplicitDecl for the gen scope "top.BB[0]", "top.BB[1]", "top.BB[2]" and "top.BB[3]" is
"0" (FALSE). The property npiImplicitDecl for the gen scope "top.gblk1[0]", "top.gblk1[1]",
"top.gblk1[2]" and "top.gblk1[3]" is "1" (TRUE).

1. For an unnamed generate, an implicit scope is created. Its npiImplicitDecl property
returns TRUE.
2. References to gen vars within the gen scope is treated as local parameters.
3. Parameters within the gen scope must be local parameters.

If, If-else
"If" (npiIf) and "If-else" (npiIfElse) belong to the class "atomic statement".

reg a, b, x, y, z;
if( a & b ) /* if statement */
x = y;
if( a | b ) /* if-else statement */
x = ~y;
x = z;
end

In the example code above, for the if-else statement, applying npi_handle(npiCondition,
ifelse_handle) returns the expression "a|b". Applying npi_handle(npiStmt, ifelse_handle)
returns the atomic statement "x = ~y".
Applying npi_handle(npiElseStmt, ifelse_handle) returns the atomic statement "x = z".

An optional qualifier, automatic or static, is used to specify the default lifetime of all
variables declared in a task, function, or block defined within a module, interface, package,
or program. The default lifetime is static.

* The npiTypedef iteration returns the user-defined typespecs that have typedefs
explicitly declared in the instance.
* The npiInstance always returns the immediate instance (package, module, or interface)
in which the object is instantiated.
* Imported items are not accessible through npi_handle_by_name().
* The propertynpiContainProtect returns 1 if any protected code (embraced by protect
and endprotect) is written inside the definition (could be module/interface/package) of
the instance. Otherwise, it returns 0.
* The property npiBind returns 1 if the instance is created by "bind" statement.

* The property npiLibraryName returns the working library name for the instance. If the
design that declares this instance is not imported from working library, the return string
is NULL.
* The property npiDefLibraryName returns the working library name for the definition of
instance. If the design that declares this definition is not imported from working library,
the return string is NULL.
* For a package object, the property npiIsRoot is used to identify if a package object is
root or a general package. If the returned value is 1, the package object is root. Else,
the object is a general package.

Instance Arrays
The instantiations of modules/interfaces/primitives/programs can contain a range
specification. This allows an array of instances to be created.
In the NPI Language model, there are five kinds of instances array objects - module array,
interface array, gate array, switch array and UDP array.
The later three instance array objects belong to the class "primitive array".

module top; /* module */
mm u1 /* module */(w1, w2[0]);
mm u2[3:0] /* module array */ (w1, w2);
initial begin : INIT_BLK

end

In the example code above, "top.u2" is an object with type "module
array" (npiModuleArray).
Applying method "npiExpr" to the handle "top.u2", an operation handle (npiOperation) with
two operands w1, w2 is returned (operands w1 and w2 are the objects with type npiNet
and npiArrayNet, separately).
Applying method "npiRange" to the handle "top.u2", an iterator handle that contains
one range object (npiRange) is returned. Applying methods "npiLeftRange" and
"npiRightRange" to the range object, constant handles (npiConstant) "3" and "0" is
returned, separately.

* Traversing from the instance array to expr returns a simple expression object of type
npiOperation with a npiOpType of npiListOp. This expression is used to access the
actual list of connections to the instance array in the SystemVerilog source code.
* npiIterator(npiRange, instance_array_handle) returns the set of instance array ranges
beginning with the left-most range of the array declaration and iterating through the
right-most range. Using the npiLeftRange/npiRightRange properties returns the bounds
of the left-most dimension of a multidimensional array.
* The property npiContainBlackBox identifies if an interface array or a module array
contains at least one black box that is set by ZeBu synthesis command.

In the example code above, "input [7:0] data", "output [7:0] result", and "ref int cnt" are
objects with type "IO declaration" (npiIODecl).
Applying method "npiExpr" to the first IO declaration of task "convert" (npiTask) returns a
reg var (npiReg) named "data".
Applying method "npiExpr" to the second IO declaration of task "convert" (npiTask) returns
a reg var (npiReg) named "result".
Applying method "npiExpr" to IO declaration of task "counter" (npiTask) returns a ref obj
named "cnt".

* npiDirection returns npiRef for pass by ref ports or arguments.
* A ref obj type handle might be returned for the npiExpr of an io decl if it is passed by
reference or if the io decl is an interface or a modport.
* If the npiExpr of an io decl is a ref objand if the npiActual of the ref obj is an interface or
modport declaration, then the npiDirection of the io decl is undefined.
* For npiDirection, available value includes npiInput, npiOutput, npiInout, and npiRef.
* If the io decl is an importing or exporting of tasks and functions from modport, its
npiExpr is a npiNIY object (NPI doesn't support it currently).
* Similar to item 5, if the io decl is a clocking block from modport, its npiExpr is a npiNIY
object (NPI doesn't support it currently).
