Variable
A variable is an abstraction of a data storage element that is written by one or more
procedural statements.
In the NPI Language model, variables are packed or unpacked aggregates of other types,
as shown in the following diagram.

example1.v
reg w1 [3:0]; /*array var*/
reg [7:0] w2 [3:0][63:0]; /*array var*/
reg [7:0] w3 = 8'hff; /*reg */
always @ (posedge clk) begin

* Any variable declared as an array with one or more unpacked ranges is an array var.
* The Boolean property npiArrayMember is TRUE if the referenced variable is a member
of an array variable. It is FALSE otherwise.
* For an array var, npi_iterate (npiRange, handle) returns the set of array range
declarations beginning with the left-most unpacked range and iterating through the
right-most unpacked range.
If any dimension of the unpacked array other than the first dimension is a dynamic
array, associative array, or queue dimension, the iteration returns an empty range (see
Object Range) for that dimension.
For a packed array, the iteration returns the set of ranges beginning with the left-most
packed range and iterating through the right-most packed range.
The ranges returned for a packed array does not include the implicit range for packed
struct or union var elements themselves, or the range (explicit or implicit) for the base
type of enum var elements.
* npi_iterate(npiIndex, var_select_handle) returns the set of indices for a var select in a
multidimensional array, starting with the index for the var select and working outward.
* A var select is an element selected from an array var.
* If the variable has an initialization expression, the expression is obtained from
npi_handle(npiExpr, var_handle).
* npiSize for a variable array returns the number of variables in the array. For variables
belonging to an integer data type, for enum vars, and for packed struct and union
variables, npiSize returns the size of the variable in bits.
For unpacked structures and unions, the size returned indicates the number of fields
in the structure or union. For a var bit, npiSize returns 1. For all other variables, the
behavior of the npiSize property is not defined.
* Variables of type npiArrayVar do not have a value property.
* npi_iterate(npiIndex, var_bit_handle) returns the set of indices for a multidimensional
variable bit select, starting with the index for the bit and working outwards.
* When the npiStructUnionMember property is TRUE, it indicates that the variable is a
member of a parent struct or union variable.
See also the relations in LRM Structures and Unions and Packed Array Variables

* If a variable is an element of an array (the npiArrayMember property is TRUE), the
npiIndex iterator returns the indexing expressions that select that specific variable out
of the array.
See Packed Array Variables for similar functionality available for elements of packed
array vars.
* Logic var, var bit, and reg array in SystemVerilog LRM are not shown in the
aforementioned diagram, in NPI SV model, these objects are defined as follows:
logic var == reg
var bit == reg bit
reg array == array var

* npiArrayType is one of npiStaticArray, npiDynamicArray, npiAssocArray, or npiQueue.
* npiRandType can be one of npiRand, npiRandC, or npiNotRand.
* For details on lifetime and memory allocation properties, see Lifetimes of Objects.
* npiVisibility denotes the visibility (local, protected, or default) of a variable that is a
class member. npiVisibility returns npiPublicVis for a class member that is not local or
protected, or for a variable that is not a class member.
* The npiParent transition is allowed on all variable objects. It returns one of the types
of objects listed below, representing one of its prefix objects (similar to the field select
prefix or indexing select prefix), or NULL, depending on whether certain criteria are
met.
For purposes of defining npiParent, a prefix object is the object obtained from
successively removing the right-most index or identifier from a compound or indexed/
multidimensional object name (excluding scope identifiers).
Consider the following npiArrayVar objects:
logic [1:0][2:3] mda [4:6][6:8];
struct { int i1; bit [1:0][2:3]bvec[4:5]; } spa [9:11][12:13];

mda[6][8][1][3] is a npiVarBit, mda[6][8][1] is its first prefix object (a 2-bit npiLogicVar
vector), and mda[6][8] is its second prefix object (a 2 x 2 npiLogicVar packed array),
and so on.
The spa[9][12].bvec[4] object is a npiBitVar (a 2 x 2 npiBitVar packed array), and spa[9]
[12].bvec is its first prefix object (a npiArrayVar struct member), and spa[9][12] is the
second prefix object (the npiStructVar containing the bvec member) and so on.

For a variable object with prefix objects, the npiParent transition returns one of the
following prefix objects, whichever comes first in prefix order (right-most to left-most):
Struct, union, or class variable.
Struct or union member variable, or class variable data member.
The largest containing packed array object.
The largest containing unpacked array object.
If no prefix object exists, or the prefix object does not meet at least one of the
aforementioned criteria, npiParent returns NULL.
Using the declarations above, the npiParent of mda[6][8][1][3] is mda[6][8], the
npiLogicVar representing the largest containing packed array prefix; the npiParent of
mda[6][8] is mda, the npiArrayVar representing the largest containing unpacked array
prefix.
Likewise, the npiParent of spa[9][12].bvec[4][0] is spa[9][12].bvec[4] (the largest
containing packed array); the npiParent of spa[9][12].bvec[4] is spa[9][12].bvec (struct
member), and applying npiParent again yields spa[9][12], the struct variable for
member bvec.
The npiParent of spa[9][12] is spa, the largest containing unpacked array of the struct
variable; npiParent of spa (or mda) would return NULL.
* For consistency with other variable-width vector objects, the npiSize property for
npiPackedArrayVar objects are the number of bits in the packed array, not the number
of struct, enum, or union var elements.
The total number of struct var, enum var, or union var elements for a packed array
var is obtained by computing the product of the npiSize property for all of its packed
ranges.
* The npiPackedArrayMember property is TRUE for any struct var, union var, enum var,
or packed array var whose npiParent is a packed array var.
* The npiStructUnionMember property is TRUE only for packed array vars that are direct
members of struct or union vars, that is, whose npiParent is a struct or union var.
This property is FALSE for all sub elements (as returned by the npiElement iterator) of
such packed array vars.
* npi_iterate(npiIndex, packed_array_var_handle) returns the set of indices for a sub
element of a packed array variable (relative to its npiParent), starting with the index for
the sub element and working outwards.
The indices is retrieved in right-to-left order as they appear in the text.

Variable Select
In the NPI language model, a var select is an element selected from an array var.
More specifically, if there is a variable whose access dimension is less than the array's
unpacked dimension, the variable is a variable select object.

reg w1 [3:0];
reg [7:0] w2 [3:0][63:0];
reg [7:0] w3;
always @ (posedge clk) begin
w1[0] = w2[0][0][0];
w2[3] /*var select*/ = {64{w2[2][0]}};
w3[7] = w2[0][0][0];
end

In the example code above, "w2" is an object with type "array var" (npiArrayVar) whose
unpacked dimension is 2, "w2[3]" is an object with "var select" (npiVarSelect) whose
access dimension is 1.

Virtual Interface Var
A virtual interface variable denotes an interface instance.

In the preceding example,
interface PBus (parameter WIDTH=8); // A parameterized bus interface
logic req, grant;
logic [WIDTH-1:0] addr, data;

parameter tp = 35;
PBus (16) p16();
PBus (16) p16Arr [1:0] ();
PBus (32) p32();

virtual PBus v8; // legal declaration, but no legal assignments
virtual PBus (tp) v35; // legal declaration, but no legal assignments
virtual PBus (.WIDTH(16)) v16;
virtual PBus (.WIDTH(16)) v16Arr [1:0] = p16Arr;
virtual PBus (.WIDTH(16)) v16a = p16;
virtual PBus (16) v16b = v16a;
virtual PBus (16) v16c = p16Arr[0];
virtual PBus (16) v16d = v16Arr[0];
virtual PBus (16).phy v16_phy = p16.phy;
virtual PBus (32) v32;
virtual PBus (32).phy v32_phy;
virtual PBus v8Arr [1:0];
virtual PBus v8pArr [1:0];
virtual PBus.phy v8_phyArr [1:0];
v16 = p16; // legal parameter values match
v32 = p32; // legal parameter values match
v32_phy = p32; // legal assignment from no selected modport to selected
modport
end

While, Repeat
In the NPI Language model, while objects denote while-loop statement that execute a
statement until an expression becomes FALSE, while repeat objects denote repeat-loop
statements that execute a statement a fixed number of times.

integer a, b;
while ( a < b ) /* while statement*/
a = a + 1;
repeat (a) /*repeat statement*/
b = $random;
end

For the while statement shown above, npiCondition transition returns an operation object
(npiOperation) that represents "a < b", and npiStmt transition returns an assignment object
(npiAssignment) that represents "a = a + 1;".
For the repeat statement shown above, npiCondition transition returns a reg variable
(npiReg) named "a", and npiStmt transition returns an assignment object (npiAssignment)
that represents "b = $random;".

Vh Aggregate, Vh Elem Assoc
An aggregate is a basic operation that combines one or more values into a composite
value of a record or array type. An elem assoc is used to describe the relation of value
assigned for object.

constant OP_CODES1 : BIT_VECTOR(1 to 5) := "01001";
-- A string literal is assigned.
constant OP_CODES2 : BIT_VECTOR(1 to 5) := ('0', '1', '0', '0', '1');
-- Positional association is implicit;
-- first value is assigned to OP_CODES(0), second value to OP_CODES(1),
and so on.
constant OP_CODES3 : BIT_VECTOR(1 to 5) := (2=>'1', 5=>'1', others=>'0');
-- Named association;
-- second and fifth element of OP_CODES get the value '1', and
-- the rest get a value of '0'.
constant OP_CODES4 : BIT_VECTOR(1 to 5) := (others=>'0');
-- All values set to '0'.
constant OP_CODES5 : BIT_VECTOR(1 to 5) := (2 to 3=>'0', others =>'1');
-- second and third element of OP_CODES get the value '0',
-- the rest values set to '1'.
configuration ctop of top is -- configuration
for rt_body
end for;
end configuration ctop;

The property npiVhIsNamed indicates this element association is a positional association
or named association.

For positional association, the npiVhChoices gets no handle from npiVhElemAssoc.

Vh Block
The vh block is a concurrent statement, and it is used to limit the scope of declarations
and disable signal drivers by applying guard signals.

-- npiVhBlock (label name: bk)
-- with guarded expr: (cin = '1')
bk: block (cin = '1')
generic (bg: integer := 0);
generic map (bg => 5);
port (ba, bb: in std_logic; bo: out std_logic);
port map (ba => a(0), bb => a(1), bo => cout);
-- "bks" is assigned as '0' when the result of guard expression is true
bks <= guarded '0';
bo <= ba and bb after 5 ns;
end block bk;

In example.vhd, the block with a label name, "bk", contains a generic (bg), three ports (ba,
bb and bo) and one signal (bks).
A guard expression (cin = '1') is obtained from the block "bk". This guard expression
determines whether the assignment with keyword "guarded" works.

npiVhBlock

Vh Branch
The vh branch is derived from vh if and vh cases. The vh branch contains conditional
expressions and sub statements.

signal qta: integer := 0;
type WEEK_DAY is (MON, TUE, WED, THU, FRI, SAT, SUN);
procedure incr_proc (signal cnt: inout integer) is
-- npiVhIf => 4 branches under it
if cnt > 1 then
cnt <= cnt + 1;
elsif cnt = 0 then
cnt <= 0;
elsif cnt = 1 then
cnt <= 1;
cnt <= -1;
function check_week_day(signal day:WEEK_DAY) return integer is
-- npiVhCase => 4 branches under it
case day is
when MON => quota := 100;
when TUE to WED | FRI => quota := 50;
when SAT | SUN => quota := 500;
when others => quota := 75;

incr_proc(isig);
qta <= check_week_day(WED);

For vh if inside procedure "incr_proc", four branches is obtained when applying one-tomany method npiVhBranch. The first branch obtains "cnt > 1" for conditional expression
and obtain "cnt <= cnt + 1;" for sub-statement.
The second branch obtains "cnt = 0" for conditional expression and obtain "cnt <= 0;" for
sub-statement. The third branch obtains "cnt = 1" for conditional expression and obtain
"cnt <= 1;" for sub-statement.
The last branch obtains NULL for conditional expression and obtain "cnt <= -1;" for substatement. For vh case inside function "check_week_day", four branches is obtained
respectively when applying one-to-many method npiVhBranch.
The first branch obtains "MON" for conditional expression and obtain "quota := 100;"
for sub-statement. The second branch obtains "TUE to WED" and "FRI" for conditional
expression and obtain "quota := 50;" for sub-statement.
The third branch obtains "SAT" and "SUN" for conditional expression and obtain "quota :=
500;" for sub-statement. The last branch obtains NULL for conditional expression and
obtain "quota := 75;" for sub-statement.

x"00000000";

Vh Design Unit
Design unit includes entity, architecture body, package declaration, and package body.
Root and component are composed of entity and architecture body.
Entity decides the instance shape and input or output structure. Architecture body
decides the actual behavior of the instance. Package instance are composed of package
declaration and package body.

The objects declared in the package declaration is used by other design objects if they

lcv := lcvv(0) or flag;

lcv := lcv xor flag;
lcv := lcv xnor flag;
-- relational operator
if flag = '0' then
elsif flag /= '0' then
elsif flag < '0' then
elsif flag <= '0' then
elsif flag > '0' then
elsif flag >= '0' then
-- shift operator
lcbv := lcbv sll 2;
lcbv := lcbv srl 2;
lcbv := lcbv sla 2;
lcbv := lcbv sra 2;
lcbv := lcbv rol 2;
lcbv := lcbv ror 2;

cnt <= cnt + 0;

Vh Generate, Vh Index Var
In the NPI Language model, the vh generate contains generate-if and generate-for. Similar
to the gen-scope in the NPI Language SystemVerilog model, the vh generate is also a
flattened scope.
That is, the hierarchy shows the results of the scope tree according to the elaboration
result. The vh index var means the index number according to the generate-for condition.

component add32 -- duplicates entity port
end component add32;
-- npiVhGenerate (generate-for)
-- => 3 scopes is generated: gfor(0), gfor(1) and gfor(2)
gfadd: add32 port map(a, b, cin, sum, cout);
-- sum(I) => "I" is vh index var
gforCsa: cout <= cin or sum(I); end generate gfor;
-- npiVhGenerate (generate-if)
-- => 1 scope is generated: gif
giadd: add32 port map(a, b, cin, sum, cout);

Four vh generate scopes is generated under top: "gfor(0)", "gfor(1)", "gfor(2)" and "gif".
"gfor(0)", "gfor(1)" and "gfor(2)" are flattened by generate-for, and "gif" is flattened by
generate-if.
After flattening the generate scopes, the index generated by the condition is the vh index
var, for example, the index expression "I" of the indexed name "sum(I)" is a vh index var.

To distinguish between generate-for scopes and generate-if scopes, check whether an
index number embraced by parentheses is in the tail of the scope name.

Vh If, Vh Case
The vh if and vh case belong to a sequential statement. Their branches (including
condition and statement) is obtained by applying one-to-many method npiVhBranch.

signal qta: integer := 0;
type WEEK_DAY is (MON, TUE, WED, THU, FRI, SAT, SUN);
procedure incr_proc (signal cnt: inout integer) is
-- npiVhIf => 4 branches under it
if cnt > 1 then
cnt <= cnt + 1;
elsif cnt = 0 then
cnt <= 0;
elsif cnt = 1 then
cnt <= 1;
cnt <= -1;
function check_week_day(signal day:WEEK_DAY) return integer is

-- npiVhCase => 4 branches under it
case day is
when MON => quota := 100;
when TUE to WED | FRI => quota := 50;
when SAT | SUN => quota := 500;
when others => quota := 75;
incr_proc(isig);
qta <= check_week_day(WED);

For vh if inside procedure "incr_proc" and vh case inside function "check_week_day", four
branches is obtained when applying one-to-many method npiVhBranch.

Vh Loop
Loop statement is a class that contains three types of loops: for-loop, while-loop and
forever-loop.

process (a, b)

-- npiVhForLoop
fLoop: for loopCnt in 3 downto 0 loop
es: exit fLoop when a(loopCnt)='0';
-- npiVhWhileLoop
wLoop: while (b(0) /= '0') loop
next;
-- npiVhForeverLoop
feLoop: loop
if (a(1) = '0') then
exit;
elsif (a(1) = '1') then
nxs: next feLoop when a(2) = '1';
elsif (a(2) = '0') then
nus: null;

For vh for loop "fLoop", a vh index var "loopCnt" is obtained by applying one-to-one
method npiVhParam and a vh range "3 downto 0" is obtained by applying one-to-one
method npiVhConstraint. In addition, a vh exit "es" is obtained by applying one-to-many
method npiVhStmt.
For vh while loop "wLoop", a vh operation "b(0) /= '0'" is obtained by applying one-toone method npiVhCondExpr and a vh next is obtained by applying one-to-many method
npiVhStmt.
For vh forever loop "feLoop", a vh if is obtained by applying one-to-many method
npiVhStmt.

Vh Map Element
In the NPI Language VHDL model, the vh map element is used to describe the
interconnection relationship for port or generic.

-- Component adder0 has three npiPort: ea, eb, esum
-- => ea can get 5 map elements by 1-to-many method npiVhMapElem
adder0: add32 generic map(GNR0 => x"01010101",
GNR1 => x"10101010")
port map(ea(cv downto 16) => a(cv downto 16),

In example.vhd above, the port "ea" of "top.adder0" has five vh map elements for the port
connection relation. They are "ea(cv downto 16) => a(cv downto 16)", "ea(15 downto 3) =>
a(15 downto 3)", "ea(2 downto 2) => a(2 downto 2)", "ea(1) => '1'" and "ea(0) => a(0)".
For the generic connection relation, "top.adder0" obtains two vh map elements "GNR0 =>
x"01010101"" and "GNR1 => x"10101010"" by applying method npiVhGenericMap.
In each map element, the left side of "=>" is the formal part that is obtained by applying
method npiVhFormal, and the right-hand side of "=>" is the actual part that is obtained by
applying method npiVhActual.

The npiVhScope returns vh subp decl if the formal of this vh map elem is vh param or its
partial object.

constant pc: in std_logic_vector(1 downto 0);
variable pv: out std_logic_vector(3 downto 0)) is
-- pv(3), pc(0): npiVhIndexedName
pv(3) := pc(0);
-- pv(2 downto 0), pc(2 downto 0): npiVhSliceName

prcs: process (a, b)
-- px: npiVhVar

-- px(0), b(0): npiVhIndexedName
kkk: prcs.px(0) := b(0) and c(0) and tg(0) and pa(0);
elsif a(1) = '0' then

Vh Scope
In the NPI Language VHDL model, scope is a class that contains several objects,
including vh block (npiVhBlock) and vh generate (npiVhGenerate).
Scope also contains two classes "vh instance" and "vh subprogram".

package test_pack is
procedure incr_proc (signal cnt: inout integer);
function get_quotient_func(signal dividend: integer; signal divisor:
integer) return integer;
package body test_pack is
-- npiVhProcedure
procedure incr_proc (signal cnt: inout integer) is
cnt <= cnt + 1;
-- npiVhFunction
function get_quotient_func(signal dividend: integer; signal divisor:
integer) return integer is
return dividend/divisor;

-- npiVhBlock
bk: block
generic (bg: integer := 0);
generic map (bg => 5);
port (ba, bb: in std_logic; bo: out std_logic);
port map (ba => a(0), bb => a(1), bo => cout);
bo <= ba and bb after 5 ns;
end block bk;
-- npiVhComponent
adder0: add32 generic map(GNR0 => x"01010101",
GNR1 => x"10101010")
port map(ea(cv downto 16) => a(cv downto 16),
-- npiVhGenerate
gforadd: add32 port map(a, b, sum);

-- npiVhGenerate
gifadd: add32 port map(a, b, sum);

In example.vhd above, "top.adder0" is a vh component (npiVhComponent) that belongs
to vh instance. "top.bk" is a vh block. "top.gfor(0)", "top.gfor(1)", "top.gfor(2)" and "top.gif"
are all vh generate (npiVhGenerate). "test_pack.incr_proc" is a vh procedure, and
"test_pack.get_quotient_func" is a vh function.
Both of these belong to vh subprogram.

In mixed language designs, if a different language sub-scope is under this scope, vh
scope can obtain the language interface when applying method npiVhInternalScope.
Language interface is a boundary for different languages.

Vh Signal Assignment
Signal assignment contains simple signal assignment, conditional signal assignment,
selected signal assignment, and sequential signal assignment.
The first three assignments belong to concurrent statement, and the last one belongs to
sequential statement.

ssa0: sum <= a or b;
ssa1: sum <= a or b after 1 ns;
csa0: sum <= a or b after 2 ns when cin = '0';
csa1: sum <= a after 3 ns when cin = '0' else
sesa0: with NEXT_STATE select

prcs: process (a, b, sum)
-- sequential signal assignment stmt
sqsa: sum <= a and b;

For a concurrent signal assignment, npiVhCondSigAssign is obtained when there
is a when-else reserved word condition. If there is a with-select reserved word in it,
npiVhSelectSigAssign is obtained. Otherwise, npiVhSimpleSigAssign is obtained.
The simple signal assignment "ssa1" obtains a vh waveform element "a or b after 1 ns" by
applying one-to-many method npiVhWaveform.
The conditional signal assignment "csa1" obtains one vh expression "NEXT_STATE"
by applying one-to-one method npiVhSelectExpr and three conditional waveforms by
applying one-to-many method npiVhWaveform.
These three waveforms are "a after 3 ns when cin = `0'", "b after 3 ns when cin = `1'"
and "a and b after 3 ns", and they can obtain their own waveform elements by applying
one-to-one method npiVhWaveformElem. The former two conditional waveforms can
obtain the conditional expressions "cin = `0'" and "cin = `1'" by applying one-to-one method
npiVhCondExpr.
The selected signal assignment "sesa0" obtains four selected waveforms by applying oneto-many method npiVhWaveform.
These four waveforms are "x"00000001" after 1 ns when APPLY | RECEIVE | KEEP",
"x"00000010" after 2 ns when WAITS | SLEEP", "x"00000100" after 3 ns when RESET"
and "unaffected when others", and they can obtain their own waveform elements by
applying one-to-one method npiVhWaveformElem.
For the first conditional waveform, three choice expressions "APPLY", "RECEIVE" and
"KEEP" is obtained by applying one-to-many method npiVhChoices.
The sequential signal assignment "sqsa" obtains a vh waveform element "a and b" by
applying one-to-many method npiVhWaveform.

Referring to the following example, if a signal assignment includes the reserved word
guarded, its property npiVhGuarded returns 1. Otherwise, it returns 0.
bo <= guarded ba and bb after 5 ns;

Vh Statement
Statements in VHDL contain sequential statements and concurrent statements.
Concurrent statements inside the architecture body describe the internal composition of
the entity.
Sequential statements are also named process statements, and they describe the
functionality of a portion of an entity in sequential terms.

The vh statement is a class of statements containing many objects. Refer to the individual
object introductions for examples.

The property npiVhSeqStmt returns -1 for a non-statement handle, return 0 for a
concurrent statement handle (vh conc stmt) and return 1 for a sequential statement handle
(vh seq stmt).

N/A

Vh Subprogram, Vh Subprogram Declaration
In the NPI Language model, the vh subprogram is a class that contains vh function and vh
procedure. The subprogram in the NPI VHDL model means the subprogram body, not the
declaration.
The subprogram declaration part is modeled as vh subp decl. Similarly, vh subp decl is
also a class that contains vh func decl and vh proc decl.

package PP is

type WEEK_DAY is (MON, TUE, WED, THU, FRI, SAT, SUN);
-- subprogram declaration (vh func decl)
function funcA (d1, d2, d3:WEEK_DAY) return integer;
end PP;
package body PP is
-- subprogram body (vh func body)
function funcA (d1, d2, d3:WEEK_DAY) return integer is
end PP;
use work.PP.all;
-- subprogram declarations
procedure procA (P1: in WEEK_DAY; P2:WEEK_DAY; P3: out WEEK_DAY; P4:
inout WEEK_DAY);
impure function funcB (d1: in WEEK_DAY) return integer;
-- subprogram declarations without bodies
procedure procDeclOnly (DP: in WEEK_DAY);
pure function funcDeclOnly (DD: in WEEK_DAY) return integer;
-- subprogram bodies (vh procedures and vh functions)
procedure incr_proc (signal I1:WEEK_DAY; variable I2:WEEK_DAY; constant
I3:WEEK_DAY) is
procedure procA (P1: in WEEK_DAY; P2:WEEK_DAY; P3: out WEEK_DAY; P4:
inout WEEK_DAY) is
impure function funcB (d1: in WEEK_DAY) return integer is
function check_week_day(signal day, day2, day3:WEEK_DAY) return integer
is
case day is
when MON => quota := 100;
when TUE to WED | FRI => quota := 50;
when SAT | SUN => quota := 500;
when others => quota := 75;
signal WDS: WEEK_DAY := MON;

shared variable WDV: WEEK_DAY := TUE;
constant WDC: WEEK_DAY := WED;
incr_proc(WDS, WDV, WDC);
process (WDS)
variable PWDV: WEEK_DAY := TUE;
variable PIV: integer := 0;
procA(WDS, WDS, PWDV, PWDV);
PIV := funcA(WDS) + funcB(WDS) + check_week_day(WDS, WDS, WDS);

A function declaration (npiVhFuncDecl) named "funcA" under package declaration "PP"
is obtained by applying one-to-one method npiVhSubpDecl. However, the function
declaration "funcA" can also obtain its function (body) by applying one-to-one method
npiVhSubpBody.
In vh root "top", there are four subprogram declarations (two npiVhProcDecl objects and
two npiVhFuncDecl objects): procA, funcB, procDeclOnly and funcDeclOnly.
Two relative subprogram bodies ("top.procA" and "top.funcB") for procA and funcB is
obtained by applying one-to-one method npiVhSubpBody.
In vh root "top", there are four subprograms (two npiVhProcedure objects and two
npiVhFunction objects): incr_proc, procA, procB and check_week_day.
For npiVhProcedure "top.procA" and npiVhFunction "top.funcB", npiVhProcDecl and
npiVhFuncDecl is obtained by applying one-to-one method npiVhSubpDecl.

npiVhPure returns 0 if the vh func decl contains the keyword impure, otherwise it returns 1.
In addition, this property only attaches on vh func decl, not vh function.

npiVhProcedure

Vh Subprogram call
A subprogram call contains procedural call (npiVhSeqProcCall and npiVhConcProcCall)
and function call (npiVhFuncCall).
A procedural call contains concurrent procedural calls and sequential procedural calls
because it belongs to vh stmt. A function call has no sub-type because it belongs to vh
expr.

package PP is
type WEEK_DAY is (MON, TUE, WED, THU, FRI, SAT, SUN);
function funcA (d1, d2, d3:WEEK_DAY) return integer;
end PP;
package body PP is
function funcA (d1, d2, d3:WEEK_DAY) return integer is
end PP;

use work.PP.all;
-- subprogram declarations
procedure procA (P1: in WEEK_DAY; P2:WEEK_DAY; P3: out WEEK_DAY; P4:
inout WEEK_DAY);
impure function funcB (d1: in WEEK_DAY) return integer;
-- subprogram declarations without bodies
procedure procDeclOnly (DP: in WEEK_DAY);
pure function funcDeclOnly (DD: in WEEK_DAY) return integer;
-- subprogram bodies (vh procedures and vh functions)
procedure incr_proc (signal I1:WEEK_DAY; variable I2:WEEK_DAY;
constant I3:WEEK_DAY) is
procedure procA (P1: in WEEK_DAY; P2:WEEK_DAY; P3: out WEEK_DAY; P4:
inout WEEK_DAY) is
impure function funcB (d1: in WEEK_DAY) return integer is
function check_week_day(signal day, day2, day3:WEEK_DAY) return
integer is
case day is
when MON => quota := 100;
when TUE to WED | FRI => quota := 50;
when SAT | SUN => quota := 500;
when others => quota := 75;
-- signal decl
signal WDS: WEEK_DAY := MON;
shared variable WDV: WEEK_DAY := TUE;
constant WDC: WEEK_DAY := WED;
-- conc proc call
incr_proc(WDS, WDV, WDC);
process (WDS)
variable PWDV: WEEK_DAY := TUE;
variable PIV: integer := 0;
-- seq proc call
procA(WDS, WDS, PWDV, PWDV);
-- Right-hand-side contains 3 funcCalls

PIV := funcA(WDS) + funcB(WDS) + check_week_day(WDS, WDS, WDS);

Vh Use
npiVhUse is a group that contains npiVhStmt, npiVhBranch and npiVhMapElem. Only
object declaration, parameter, indexed, slice and select name can obtain use by applying
method npiVhUse.
Use contains the object that overlaps the reference handle.

generic (GNR0, GNR1: std_logic_vector(31 downto 0));
port(ea : in std_logic_vector(31 downto 0));
architecture circus of add32 is
signal SI1: std_logic_vector(31 downto 0) := GNR0;
SI1 <= GNR0; -- use GNR0, SI1
SI1(5) <= ea(0); -- use SI1(5)
end architecture circus;

In example.vhd above, generic "GNR0" gets signal assignment "SI1 <= GNR0;" by
applying method npiVhUse. Indexed name "SI1(5)" gets signal assignment "SI1 <=
GNR0;" and signal assignment "SI1(5) <= ea(0);" Port "ea" gets signal assignment "SI1(5)
<= ea(0);".

* For array, the npiVhUse relationship accesses any use of the array, the overlapped
part, the indexed select or slice select of the array. If any variable is in the index or
slice, it is treated as a free index.
For the following example, if npiVhUse is applied for "V1(5)", the results is "V1(i) :=
A1(i);", "V1(5) := V1(0);" and "V1(6 downto 5) := A1(0 to 1);"; if it is applied for "V1(0)",
the result is "V1(i) := A1(i);" and "V1(4 downto i) := A1(4 downto i);".
for i in 2 to 3 loop
V1(i) := A1(i);
V1(4 downto i) := A1(4 downto i);
V1(5) := V1(0);
V1(6 downto 5) := A1(0 to 1);

* For npiPort, there are four different behavior for each kind of port:
VHDL port under VHDL scope: The npiVhStmt which use this port and the
npiVhMapElem of this port.
VHDL port under SV scope: The npiVhStmt which use this port.
SV port under VHDL scope: The npiVhMapElem of this port.
SV port under SV scope: NULL.

Vh Waveform
A waveform element is the basic waveform that contains the value expression and time
expression. A conditional waveform is a vh waveform element with conditional expression.
A selected waveform is a waveform element with choice expressions.

-- => obtain 1 waveform element with value expr: "a or b" and time
expr: "1 ns"
ssa0: sum <= a or b after 1 ns;
-- => obtain 3 conditional waveforms
csa0: sum <= a after 3 ns when cin = '0' else

-- => obtain 4 selected waveforms
sesa0: with NEXT_STATE select

The simple signal assignment "ssa0" obtains a waveform element "a or b after 1 ns" by
applying one-to-many method npiVhWaveform.
The value expression "a or b" and the time expression "1 ns" is obtained by applying oneto-one method npiVhValExpr and npiVhTimeExpr, respectively.
The conditional signal assignment "csa0" obtains three conditional waveforms by applying
one-to-many method npiVhWaveform.
These three waveforms are "a after 3 ns when cin = `0'", "b after 3 ns when cin = `1'" and
"a and b after 3 ns", and they can obtain their own waveform elements by applying one-toone method npiVhWaveformElem.
The former two conditional waveforms can obtain the conditional expressions "cin = `0'"
and "cin = `1'" by applying one-to-one method npiVhCondExpr.
The selected signal assignment "sesa0" obtains four selected waveforms by applying
one-to-many method npiVhWaveform. These four waveforms are "x"00000001" after 1
ns when APPLY | RECEIVE | KEEP", "x"00000010" after 2 ns when WAITS | SLEEP",
"x"00000100" after 3 ns when RESET" and "unaffected when others", and they can obtain
their own waveform elements by applying one-to-one method npiVhWaveformElem.
For the first conditional waveform, three choice expressions "APPLY", "RECEIVE" and
"KEEP" is obtained by applying one-to-many method npiVhChoices.

* For vh cond waveform, applying one-to-many method npiVhChoices returns nothing
when the choice condition is the reserved word others.
* For vh waveform elem, the reserved word unaffected is returned if its property
npiVhUnaffected returns 1.

Library
A library object in the NPI Netlist model serves as a container for cell objects. If you can
import design with symbol libraries, the NPI Netlist model can create corresponding cells
and shapes based on the cell definitions.

* Libraries is accessed using npi_nl_iterate with a NULL reference object.
* The npiNlLibPath property returns a string that represents the path of the library.
* The handles to library objects returned by npi_nl_iterate is not sorted since the
order of symbol libraries depends on the user configuration.

Cell
A cell object in the NPI Netlist model is a cell view which contains the information of cell
pins and cell functions.

1. The npiNlCellType property returns cell functions of instance objects, for example,,
npiNlEQCell, npiNlAndCell, and npiNlBufCell (refer to npi_nl.h).
2. The npiNlPowerCellType property returns power cell functions of instance objects
inferred from liberty.
For example,, npiNlPowerISOCell, npiNlPowerRETCell and npiNlPowerLVSCell
(refer to npi_nl.h).
3. The Boolean property npiNlIsMemoryCell returns TRUE if it has memory() definition in
liberty.
4. The Boolean property npiNlIsPadCell returns TRUE if it has the attribute "pad_cell"
being "true" in liberty.

Cell Pin
A cell pin object in the NPI Netlist model represents the pin of a library cell.

Following is an example of library definition:
library(test) {
cell(level_shifter) {
is_level_shifter : true;
level_shifter_type : HL;
pad_cell : "true";
std_cell_main_rail : true;
pg_function : "VSS";
switch_function : "VDD + VSS";
}
}
area:1;
pin (A) {
input_voltage_range ( 0.7 , 0.9);
}
pin (B) {

function : "A";
power_down_function : "!VDD + VSS";
is_pad : "true" ;
output_voltage_range (1.1 , 1.3)
}
}
cell(ret_cell) {
retention_cell : my_ret_cell;
}
}
pin (RETN) {
related_ground_pin: VSS;
always_on : true;
retention_pin (save_restore, "1");
}
}
}

* For cell pin handle "test.level_shifter.VDD", the npiNlIsStdCellMainRailPin
returns TRUE.
* The npiNlVoltageName returns "VDD", the npiNlPGFunc returns "VSS" and the
npiNlSwitchFunc returns "VDD + VSS".
* For cell pin handle "test.level_shifter.A", the npiNlRelatedPower and
npiNLRelatedGround returns "VDD" and "VSS". The npiNlInputVoltageRngMax and
npiNlInputVoltageRngMin returns "0.9" and "0.7" respectively.
* For cell pin handle "test.level_shifter.B", the npiNlIsPad returns TRUE; the
npiNlRelatedPower and npiNLRelatedGround returns "VDD" and "VSS".
The npiNlOutputVoltageRngMax and npiNlOutputVoltageRngMin returns "1.3"
and "1.1" respectively, and the npiNlPowerDownFunc returns "!VDD + VSS".
* For cell pin handle "test.ret_cell.RETN", the npiNlIsAlwaysOn returns TRUE, the

A port object represents the port of a module instance. It is used to communicate between
instance port and net objects belonging to the module instance.

which the pseudo object is created.

are drivers or loads of the given port.

For an input port, npiNlDriver relation returns the connected instance port object,
while npiNlLoad relation returns the connected net object.
For an output port, npiNlDriver relation returns the connected net object, while

{"PnR_info": [{"x":LowerLeftX, "y":LowerLeftY}, {"x":UpperRightX,

always @ (posedge clk) begin
w1[0] = w2[0][0][0];
w2[3] /*var select*/ = {64{w2[2][0]}};
w3[7] = w2[0][0][0];
end

In the example code above, "w2" is an object with type "array var" (npiArrayVar) whose
unpacked dimension is 2, "w2[3]" is an object with "var select" (npiVarSelect) whose
access dimension is 1.

Virtual Interface Var
A virtual interface variable denotes an interface instance.

In the preceding example,
interface PBus (parameter WIDTH=8); // A parameterized bus interface
logic req, grant;
logic [WIDTH-1:0] addr, data;
modport phy(input addr, ref data);
parameter tp = 35;
PBus (16) p16();
PBus (16) p16Arr [1:0] ();
PBus (32) p32();

virtual PBus v8; // legal declaration, but no legal assignments
virtual PBus (tp) v35; // legal declaration, but no legal assignments
virtual PBus (.WIDTH(16)) v16;
virtual PBus (.WIDTH(16)) v16Arr [1:0] = p16Arr;
virtual PBus (.WIDTH(16)) v16a = p16;
virtual PBus (16) v16b = v16a;
virtual PBus (16) v16c = p16Arr[0];
virtual PBus (16) v16d = v16Arr[0];
virtual PBus (16).phy v16_phy = p16.phy;
virtual PBus (32) v32;
virtual PBus (32).phy v32_phy;
virtual PBus v8Arr [1:0];
virtual PBus v8pArr [1:0];
virtual PBus.phy v8_phyArr [1:0];
v16 = p16; // legal parameter values match
v32 = p32; // legal parameter values match
v32_phy = p32; // legal assignment from no selected modport to selected
modport
end

* v16 is a virtual interface variable and v16Arr is an array of virtual interface variable.
* v16a is a virtual interface variable, and it returns a p16 interface by applying the
npiExpr one-to-one method.
* v16b is a virtual interface variable, and it returns the v16a interface variable by applying
the npiExpr one-to-one method.
* v16_phy is a virtual interface variable assigned by a modport, and it returns the phy
modport by applying the npiExpr one-to-one method. The npiIsModport property value
is 1.

The npiExpr relation returns the interface instance assigned to the virtual interface in its
declaration, if any; otherwise, npiExpr returns NULL.

Refer to the npiVirtualInterfaceVar section in the Language Model - Complete Supported
List section of Appendix A.

Wait
"Wait" belongs to the class "atomic statement".

wait(!enable) /* wait statement */
10 a = b;
end

In the example code above, applying npi_handle(npiCondition, wait_handle) returns the
expression "!enable". Applying npi_handle(npiStmt, wait_handle) returns the delay control
statement "#10 a = b".

While, Repeat
In the NPI Language model, while objects denote while-loop statement that execute a
statement until an expression becomes FALSE, while repeat objects denote repeat-loop
statements that execute a statement a fixed number of times.

integer a, b;
while ( a < b ) /* while statement*/
a = a + 1;
repeat (a) /*repeat statement*/
b = $random;
end

For the while statement shown above, npiCondition transition returns an operation object

at execute a statement a fixed number of times.

integer a, b;
while ( a < b ) /* while statement*/
a = a + 1;
repeat (a) /*repeat statement*/
b = $random;
end

For the while statement shown above, npiCondition transition returns an operation object
(npiOperation) that represents "a < b", and npiStmt transition returns an assignment object
(npiAssignment) that represents "a = a + 1;".
For the repeat statement shown above, npiCondition transition returns a reg variable
(npiReg) named "a", and npiStmt transition returns an assignment object (npiAssignment)
that represents "b = $random;".

In example.vhd, the block with a label name, "bk", contains a generic (bg), three ports (ba,

Vh Branch
The vh branch is derived from vh if and vh cases. The vh branch contains conditional
expressions and sub statements.

incr_proc(isig);
qta <= check_week_day(WED);

For vh if inside procedure "incr_proc", four branches is obtained when applying one-tomany method npiVhBranch. The first branch obtains "cnt > 1" for conditional expression
and obtain "cnt <= cnt + 1;" for sub-statement.
The second branch obtains "cnt = 0" for conditional expression and obtain "cnt <= 0;" for
sub-statement. The third branch obtains "cnt = 1" for conditional expression and obtain
"cnt <= 1;" for sub-statement.
The last branch obtains NULL for conditional expression and obtain "cnt <= -1;" for substatement. For vh case inside function "check_week_day", four branches is obtained
respectively when applying one-to-many method npiVhBranch.
The first branch obtains "MON" for conditional expression and obtain "quota := 100;"
for sub-statement. The second branch obtains "TUE to WED" and "FRI" for conditional
expression and obtain "quota := 50;" for sub-statement.
The third branch obtains "SAT" and "SUN" for conditional expression and obtain "quota :=
500;" for sub-statement. The last branch obtains NULL for conditional expression and
obtain "quota := 75;" for sub-statement.

Vh Design Unit
Design unit includes entity, architecture body, package declaration, and package body.
Root and component are composed of entity and architecture body.
Entity decides the instance shape and input or output structure. Architecture body
decides the actual behavior of the instance. Package instance are composed of package
declaration and package body.

The objects declared in the package declaration is used by other design objects if they
have used this package.

-- [ npiVhPackage: test_pack
-- <npiVhPackDecl>
package test_pack is
procedure ccc (signal cnt: inout integer);
-- <npiVhPackBody>
package body test_pack is
procedure ccc (signal cnt: inout integer) is
if cnt > 0 then
cnt <= cnt + 1;
-- ]
signal es: integer := 0;

Four vh generate scopes is generated under top: "gfor(0)", "gfor(1)", "gfor(2)" and "gif".
"gfor(0)", "gfor(1)" and "gfor(2)" are flattened by generate-for, and "gif" is flattened by
generate-if.
After flattening the generate scopes, the index generated by the condition is the vh index
var, for example, the index expression "I" of the indexed name "sum(I)" is a vh index var.

To distinguish between generate-for scopes and generate-if scopes, check whether an
index number embraced by parentheses is in the tail of the scope name.

cnt <= 1;
cnt <= -1;

Vh Loop
Loop statement is a class that contains three types of loops: for-loop, while-loop and
forever-loop.

process (a, b)

-- npiVhForLoop
fLoop: for loopCnt in 3 downto 0 loop
es: exit fLoop when a(loopCnt)='0';
-- npiVhWhileLoop
wLoop: while (b(0) /= '0') loop
next;
-- npiVhForeverLoop
feLoop: loop
if (a(1) = '0') then
exit;
elsif (a(1) = '1') then
nxs: next feLoop when a(2) = '1';
elsif (a(2) = '0') then
nus: null;

For vh for loop "fLoop", a vh index var "loopCnt" is obtained by applying one-to-one
method npiVhParam and a vh range "3 downto 0" is obtained by applying one-to-one
method npiVhConstraint. In addition, a vh exit "es" is obtained by applying one-to-many
method npiVhStmt.
For vh while loop "wLoop", a vh operation "b(0) /= '0'" is obtained by applying one-toone method npiVhCondExpr and a vh next is obtained by applying one-to-many method
npiVhStmt.
For vh forever loop "feLoop", a vh if is obtained by applying one-to-many method
npiVhStmt.

Vh Map Element
In the NPI Language VHDL model, the vh map element is used to describe the
interconnection relationship for port or generic.

-- Component adder0 has three npiPort: ea, eb, esum
-- => ea can get 5 map elements by 1-to-many method npiVhMapElem
adder0: add32 generic map(GNR0 => x"01010101",
GNR1 => x"10101010")
port map(ea(cv downto 16) => a(cv downto 16),

In example.vhd above, the port "ea" of "top.adder0" has five vh map elements for the port
connection relation. They are "ea(cv downto 16) => a(cv downto 16)", "ea(15 downto 3) =>
a(15 downto 3)", "ea(2 downto 2) => a(2 downto 2)", "ea(1) => '1'" and "ea(0) => a(0)".
For the generic connection relation, "top.adder0" obtains two vh map elements "GNR0 =>
x"01010101"" and "GNR1 => x"10101010"" by applying method npiVhGenericMap.
In each map element, the left side of "=>" is the formal part that is obtained by applying
method npiVhFormal, and the right-hand side of "=>" is the actual part that is obtained by
applying method npiVhActual.

The npiVhScope returns vh subp decl if the formal of this vh map elem is vh param or its
partial object.

constant pc: in std_logic_vector(1 downto 0);
variable pv: out std_logic_vector(3 downto 0)) is
-- pv(3), pc(0): npiVhIndexedName
pv(3) := pc(0);
-- pv(2 downto 0), pc(2 downto 0): npiVhSliceName

-- px(0), b(0): npiVhIndexedName
kkk: prcs.px(0) := b(0) and c(0) and tg(0) and pa(0);

Vh Process
The vh process is a type of concurrent statement and the signals in its sensitivity list is
obtained by applying one-to-many method npiVhSensitivities.
In addition, its sub statements is obtained by applying one-to-many method npiVhStmt and
its declarations under it is obtained by applying one-to-many method npiVhDecl.

-- npiVhProcess
prcs: process (a, b, sum)
variable px: std_logic;
va: px := a(0) or b(0);
if px = '1' then
ssa: sum <= a and b;

The process "prcs" obtains three signals "a", "b" and "sum" by applying one-to-many
method npiVhSensitivities. In addition, variable declaration "px" is obtained by applying
one-to-many method npiVhDecl.
Finally, vh var assign "va" and vh if is obtained by applying one-to-many method
npiVhStmt.

Vh Signal Assignment
Signal assignment contains simple signal assignment, conditional signal assignment,
selected signal assignment, and sequential signal assignment.
The first three assignments belong to concurrent statement, and the last one belongs to
sequential statement.

ssa0: sum <= a or b;
ssa1: sum <= a or b after 1 ns;
csa0: sum <= a or b after 2 ns when cin = '0';
csa1: sum <= a after 3 ns when cin = '0' else
sesa0: with NEXT_STATE select

prcs: process (a, b, sum)
-- sequential signal assignment stmt
sqsa: sum <= a and b;

For a concurrent signal assignment, npiVhCondSigAssign is obtained when there
is a when-else reserved word condition. If there is a with-select reserved word in it,
npiVhSelectSigAssign is obtained. Otherwise, npiVhSimpleSigAssign is obtained.
The simple signal assignment "ssa1" obtains a vh waveform element "a or b after 1 ns" by
applying one-to-many method npiVhWaveform.
The conditional signal assignment "csa1" obtains one vh expression "NEXT_STATE"
by applying one-to-one method npiVhSelectExpr and three conditional waveforms by
applying one-to-many method npiVhWaveform.
These three waveforms are "a after 3 ns when cin = `0'", "b after 3 ns when cin = `1'"
and "a and b after 3 ns", and they can obtain their own waveform elements by applying
one-to-one method npiVhWaveformElem. The former two conditional waveforms can
obtain the conditional expressions "cin = `0'" and "cin = `1'" by applying one-to-one method
npiVhCondExpr.
The selected signal assignment "sesa0" obtains four selected waveforms by applying oneto-many method npiVhWaveform.
These four waveforms are "x"00000001" after 1 ns when APPLY | RECEIVE | KEEP",
"x"00000010" after 2 ns when WAITS | SLEEP", "x"00000100" after 3 ns when RESET"
and "unaffected when others", and they can obtain their own waveform elements by
applying one-to-one method npiVhWaveformElem.
For the first conditional waveform, three choice expressions "APPLY", "RECEIVE" and
"KEEP" is obtained by applying one-to-many method npiVhChoices.
The sequential signal assignment "sqsa" obtains a vh waveform element "a and b" by
applying one-to-many method npiVhWaveform.

Referring to the following example, if a signal assignment includes the reserved word
guarded, its property npiVhGuarded returns 1. Otherwise, it returns 0.
bo <= guarded ba and bb after 5 ns;

Vh Statement
Statements in VHDL contain sequential statements and concurrent statements.
Concurrent statements inside the architecture body describe the internal composition of
the entity.
Sequential statements are also named process statements, and they describe the
functionality of a portion of an entity in sequential terms.

The vh statement is a class of statements containing many objects. Refer to the individual
object introductions for examples.

The property npiVhSeqStmt returns -1 for a non-statement handle, return 0 for a
concurrent statement handle (vh conc stmt) and return 1 for a sequential statement handle
(vh seq stmt).

N/A

Vh Subprogram, Vh Subprogram Declaration
In the NPI Language model, the vh subprogram is a class that contains vh function and vh
procedure. The subprogram in the NPI VHDL model means the subprogram body, not the
declaration.
The subprogram declaration part is modeled as vh subp decl. Similarly, vh subp decl is
also a class that contains vh func decl and vh proc decl.

package PP is

shared variable WDV: WEEK_DAY := TUE;
constant WDC: WEEK_DAY := WED;
incr_proc(WDS, WDV, WDC);
process (WDS)
variable PWDV: WEEK_DAY := TUE;
variable PIV: integer := 0;
procA(WDS, WDS, PWDV, PWDV);
PIV := funcA(WDS) + funcB(WDS) + check_week_day(WDS, WDS, WDS);

A function declaration (npiVhFuncDecl) named "funcA" under package declaration "PP"
is obtained by applying one-to-one method npiVhSubpDecl. However, the function
declaration "funcA" can also obtain its function (body) by applying one-to-one method
npiVhSubpBody.
In vh root "top", there are four subprogram declarations (two npiVhProcDecl objects and
two npiVhFuncDecl objects): procA, funcB, procDeclOnly and funcDeclOnly.
Two relative subprogram bodies ("top.procA" and "top.funcB") for procA and funcB is
obtained by applying one-to-one method npiVhSubpBody.
In vh root "top", there are four subprograms (two npiVhProcedure objects and two
npiVhFunction objects): incr_proc, procA, procB and check_week_day.
For npiVhProcedure "top.procA" and npiVhFunction "top.funcB", npiVhProcDecl and
npiVhFuncDecl is obtained by applying one-to-one method npiVhSubpDecl.

npiVhPure returns 0 if the vh func decl contains the keyword impure, otherwise it returns 1.
In addition, this property only attaches on vh func decl, not vh function.

Vh Use
npiVhUse is a group that contains npiVhStmt, npiVhBranch and npiVhMapElem. Only
object declaration, parameter, indexed, slice and select name can obtain use by applying
method npiVhUse.
Use contains the object that overlaps the reference handle.

generic (GNR0, GNR1: std_logic_vector(31 downto 0));
port(ea : in std_logic_vector(31 downto 0));
architecture circus of add32 is
signal SI1: std_logic_vector(31 downto 0) := GNR0;
SI1 <= GNR0; -- use GNR0, SI1
SI1(5) <= ea(0); -- use SI1(5)
end architecture circus;

In example.vhd above, generic "GNR0" gets signal assignment "SI1 <= GNR0;" by
applying method npiVhUse. Indexed name "SI1(5)" gets signal assignment "SI1 <=
GNR0;" and signal assignment "SI1(5) <= ea(0);" Port "ea" gets signal assignment "SI1(5)
<= ea(0);".

* For array, the npiVhUse relationship accesses any use of the array, the overlapped
part, the indexed select or slice select of the array. If any variable is in the index or
slice, it is treated as a free index.
For the following example, if npiVhUse is applied for "V1(5)", the results is "V1(i) :=
A1(i);", "V1(5) := V1(0);" and "V1(6 downto 5) := A1(0 to 1);"; if it is applied for "V1(0)",
the result is "V1(i) := A1(i);" and "V1(4 downto i) := A1(4 downto i);".
for i in 2 to 3 loop
V1(i) := A1(i);
V1(4 downto i) := A1(4 downto i);
V1(5) := V1(0);
V1(6 downto 5) := A1(0 to 1);

* For npiPort, there are four different behavior for each kind of port:
VHDL port under VHDL scope: The npiVhStmt which use this port and the
npiVhMapElem of this port.
VHDL port under SV scope: The npiVhStmt which use this port.
SV port under VHDL scope: The npiVhMapElem of this port.
SV port under SV scope: NULL.

Vh Waveform
A waveform element is the basic waveform that contains the value expression and time
expression. A conditional waveform is a vh waveform element with conditional expression.
A selected waveform is a waveform element with choice expressions.

-- => obtain 1 waveform element with value expr: "a or b" and time
expr: "1 ns"
ssa0: sum <= a or b after 1 ns;
-- => obtain 3 conditional waveforms
csa0: sum <= a after 3 ns when cin = '0' else

-- => obtain 4 selected waveforms
sesa0: with NEXT_STATE select

The simple signal assignment "ssa0" obtains a waveform element "a or b after 1 ns" by
applying one-to-many method npiVhWaveform.
The value expression "a or b" and the time expression "1 ns" is obtained by applying oneto-one method npiVhValExpr and npiVhTimeExpr, respectively.
The conditional signal assignment "csa0" obtains three conditional waveforms by applying
one-to-many method npiVhWaveform.
These three waveforms are "a after 3 ns when cin = `0'", "b after 3 ns when cin = `1'" and
"a and b after 3 ns", and they can obtain their own waveform elements by applying one-toone method npiVhWaveformElem.
The former two conditional waveforms can obtain the conditional expressions "cin = `0'"
and "cin = `1'" by applying one-to-one method npiVhCondExpr.
The selected signal assignment "sesa0" obtains four selected waveforms by applying
one-to-many method npiVhWaveform. These four waveforms are "x"00000001" after 1
ns when APPLY | RECEIVE | KEEP", "x"00000010" after 2 ns when WAITS | SLEEP",
"x"00000100" after 3 ns when RESET" and "unaffected when others", and they can obtain
their own waveform elements by applying one-to-one method npiVhWaveformElem.
For the first conditional waveform, three choice expressions "APPLY", "RECEIVE" and
"KEEP" is obtained by applying one-to-many method npiVhChoices.

* For vh cond waveform, applying one-to-many method npiVhChoices returns nothing
when the choice condition is the reserved word others.
* For vh waveform elem, the reserved word unaffected is returned if its property
npiVhUnaffected returns 1.

Library
A library object in the NPI Netlist model serves as a container for cell objects. If you can
import design with symbol libraries, the NPI Netlist model can create corresponding cells
and shapes based on the cell definitions.

* Libraries is accessed using npi_nl_iterate with a NULL reference object.
* The npiNlLibPath property returns a string that represents the path of the library.
* The handles to library objects returned by npi_nl_iterate is not sorted since the
order of symbol libraries depends on the user configuration.

Cell
A cell object in the NPI Netlist model is a cell view which contains the information of cell
pins and cell functions.

1. The npiNlCellType property returns cell functions of instance objects, for example,,
npiNlEQCell, npiNlAndCell, and npiNlBufCell (refer to npi_nl.h).
2. The npiNlPowerCellType property returns power cell functions of instance objects
inferred from liberty.
For example,, npiNlPowerISOCell, npiNlPowerRETCell and npiNlPowerLVSCell
(refer to npi_nl.h).
3. The Boolean property npiNlIsMemoryCell returns TRUE if it has memory() definition in
liberty.
4. The Boolean property npiNlIsPadCell returns TRUE if it has the attribute "pad_cell"
being "true" in liberty.

Cell Pin
A cell pin object in the NPI Netlist model represents the pin of a library cell.

Following is an example of library definition:
library(test) {
cell(level_shifter) {
is_level_shifter : true;
level_shifter_type : HL;
pad_cell : "true";
std_cell_main_rail : true;
pg_function : "VSS";
switch_function : "VDD + VSS";
}
}
area:1;
pin (A) {
input_voltage_range ( 0.7 , 0.9);
}
pin (B) {

function : "A";
power_down_function : "!VDD + VSS";
is_pad : "true" ;
output_voltage_range (1.1 , 1.3)
}
}
cell(ret_cell) {
retention_cell : my_ret_cell;
}
}
pin (RETN) {
related_ground_pin: VSS;
always_on : true;
retention_pin (save_restore, "1");
}
}
}

* For cell pin handle "test.level_shifter.VDD", the npiNlIsStdCellMainRailPin
returns TRUE.
* The npiNlVoltageName returns "VDD", the npiNlPGFunc returns "VSS" and the
npiNlSwitchFunc returns "VDD + VSS".
* For cell pin handle "test.level_shifter.A", the npiNlRelatedPower and
npiNLRelatedGround returns "VDD" and "VSS". The npiNlInputVoltageRngMax and
npiNlInputVoltageRngMin returns "0.9" and "0.7" respectively.
* For cell pin handle "test.level_shifter.B", the npiNlIsPad returns TRUE; the
npiNlRelatedPower and npiNLRelatedGround returns "VDD" and "VSS".
The npiNlOutputVoltageRngMax and npiNlOutputVoltageRngMin returns "1.3"
and "1.1" respectively, and the npiNlPowerDownFunc returns "!VDD + VSS".
* For cell pin handle "test.ret_cell.RETN", the npiNlIsAlwaysOn returns TRUE, the
npiNlRetPinClassName returns "save_restore".

* For a pg_pin,
npiNlIsStdCellMainRailPin property returns TRUE when std_cell_main_rail
attribute is set true, return FALSE when set false or not set.
npiNlVoltageName property returns the string that represents the voltage_name
attribute defined in the pg_pin.
npiNlPGFunc, npiNlSwitchFunc returns the string that represents the
pg_function, and switch_function attribute specified in the pg_pin, respectively.
* For a non-pg_pin,
npiNlRelatedPower and npiNLRelatedGround property returns the string of its
specified related_power_pin and related_ground_pin.
If it is not specified, it returns npiNlUndefined. That means, it does not return the
default first primary_power nor the first primary_ground.
npiNlIsAlwaysOn property returns TRUE when always_on attribute is set true;
return FALSE when set false or not set.
For a cell pin in a pad_cell(with pad_cell set "true"), npiNlIsPad property
returns TRUE when is_pad is set (According to LRM, at least one pin in the
pad_cell must have an is_pad attribute). And it returns FALSE when set false or
not set.
For an output pin, npiNlPowerDownFunc property returns the string of its specified
power_down_function.
For a cell pin of a retention_cell, npiNlRetPinClassName property returns
the string that represents the "pin_class" of the retention_pin (pin_class,
disable_value) attribute specified.
For a cell pin in a level-shifter cell (with is_level_shifter set
"true"), npiNlInputVoltageRngMax, npiNlInputVoltageRngMin,

erty returns
the string that represents the "pin_class" of the retention_pin (pin_class,
disable_value) attribute specified.
For a cell pin in a level-shifter cell (with is_level_shifter set
"true"), npiNlInputVoltageRngMax, npiNlInputVoltageRngMin,
npiNlOutputVoltageRngMax, and npiNlOutputVoltageRngMin property returns
the string of "max_value" and "min_value" specified in the input_voltage_range
(min_value, max_value) and output_voltage_range(min_value, max_value)

If it is not specified, it returns npiNlUndefined.
The input_voltage_range and output_voltage_range attributes
defined as default on cell-level is not supported nor accessible from a cell

npiNlCellPin

An instance object in the NPI Netlist model could be a module instance or a primitive
instance. A module instance denotes a module reference in the design that serves as a
container for sub instance, port, instance port, and net objects.
A primitive instance denotes the minimum design unit. It is used to represent low-level
logic gates and switches with specific cell functions.
For example, npiNlAndCell, npiNlFSMCell, and npiNlBufCell.

* Top-level instances are accessed using npi_nl_iterate with a NULL reference object.
* The npiNlInstType property denotes the instance type used in the NPI Netlist model.
Available values include npiNlHierInst, npiNlRTLInst, npiNlSymbolLibInst,
npiNlFSMInst, and npiNlUDPInst.
The npiNlFSMInst is returned for npiNlInstType only when the value of
option "RecogFSM" is TRUE (see Schematic Configurations).
* The npiNlDefName property denotes the instance definition name. For any instance
objects with npiNlInstType of npiNlRTLInst or npiNlFSMInst, the npiNlDefName
property returns NULL.
* The npiNlCellType property returns cell functions of instance objects. for example,
npiNlModuleCell, npiNlAndCell, and npiNlBufCell (refer to npi_nl.h).
* The Boolean property npiNlIsInterface returns TRUE for an instance object if it is
inferred from a SystemVerilog interface.
* The Boolean property npiNlIsModport returns TRUE for an instance object if it is
inferred from a SystemVerilog modport.
* The Boolean property npiNlIsIntfConnector returns TRUE for an instance object if it
is inferred to connect the modport net and the whole interface port.
* The Boolean property npiNlIsIntfNet returns TRUE for an instance object if it is
inferred from the net of interface.
* The location properties npiNlFile, npiNlBeginLineNo, and npiNlEndLineNo returns
the file and line information of an instance object.
An instance object could be inferred from multiple sources. However, the
properties npiNlFile, npiNlBeginLineNo, and npiNlEndLineNo can only
obtain the information of the first source.
* The npiNlSrcInfo property returns a string that represents multiple source
information. The format of a returned string is as follows:
{ File1, BeginLineNo1, EndLineNo1} {File2, BeginLineNo2,
EndLineNo2}

To obtain more precise source information of an instance object, it is highly
recommended to use npiNlSrcInfo instead ofnpiNlFile, npiNlBeginLineNo, and
npiNlEndLineNo.

* An instance object with npiNlCellType of npiNlModuleCell, indicates that the
object is a module instance. For such instances,npiNlDriver, npiNlLoad, and

* An instance object with npiNlCellType that is not npiNlModuleCell, indicates that the

Ports
A port object represents the port of a module instance. It is used to communicate between
instance port and net objects belonging to the module instance.

* The npiNlDirection property returns npiNlInput, npiNlOutput, or npiNlInout.
* For a pseudo port object, the npiNlParent relation returns the actual port object from
which the pseudo object is created.
* The npiNlDriver and npiNlLoad relations return net and instance port objects that
are drivers or loads of the given port.

For an input port, npiNlDriver relation returns the connected instance port object,
while npiNlLoad relation returns the connected net object.
For an output port, npiNlDriver relation returns the connected net object, while
npiNlLoad relation returns the connected instance port object.
For an inout port, both npiNlDriver and npiNlLoad relations return the connected
net and instance port objects.
* The npiNlConnectivity relation always returns the connected net and instance port
objects regardless of the port directions.
* Objects returned from npiNlInstPort, npiNlNet, and npiNlInst relations are
always actual objects.
* For the port with npiNlLangType of npiNlSPICE, the npiNlDirection property returns
npiNlInout.

Instance Ports
An instance port object represents the port instance along with the instance object. In
the NPI Netlist model, each instance port object has a specific property to indicate its
functional type.
For example, npiNlDataPort, npiNlClockPort, and npiNlLatchedPort.

* The npiNlDirection property returns npiNlInput, npiNlOutput, or npiNlInout.
* For a pseudo instance port object, the npiNlParent relation returns the actual instance
port object from which the pseudo object is created.
* The npiNlDriver and npiNlLoad relations returns net and port objects that are drivers
or loads of the given instance port.
* The npiNlConnectivity relation always returns the connected net and port objects
regardless of the port directions.
For an input instance port, npiNlDriver relation returns the connected net object,
while npiNlLoad relation returns the connected port object.
For an output instance port, npiNlDriver relation returns the connected port
object, while npiNlLoadrelation returns the connected net object.
For an inout instance port, both npiNlDriver and npiNlLoad relations return the
connected net and port objects.
* The npiNlPortType property returns functional types of instance port objects.
For example, npiNlDataPort, npiNlClockPort, and npiNlSyncSetPort (refer to
npi_nl.h).
* The npiNlPortState property returns the state of instance port objects. Available
values include: npiNlHighActive, npiNlLowActive, npiNlRisingActive, and
npiNlFallingActive.
For instance, port belonging to the instance with npiNlInstType of npiNlRTLInst,
npiNlSymbolLibInst, and npiNlFSMInst, the npiNlPortState property returns one
of the available values.

Object Type: npiTextFile

There is a one-to-many relationship from a NULL object to objects of type file.

Objects of type file have properties with their data type npiTextHandleType (string),
npiTextFileFullName (string), npiTextFileName (string), npiTextFileElabName (string),
npiTextFileContent (string), and npiTextLineCount (integer).

The property npiTextFileElabName means the file name used during the design
elaboration time of Verdi. Take the following case as an example:
The design file "example_inc.vh":

The design file "example.v":

After importing the design, the same source file "example_inc.vh" might becomes three
different text file handles, because of the define-undef sequence used in the example.v.

Therefore, in the design, there are four text file handles:
* npiTextFileName = example.v, npiTextFileElabName = example.v
* npiTextFileName = example_inc.vh, npiTextFileElabName = example_inc.vh
* npiTextFileName = example_inc.vh, npiTextFileElabName = example_inc.vh#$#1
* npiTextFileName = example_inc.vh, npiTextFileElabName = example_inc.vh#$#2
The name of npiTextFileElabName is determined by Verdi system.
To map the type of object shown in the object diagram to the real type name
used in the C++/Tcl program, you need to add the prefix "npiText" in front of
the object name enclosed in the circle cape rectangle and change the first
character of the object name to uppercase.

Assign Statement, Deassign, Force, Release
Object Types: Assign Statement (npiDMAssignStmt), Deassign (npiDmDeassign),
Force (npiDmForce), Release (npiDmRelease)

Assign statement and force are procedural continues assignments (using keywords assign
and force) that allow expressions to be driven continuously onto variables or nets.
De-assign and release are procedure statements ends a procedure continues assignment
to a variable or a net.
Assign statement, de-assign, force, and release belong to the class of the atomic

reg ra;

assign ra = 1'bx; /* assign stmt */
deassign ra; /* deassign */
force w2 = 1'bz; /* force */
release w2; /* release */

* Apply method "npiDmLeft" to the handle "assign ra = 1'bx", and the npiDmVar handle
"ra" is returned.
* Apply method "npiDmRight" to the handle "assign ra = 1'bx", and the npiDmConstant
handle "1'bx" is returned.

Assignment
Object Type: npiDmAssignment

Assignment means a procedural assignment within a process and belongs to the class
atomic statement.
Property "npiDmOperator" returns npiDmAssignmentOp_e.

reg LHS, RHS, clk;
LHS = RHS; /* assignment_1 */

LHS = 10 RHS; /* assignment_2 */
LHS <= @(posedge clk) RHS; /* assignment_3 */
LHS <= repeat (5) @(posedge clk) RHS; /* assignment_4 */
LHS += 1; /* assignment_5 */
LHS++; /* assignment_6 */
end

* Apply method "npiDmLeft" to the handle "assignment_#1", and the npiDmVar handle
"LHS" is returned.
* Apply method "npiDmRight" to the handle "assignment_#1", and the npiDmVar handle
"RHS" is returned.
* Apply method "npiDmDelayControl" to the handle "assignment_#2", and the
npiDmConstant handle "10" is returned.
* Apply method "npiDmEventControl" to the handle "assignment_#3", and the
npiDmEventControl handle "@(posedge clk)" is returned.

Case, Case Item
Object Type: Case (npiDmCase), Case Item (npiDmCaseItem)

Case is a statement that is a multi way decision statement and tests whether an
expression matches one of a number of other expressions and branches accordingly.
Case item is a handle that consists of a condition expression and a statement. The
statement within case item represents a scenario of the case branches.
Case belongs to the class of the atomic statement. However, case item doesn't belong to
statement class.
Property "npiDmCaseType" returns npiDmCaseType_e.

module TOP(a, b, c);
input a, b, c;
reg [15:0] result;
reg [3:0] select;
always @ (a or b or c) begin
case(select) /* case statement */
4'd1, 4'd2, 4'd3: result = 16'h1111; /*case item 1*/
4'd4, 4'd5: result = 16'h2222; /*case item 2*/
default : result = 16'h0000; /*case item 3*/
end

* Apply method "npiDmCondition" to the handle "case", and the npiDmVar handle
"select" is returned.
* Apply method "npiDmCaseItem" to the handle "case", and three npiDmCaseItem
handles is returned.
* Apply method "npiDmExpr" to the handle "case item 1", and the npiDmConstant handle
"4'd1", "4'd2", and "4'd3" is returned.
* Apply method "npiDmStmt" to the handle "case item 1", and three npiDmAssignment
handle "result = 16'h1111" is returned.

* Apply method "npiDmExpr" to the handle "case item 3", no handle is returned since it is
a default case item.
* Apply property "npiDmCaseType" to handle "case", and "npiDmCaseExact" is returned.

File
Object Type: npiTextFile

There is a one-to-many relationship from a NULL object to objects of type file.
There is a one-to-many relationship from an object of type file to objects of type line and a
many-to-one relationship from objects of type line to an object of type file.
Objects of type file have properties with their data type npiTextHandleType (string),
npiTextFileFullName (string), npiTextFileName (string), npiTextFileElabName (string),
npiTextFileContent (string), and npiTextLineCount (integer).

The property npiTextFileElabName means the file name used during the design
elaboration time of Verdi. Take the following case as an example:
The design file "example_inc.vh":

The design file "example.v":

After importing the design, the same source file "example_inc.vh" might becomes three
different text file handles, because of the define-undef sequence used in the example.v.

Therefore, in the design, there are four text file handles:
* npiTextFileName = example.v, npiTextFileElabName = example.v
* npiTextFileName = example_inc.vh, npiTextFileElabName = example_inc.vh
* npiTextFileName = example_inc.vh, npiTextFileElabName = example_inc.vh#$#1
* npiTextFileName = example_inc.vh, npiTextFileElabName = example_inc.vh#$#2
The name of npiTextFileElabName is determined by Verdi system.
To map the type of object shown in the object diagram to the real type name
used in the C++/Tcl program, you need to add the prefix "npiText" in front of
the object name enclosed in the circle cape rectangle and change the first
character of the object name to uppercase.
For example, the "file" object type is named as "npiTextFile" in C++/Tcl.
A file handle is traversed through other related objects (refer to the depicted arrows).

Tcl: set file_iterator [ npi_text_iter_start -type npiTextFile -ref "" ]

Tcl: set file_handle [ npi_text_handle -type npiTextFile -ref
$line_handle ]

Object Types: Assign Statement (npiDMAssignStmt), Deassign (npiDmDeassign),

Assign statement and force are procedural continues assignments (using keywords assign
and force) that allow expressions to be driven continuously onto variables or nets.

handle "1'bx" is returned.

Case, Case Item
Object Type: Case (npiDmCase), Case Item (npiDmCaseItem)

Case is a statement that is a multi way decision statement and tests whether an
expression matches one of a number of other expressions and branches accordingly.
Case item is a handle that consists of a condition expression and a statement. The
statement within case item represents a scenario of the case branches.
Case belongs to the class of the atomic statement. However, case item doesn't belong to
statement class.
Property "npiDmCaseType" returns npiDmCaseType_e.

module TOP(a, b, c);
input a, b, c;
reg [15:0] result;
reg [3:0] select;
always @ (a or b or c) begin
case(select) /* case statement */
4'd1, 4'd2, 4'd3: result = 16'h1111; /*case item 1*/
4'd4, 4'd5: result = 16'h2222; /*case item 2*/
default : result = 16'h0000; /*case item 3*/
end

* Apply method "npiDmCondition" to the handle "case", and the npiDmVar handle
"select" is returned.
* Apply method "npiDmCaseItem" to the handle "case", and three npiDmCaseItem
handles is returned.
* Apply method "npiDmExpr" to the handle "case item 1", and the npiDmConstant handle
"4'd1", "4'd2", and "4'd3" is returned.
* Apply method "npiDmStmt" to the handle "case item 1", and three npiDmAssignment
handle "result = 16'h1111" is returned.

* Apply method "npiDmExpr" to the handle "case item 3", no handle is returned since it is
a default case item.
* Apply property "npiDmCaseType" to handle "case", and "npiDmCaseExact" is returned.

Continuous Assignment means SystemVerilog continuous assignment.

wire [3:0] w2 = 0 /*npiDmContAssign*/;
wire w5;
reg rr;
assign w1 =
assign {w3,
assign w5 =
assign rr =

1; /*npiDmContAssign*/
w4} = 2'b01; /*npiDmContAssign*/
1; /*npiDmContAssign*/

title: 1 01; /*npiDmContAssign*/

Delay Control
Object Type: npiDmDelayControl

Delay control means that if a procedural assignment following the delay control is delayed
in its execution with respect to the procedural statement preceding the delay control by the
specified delay.
Delay control belongs to the class of the atomic statement.

reg reset, r1;
always /* process always */
100 /* delay control statement*/
begin: BLK /* named begin-end */
if(reset)
r1 = 0;
r1 = 1 1;
end

* Apply method "npiDmDelay" to the handle "#100 begin: BLK end", and the
npiDmConstant handle "100" is returned.
* Apply method "npiDmStmt" to the handle "#100 begin: BLK end", and the
npiDmNamedBegin handle "begin: BLK" is returned.

Disable
Object Type: npiDmDisable

Disable provides the ability to terminate the activity associated with concurrently active
processes, while maintaining the structured nature of procedural descriptions.
Disable belongs to the class of the atomic statement.

disable blk_n; /* npiDmDisable */
end

Apply method "npiDmExpr" to the handle "disable blk_n", and the npiDmNamedBegin
handle "blk_n" is returned.

Do-while
Object Type: npiDmDoWhile

Do-while is a kind of loop statement. It executes a statement first and tests its control
expression at the end of the loop.

The loop stops until do-while's control expression becomes false. Do-while belongs to the
class of the atomic statement.

do
// do while statement
begin : fff
x = x - 1;
if (x > 5) begin
end
end
while (x > 0);
return x + 10;
end

* Apply method "npiDmCondition" to the handle "do-while", and the npiDmOperation
handle "x > 0" is returned.
* Apply method "npiDmStmt" to the handle "do-while", and the npiDmNamedBegin
handle "begin: fff" is returned.

Object Type: npiDmEvent

Event means the SystemVerilog event construct.

event ev; /*npiDmEvent*/
event evAry1 [3:0]; /*npiDmEvent*/
event evAry2 [1:0][2:0]; /*npiDmEvent*/
task too( ref event task_e /*npiDmEvent*/ );

Apply property "npiDmTaskFuncArgument" to the handle "task_e", and "1" is returned.

Event Control
Object Type: npiDmEventControl

Event control means that the execution of a procedural statement is synchronized with a
value change on a net or variable or the occurrence of a declared event.
Event control belongs to the class of the atomic statement.

reg clk, reset, r1;

Object Type: npiDmEventStmt

Event statement means an event triggering statement. The blocking event is triggered
using the -> operator, and the non-blocking event is triggered using the ->> operator.

event e2;
->e1; /* npiDmEventStmt_1 */
->>e2; /* npiDmEventStmt_2 */

* Apply property "npiDmBlocking" to handle "->>e2", and "0" is returned.

Expression, Constant, Operation
Object Type: Constant (npiDmConstant), Operation (npiDmOperation)

Simple expression is a class composed of net, variable, parameter, and interface
reference.
Constant means SystemVerilog constant literals or values such as "3'b001".
Operation is a construct that combines operands with operators such as "a[0]" or "{a, b}".
Property "npiDmConstType" returns npiDmConstType_e.
Property "npiDmOpType" returns npiDmOpType_e.
Property "npiDmDataType" returns npiDmDataType_e.
The "npiDmTypespec" method and the property "npiDmDataType" for operation are only
for the npiDmOpTypeCasting, npiDmOpTypeKeyAsgPtn, npiDmOpTypeStreamRL and
npiDmOpTypeStreamLR operations.

logic [$bits(w1):0] v1;
typedef integer usr_def_type;
usr_def_type u1;
assign {w1, w2} /*npiDmOperation*/ = 2'b01 /*npiDmConstant*/;
assign u1 = usr_def_type'(2'b11) /*npiDmOperation*/;

and "w2" is returned.

npiDmTypespec handle "usr_def_type" is returned.

* Apply property "npiDmDataType" to handle "usr_def_type'(2'b11)", and
"npiDmDtTypespec" is returned.

For
Object Type: npiDmFor

For is a kind of loop statement. It consists of one or more initial statements, a control
expression, one or more step statements, and a statement which is executed every time
the control expression return true.
For belongs to the class of the scope and the atomic statement.
Only for statements containing variable declarations as part of the for-initialization
assignment create implicit begin-end block around the for-loop.
The block creates a new hierarchy scope, making the variables local to the loop scope.
Therefore, the proerty npiDmLocalVarDecls is used to decide whether a for statement is a

parameter int SIZE = 256;
integer index=0;
function myfunc;
for(index=0; index<SIZE; index=index+1) /* for statement */
begin: ggg
$display("aaa");
end
myfunc = 1;

"index=index+1" is returned.

"begin: ggg" is returned.

Forever
Object Type: npiDmForever

Forever is a kind of loop statement. It continuously executes a statement. It belongs to the
class of the atomic statement.

forever CYCLE clk = ~clk; /* forever */
end

"#CYCLE clk = ~clk is returned.

Generate Block
Object Type: npiDmGenBlock

Generate block is a collection of one or more module items. It is either conditionally or
multiply instantiated in generate constructs.

A generate block might not contain port declarations, parameter declarations, specify
blocks or specparam declarations. All other modules items, including other generate
constructs, are allowed in a generate block.
* A generate construct must contain a generate block in DM model.
* A generate block is not a scope only if (1) it is within a conditionally generate
construct, (2) it has no begin-end keyword, and (3) it only contains another
conditionally generate construct.

"npiDmImplicitDecl" returns 0. Otherwise, this property returns 1.

if (q==3) /* npiDmGenIf_4 */
begin /* npiDmGenBlock_4 */
end

Generate Construct
Object Types: npiDmGenConstruct

Generate constructs are used to either conditionally or multiply instantiate generate blocks
into a model. They are if-generate, if-else-generate, case-generate and for-generate
constructs.
The if-generate, if-else-generate and case-generate constructs instantiate at most one
generate block from a set of alternative generate blocks. They belong to conditionally
generate constructs.
The for-generate construct allow a single generate block to be instantiated into a model
multiple times. It belongs to loop generate construct.

for (i = 0; i < 2; i++ ) /* npiDmGenFor_1 */
begin : u1
end
if (p == 1) /* npiDmGenIf_1 */
end
if (p == 0) /* npiDmGenIfElse_1 */
end

end
case(p) /* npiDmGenCase_1 */
1'b0:
end
1'b1:
end

* Apply method "npiDmScope" to the handle "npiDmGenFor_#1", and the npiDmModule
handle "top" is returned.

Generate-for Construct
Object Types: npiDmGenFor

Generate-for construct belongs to the loop generate construct, which instantiates a single
generate block into a model multiple times.
It consists of one initial statement, a control expression, one step statement, and a
generate block which is instantiated every time the control expression return true.

module top; /* npiDmModule_1 */
genvar i; /* npiDmGenVar_1 */
for (i = 0; i < 2; i++ ) /* npiDmGenFor_1 */
begin : u1 /* npiDmGenBlock_1 */
end
for(genvar j = 0; j < 2; j++ ) /*npiDmGenFor_2, npiDmGenVar_2*/
begin : u2 /* npiDmGenBlock_2 */
end

npiDmAssignment handle "i = 0" is returned.
* Apply method "npiDmCondition" to the handle "npiDmGenFor_#1", and the
npiDmOperation handle "i < 2" is returned.
* Apply method "npiDmForIncStmt" to the handle "npiDmGenFor_#1", and the

handle "npiDmGenVar_#1" is returned.

* Apply method "npiDmGenVar" to the handle "npiDmGenBlock_#2", and the
npiDmGenVar handle "npiDmGenVar_#2" is returned.
* Apply method "npiDmScope" to the handle "npiDmGenVar_#2", and the
npiDmGenBlock handle "npiDmGenBlock_#2" is returned.

Object Types: Generate-if Construct (npiDmGenIf), Generate-if-else Item
(npiDmGenIfElse)

Generate-if and generate-if-else constructs belong to the conditional generate construct,
which instantiates at most one generate block from a set of alternative generate blocks.

if (p == 1) /* npiDmGenIf_1 */
begin : u1 /* npiDmGenBlock_1 */
end
if (p == 0) /* npiDmGenIfElse_1 */
begin : v1 /* npiDmGenBlock_2 */

Object Types: npiDmGenVar

Genvar is an integer during elaboration to evaluate the generate loop but it does not exist

as an index variable in an inner loop.

module top; /* npiDmModule_1 */
genvar i; /* npiDmGenVar_1 */
for (i = 0; i < 2; i++ ) /*npiDmGenFor_1, npiDmGenBlock_1*/
for (genvar j = 0; j < 4; j++) /* npiDmGenFor_2, npiDmGenVar_2 */
begin : u1 /* npiDmGenBlock_2 */
end
