Hierarchical Reference, Reference
Object Type: Hierarchical Reference (npiDmHierRef), Reference (npiDmRef)

There are several meaning for Hierarchical Reference in the DM model as follows:
* SystemVerilog hierarchial reference which accesses external scope object.
* SystemVerilog struct or union member access.
* SystemVerilog interface member access by interface port reference.
* SystemVerilog built-in method call of object.
The Reference is the segment of Hierarachical Reference. It contains the information of bit
select of part select and the actual object.

package pkg;
bit pa;
package pkg2;
bit pa2;

bit i1;
typedef struct { bit s1; bit s2; } T1;
import pkg2::pa2;
T1 s;
m1 i0();
// 1. hierarchical reference
assign pkg::pa = 1;
assign pa2 = 1;
// 1. hierarchical reference
assign top.i0.a[0][1:0] = 1;
// 2. struct member access
assign s.s1 = 1;
// 4. build-in method call
bit total;
byte b[] = { 1, 2, 3, 4 };
assign total = b.sum;
module m1( itf i );
bit [1:0][2:0] a;
// 3. interface member access by interface port reference
assign i.i1 = 1;

* Apply method "npiDmRef" to the the handle "top.i0.a[0][1:0]", and the npiDmRef
handles "top", "i0" and "a[0][1:0]" is returned.
* Apply method "npiDmSelect" to the reference handle "a[0][1:0]", and the
npiDmOperation handles "[0]" and "[1:0]" is returned.
* Apply method "npiDmActual" to the reference handle "a[0][1:0]", and the npiDmVar
handle "a" in the module m1 is returned.

Vh Loop
Object Type: npiDmVhWhile, npiDmVhFor

Vh Loop is a class composed of Loop(npiDmVhWhile) and For Loop(npiDmVhFor). A loop
statement includes a sequence of statements that is to be executed repeatedly, zero or
more times.

variable cnt: integer := 2;
-- npiDmVhWhile
loop1: loop
if_stmt1: if(cnt = 0) then -- npiDmVhIf
exit;
cnt := 0;
end loop loop1;
-- npiDmVhWhile
loop2: while (cnt > 0) loop
if_stmt2: if(cnt > 0) then -- npiDmVhIf

cnt := cnt - 1;
cnt := cnt + 1;
end loop loop2;
-- npiDmVhFor
loop3: for ii in 3 downto 0 loop
va: cnt := cnt + ii; -- npiDmVhVarAssign
end loop loop3;

* npiDmVhWhile handle "loop1"

Assert Coverage
Object Types: Assert Metric (npiCovAssertMetric), Assert (npiCovAssert), Cover
Property (npiCovCoverProperty), Cover Sequence (npiCovCoverSequence),
Success Bin (npiCovSuccessBin), Attempt Bin (npiCovAttemptBin), Failure
Bin (npiCovFailureBin), Vacuous Bin (npiCovVacuousBin), Incomplete Bin
(npiCovIncompleteBin) and Firstmatch Bin (npiCovFirstmatchBin).

Assert Metric collects all the assert, cover property and cover sequence handles.
Success bin means the hit count for assert, match count for cover property and all
matches count for cover sequence.

Attempt bin means the attempt count. Failure bin means the failure count for assert.
Vacuous bin means the vacuous success count for cover property. Incomplete bin means
the incomplete count.
Firstmatch bin means the first match count for cover sequence.

* Assert generates child bins: Success, attempt, failure and incomplete.
Cover property generates child bins: Success, attempt, vacuous and incomplete.
Cover sequence generates child bins: Success, attempt, firstmatch and incomplete.
* Cover information only shows in assert, cover property and cover sequence. The
property npiCoverable of them is 1.
The property npiCovCount of success bin determines its scope handle (assert, cover
property or cover sequence) covered or not. (the value of npiCovCovered).
* The property npiCovCount can be set for success bin, attempt bin, failure bin,
incomplete bin and firstmatch bin. Similarly, the count of success bin could affect the
property npiCovered and npiCovStatus of its scope handle.

N.A

Branch Coverage
Object Types: Branch Metric (npiCovBranchMetric), Branch (npiCovBranch), Branch
Bin (npiCovBranchBin), Branch Term (npiCovBranchTerm)

Branch Metric tracks the execution of conditional statements in the design code. Branch is
a section of block which contains the combination of conditional statements.
Branch Bin is a vector value taken on the branch term of the branch. Branch Term is the
composition of the branch.

Condition Coverage
Object Types: Condition Metric (npiCovConditionMetric), Condition
(npiCovCondition), Condition Bin (npiCovConditionBin), Condition Term
(npiCovConditionTerm)

Condition Metric monitors whether certain expressions and sub expressions in the design
code evaluate to true or false. Condition is a logical or bitwise expression.

Condition Bin is a vector value taken on the condition term of the expression. Condition
Term is the composition of the expression.

Coverage Database
Object Type: Database (npiCovDatabase), Test (npiCovTest), Test Info
(npiCovTestInfo)

Database represents the object loaded from a coverage database. It contains the
available tests and the top-level instances of the design.
Test represents the result of a single execution of a tool or the merged results of two or
more executions. It contains the coverage data which determine a coverage object is
covered or not.
Test Info represents the test information got from merged test.
To get the top-level instance, apply the method "npiCovInstance" to the database handle.
Only one database could be opened in a single process. If the application wants
to open another database, the original database should be closed first.

Covered Test
Object Type: Covered Test (npiCovCoveredTest)

Covered Test represents the test that covers the bin handle.

There are three tests: "t0", "t1", and "t2". The merged test of these three tests is "tm".
Cover bin "cbA" named "auto[0]" is covered by "t0" twice and "t2" three times. The pseudo
code for getting the covered tests would be like:
printf("Cover bin: %s is covered by\n", npi_cov_get_str(npiCovName,
cbA));
npiCovHandle ctItr = npi_cov_iter_start(npiCovCoveredTest, cbA, tm/*test
must be given*/);
npiCovHandle ct = NULL;
while ((ct = npi_cov_iter_next(ctItr))) {
printf(" %s (%d times)\n", npi_cov_get_str(npiCovName, ct),
npi_cov_get(npiCovCount, ct, tm));
}
npi_cov_iter_stop(ctItr);

Cover bin: auto[0] is covered by
t0 (2 times)
t1 (3 times)

1. One-to-many method npiCovCoveredTest must be applied to test handle when getting
iterator.
2. npiCovCount for covered test means the covered times for the associated bin handle.

Finite State Machine Coverage
Object Types: Fsm Metric (npiCovFsmMetric), Fsm (npiCovFsm), States
(npiCovStates), Transitions (npiCovTransitions), Sequences (npiCovSequences),
State Bin (npiCovStateBin), Transition Bin (npiCovTransBin), Sequence Bin
(npiCovSeqBin)

Fsm Metric tracks the states and transitions of the finite state machines recognized by
verification tools. Fsm represents a finite state machine logic.
States represents the possible states of the FSM. Transitions represents the possible
transitions of the FSM.
Sequences represents the possible sequence of the FSM. State Bin represents the
coverage object of a state.
Transition Bin represents the coverage object of a transition. Sequence Bin represents the
coverage object of a sequence.

Object Type: npiCovInstance

Instance represents the hierarchical structure of the design. Instance contains a variety of
metrics. The metric defines the method of the measurement.
To get the parent instance, apply the method "npiCovScope" to the instance handle. To get
the child instances, apply the method "npiCovInstance" to the instance handle.

npiCovDefInfo shows the instance's definition name plus the information of assigned

parameter value.

Line Coverage
Object Types: Line Metric (npiCovLineMetric), Block (npiCovBlock), Statement Bin
(npiCovStmtBin)

Line Metric tracks which statements in the design source code were executed during
simulation.
Block represents the section of code, contains statements. Statement Bin represents the
coverage object of a statement.

Power Coverage
Object Types: Power Domain (npiCovPowerDomain), Power Measure
(npiCovPowerMeasure), Power Metric (npiCovPowerMetric) and Covergroup
(npiCovCovergroup)

Power Domain is the power network defined by upf or cpf.

Power Measure is the measure unit under power domain to connect the covergroups for
power coverage estimation. Power Metric collects all the covergroups for power coverage
estimation.
Covergroup here mentions the covergroup whose purpose is to estimate power coverage.
These covergroups only appears under power metrics.

1. If coverage database generated by simulator contains low-power hierarchical
verification plan, power domains is generated from test. Otherwise, power metric is
generated from test directly.
2. For VCS, the option -power=coverage+dump_hvp needs to be applied to generate lowpower hierarchical verification plan.

N.A.

VCS Database
Database represents the object loaded from the simulator database generated by VCS.
It contains compilation information, design statistics, simulation information and test
A simulation test means running simulation once.
The number of simv runs without cleaning the database equals the number of simulation
tests.

* The database handle is obtained by the npi_vcs_open API.
* npiVcsToolName is always "VCS".

Compilation
The compilation handle shows the compilation information from the database generated
by the VCS simulator.

* npiVcsResult returns 1 if the compilation result is successful; otherwise, returns 0.

Design Statistics
The Design statistics handle shows the basic design information like the module number
and all the module information.

* Module signifies the module definition in the design.

Simulation
The simulation handle contains the simulation information like simulation begin-time and
end-time. Combined with simulation test handle, the information in every simulation test
can also be obtained.

* Waveform signifies the waveform dumped by a specific system task.

Test
Test signifies the simulation test by simv. The execution times of simv is equal to the test
number. This information (test number) can be obtained by the npiVcsTestNo property
from design statistics (npiVcsDesignStats) handle.

N/A

Time is the handle to represent the time information from compilation or simulation. The
time format could be time_t or double.

* npiVcsFormat indicates what kind of value format npi_vcs_get_value should use.
Start time, finish time, and gen time use the npiVcsTimeVal format.
Elapsed time and cpu time use the npiVcsDoubleVal format.

Module represents the module definition in the design.

* npiVcsLength signifies the number of code lines for the module definition.

Waveform
Waveform represents the waveform dumping system task. The number of waveforms is
equal to the number of dumping system tasks.

* npiVcsSize signifies the size of the waveform file and the unit is KB.

Iterator is the container to save the handles obtained by one-to-many method.

* npiVcsSize signifies the number of handles that is iterated by this iterator.

Property Note
Language type

The language of a scope is the module language.

For scope objects of instances, the returned language type is the
module language, not the instance language.
For example, u1 is instantiated under top, which is Verilog. Module
u1 is written in VHDL. Therefore, npi_crdb_get(npiCrdbLangType,
handle_of_u1) returns npiCrdbVHDL instead of npiCrdbVerilog.

Traversal Note

A composite signal reference handle can use npiCrdbVolChild to get all its member
handles. Example: struct {logic f1; logic [1:0] f2;} st1;
//-- check st1Handle is a struct

NPI_INT32 is_struct = 0;
NPI_INT32 has_prop_ = npi_crdb_get(npiCrdbSigType, st1Handle,
is_struct/*O*/);
if((0 == has_prop) || (0==is_struct))
//-- iterate childs of struct st1
npiCrdbHandle memIter = npi_crdb_vol_iter_start (npiCrdbVolChild,
st1Handle);
if( memIter == NPI_CRDB_INVALID_HANDL) {
}
npiCrdbHandle memberH = npi_crdb_vol_iter_next (memIter); //get f1
memberH = npi_crdb_vol_iter_next (topScopeIter); //get f2
NPI_INT32 code = npi_crdb_vol_iter_stop (memIter);

Only Bit signal can iterate equivalent signals and correlate signals

Does not allow sig iterate equivalent or correlate signals
Allows sig[1] and sig[0] iterate equivalent or correlate signals
Note that you need to use npi_crdb_vol_iter_start, npi_crdb_vol_iter_next, and
npi_crdb_vol_iter_stop to iterate equivalent, correlation, and child signals.
The return handles are volatile handles.
CRDB only extracts equivalent nets of signal whose dimension <= 1. NPI CRDB model
follows what CRDB has, that is, only signal of npiCrdbBit or npiCrdbBus might have
equivalent nets.

Property Note
Port direction

The direction is based on CRDB model instead of language model.
Some other ports such as ref port might be modeled as input port in
CRDB.

Signal type

The signal type is based on CRDB model instead of language model.
In CRDB model, packed and unpacked information is not reserved, so
packed array and unpacked array are modeled the same in CRDB.

Size and range

Size is the number of 1st level elements of composite signals.
Example: wire [6:4][2:0] mdap2;

Left and right

Because CRDB does not have information about a range of a struct
array is increased or decreased, decrease range is used.
Example: struct packed {reg f1;} [0:7] st1;
NPI_INT32 left_val = 0;
NPI_INT32 right_val = 0;
NPI_INT32 has_prop_ = npi_crdb_get(npiCrdbLeft,

NPI_INT32 has_prop_ = npi_crdb_get(npiCrdbRight,

HVP Plan
Plan represents the object loaded from hierarchical verification plan. The hierarchy
is composed of features. Plan defines some attributes, annotations and metrics for
estimating the coverage status.

Plan handle is obtained by API npi_hvp_load_plan.

Spec
Spec file for the hierarchical verification plan.

NA.

Attribute Declaration
Attribute declaration is declared under plan and used by features. Attribute declaration
contains four data type: integer, real, string and enum. The difference between attribute
and annotation is that attribute propagates the assigned value down to the child hierarchy
unless it is explicitly overridden at the plan or feature level.

attribute real fraction = 1.0; // attribute decl; npi_hvp_get_value
gets 1.0
annotationreal fractionAnn = 2.0;

npi_hvp_get_value for attribute decl gets the value assigned in its right-hand-side.

Annotation Declaration
Annotation declaration is declared under plan and used by features. Annotation
declaration contains four data type: integer, real, string and enum. The difference between
attribute and annotation is that attribute propagates the assigned value down to the child
hierarchy unless it is explicitly overridden at the plan or feature level.

annotation real fractionAnn = 2.0; //annotation decl;
npi_hvp_get_value gets 2.0

npi_hvp_get_value for attribute decl gets the value assigned in its right-hand-side.

Attribute Assign
Attribute assign represents the attribute value assign statement under plan.

fraction = 3.0; // attribute assign
fractionAnn= 5.0;

NA

Annotation Assign
Annotation assign represents the annotation value assign statement under plan.

attribute enum{orange, apple, banana} fruitName = orange;

fractionAnn = 5.0; //annotation assign

NA

Attribute represents the usable attribute under plan or feature.

fraction = 3.0; // attribute: fraction; npi_hvp_get_value
respectively returns 1.0 when "isGetDefaultVal" is true
// and 3.0 when "isGetDefaultVal" is false

npi_hvp_get_value for attribute returns the default value (pre-defined value or value
assigned in declaration) if setting flag "isGetDefaultVal" as true; otherwise, return the
current assigned value.

Annotation
Annotation represents the usable annotation under plan or feature.

fractionAnn = 5.0; //annotation: fractionAnn;
npi_hvp_get_value respectively returns 2.0 when "isGetDefaultVal" is
// true and 5.0 when "isGetDefaultVal" is false

npi_hvp_get_value for annotation returns the default value (pre-defined value or value
assigned in declaration) if setting flag "isGetDefaultVal" as true; otherwise, return the
current assigned value.

NPI Libraries is a set of libraries that extend the functionality of NPI Models. The goal is to
improve the NPI programmers' productivity by reducing reinvention-of-the-wheel.
The libraries are aimed at a wide range of NPI users and application domains. They
range from common design traversal applications like hierarchy tree dumping, module
annotation, signal driver/load tracing, to specific design flow enhancements like design
rule validation, design manipulation, and so on. Some special NPI Models programming
tricks are also included.
NPI Libraries covers both C/C++ APIs and Tcl commands. All of them are written using
NPI Models. They are open source. Users can download NPI Libraries and make
modifications as desired.

In SystemVerilog, the design hierarchy includes the following scopes:
* Instance (module instance, interface, or package).
* Task and function declaration.
* Named begin block.
* (unnamed) begin block.
* Named fork block.
* (unnamed) fork block.
* Generate scope for block.
In VHDL, the design hierarchy includes the following scopes:
* Instance (root, component, or package).
* Subprogram (procedure and function).
* Block.
* Generate (if-generate, for-generate, or case-generate).

hierarchy.

"npi_nl_hier_trv_reset_cb" traverses the design hierarchy and execute the callback
functions registered by the user.
All the APIs in this category are written based on the NPI Language Model and NPI Netlist

The Signal Library provides the APIs that are related to the design information of a signal
(variable or net). In general, the APIs can be classified into the following groups:
1. Trace the driver or load of a signal based on the NPI Language Model and NPI Netlist
2. Get the equivalent signals of a target signal.
3. Get the signal definition typespec of a target signal.
Driver/Load Tracing
The APIs with the prefix "npi_sv_trace" mean they function as tracing the driver or load of
a signal based on the NPI Language (SystemVerilog) Model.
The APIs with the prefix "npi_nl_trace" mean they function as tracing the driver or load of a
signal based on the NPI Netlist Model.
Equivalent Signals
The API "npi_get_equivalent_signal" obtains the net handles that are equivalent to the
target signal.
The two signals are defined as "equivalent" if they are only connected by the port/instport
of the module instances (for example, an instance whose cell type is npiNlModuleCell).
Signal Definition Typespec
The API "npi_get_signal_define_typespec" obtains the typespec handle that represents
the definition of the signal.
The API is written based on the NPI Language Model.

Limitations
1. All the APIs for tracing the drivers or loads of a signal based on NPI Language Model
does not work when the specified signal is located at the index or slice of a reference
module mm(ref bit ma);
bit [1:0] a;
mm m0(a[p]); // m0 port ma's higher connection a[p] that is a
ref-obj,
endmodule // if tracing p's load, a[p] is not shown in the results.

Description of Network Trace
Trace Network APIs are based on Netlist models. It contains three parts:
1. Trace network and generate network graph under user-specified criteria.
2. Report path according to current graph.
3. Clear network, delete whole graph. The first part is flexible. You can start tracing from a
port or a signal.
The endpoint can also be an instance or a signal. Some options support wildcard
patterns. In addition, you can set different properties.
Complexity of the graph by detail mode.
Stop condition when tracing.
Ports that you particularly want to observe( = link ports).
It also reports floating signals, constant-tied signals, and ports of top boundary
module.
Detail Mode Setting
By default, 0, the network graph contains the start ports and end ports, both sides of ports
of mapping module, link ports that you want to observe, the stop ports or instports and
literal net that meet the stop conditions.
1. Adding all past ports of module into the graph.
2. Adding all instports of instance from symbol library.

3. Adding all past ports of module, and the past instports from the passCellFile into the
graph.
Figure 52

Detail Mode Setting

There are a bunch of stop conditions for this system. You can specify the cell type of
instance that can be passed through, either with positive listing or negative listing. You can
also specify the module names that you want to stop tracing.
To prevent loop and complexity of the graph, it does not pass through flip-flops, and a
maximum tracing depth is also specified.
Further, a module ports mapping can be given to prevent tracing too deep into modules. It
simply jumps from input port to the corresponding output port while tracing.
The following section covers the map file mapping rules:
Basic Mapping Rules
Map file:
modName portA portB
1. If trace to portA, it maps to portB.
2. If trace to a bit portA[idx], it maps to portB[idx].
3. If trace to slice portA[lidx,ridx], it maps to slice portB[lidx:ridx]. (For example, portA [1:0]
maps to portB[1:0]).
4. If output port not existed, it stops tracing at input port and the port is listed in the result
5. If portB has size = 1, then any part of portA maps to portB. (for example, both portA[1]
and portA[1:0] maps to portB).

Extended Mapping Rules
Map file:
modName portA portB
modName portA[0] portB[2]
If trace to portA, it maps to portB.
If trace to portA[0], it maps to portB[2]. Since the map relation is specified.
If trace to portA[1], maps to portB[1] according to basic mapping rules.
Map file:
modName portA portB
modName portA[0] portB
If trace to portA, it maps to portB.
If trace to port portA[0], maps to portB. Since the map relation is specified.
If trace to port portA[1], maps to portB[1] according to basic mapping rules.
Map file:
modName portA portB[1]
If trace to portA, it maps to portB[1].
If trace to portA[idx], maps to portB[1].
If trace to portA[lidx:ridx], maps to portB[1].
The map is bidirectional. portB maps to portA, and the spec is also applicable.

setenv NPI_NL_TRACE_DUMP_STATUS 1 - Dump tracing status information.
setenv NPI_NL_TRACE_REG_PASS_DQ 1

Pass register from D to Q and reverse. You must be careful with this option because this
might increase the graph complexity significantly.

The Netlist Library provides some commonly used APIs written based on the NPI Netlist
Obtain Handles (npiNlHandle) by nl_name
Since the NPI Netlist Model regards the design as a netlist after inference, the objects
in the Netlist model might have its specific name, which might not be their names in the
design source code.
In the Netlist model, the object name "nl_name" is called. The "nl_name" can be obtained
from the property npiNlName for that handle.
However, if you dump the nl_name into a file, it is difficult to recover the handle directly
from the nl_name.
To overcome the difficulties described above, the Netlist Library provides the following
APIs to get the handles from the nl_name:
* npi_nl_inst_handle_by_nl_name
* npi_nl_port_handle_by_nl_name
* npi_nl_instport_handle_by_nl_name
* npi_nl_net_handle_by_nl_name
As the names suggest, these APIs can obtain the handles from the nl_name and therefore
users can continue with their applications with the handles.
Obtain Signal Handles (npiNlHandle) by Signal Hierarchical Name
To provide more flexibility in developing applications using the NPI Netlist model, the API
npi_nl_sig_handle_by_name allows you to obtain a net handle based on the input signal
hierarchical name.
Unlike the API npi_nl_handle_by_name that can only obtain npiNlDeclNet object, the
string input for npi_nl_sig_handle_by_name can be a signal hierarchical name or an
instance port name of library cell.
Moreover, index or range information is allowed for getting a slice of net object. For the
more detailed information, refer to npi_nl_sig_handle_by_name.
Obtain Connected Handles by net/instport/port Object
The connection relationship in the NPI Netlist model can be very complex, the following
APIs provide a simple way to get the connected object by the specified objects.
* npi_nl_instport_2_port

* npi_nl_port_instport_2_net

The NPI VANL Library provides some C-APIs and Tcl interfaces written based on the NPI
Netlist Model and the NPI Netlist Library.
The NPI VANL Library can be seen as Netlist Model + Value on ports and inst ports. Thus,
despite those basic APIs which focus on value propagation, it also provides APIs related
to the design information of a signal like Signal Library and APIs that can identify the
connected components from a signal like Connection Library.
The difference between Netlist and VANL tracing is that the VANL Library traces driver or
load or fan-in or fan-out in an active way, so called "Active Trace".

You can trace driver or load with value, and find the possible signals that cause the value
change of the target signal, or conversely find the signals affected by the target signal. For
more information about Active Trace, see Rules for Active Trace.

Rules for Active Trace
When tracing an active driver/load from output/input pins of instances, different rules are
applied for different npiNlInstType
This section introduces the rules for Active Trace of every supported instance.

NPI VANL provides "Active Trace" functionality, which is a way to trace driver or load with
value. Active trace only happens when tracing driver from an instance output or tracing
load from an instance input.
It considers its npiNlCellType and the values of its inputs and outputs. You can trace
active drivers and then conveniently find the possible signals which are the root cause to
the value change of the target signal.
On the contrary, you can trace active loads whose values are mainly or partially affected
by the target signal.
The relationship between active driver and active load is mutual. If A and B are the active
drivers of O, then O must be the active load of A and B.
Rules for User Set Signals
Since VANL Library is based on NPI Netlist Model, user can set or define values on
npiNlNet, npiNlInstPort, and npiNlPort.
The user-defined or user-set signals are "value-tied" and they do not change their values
until user cleans or resets them. More importantly, they do NOT have any active driver.
For example, as shown in the figure below, if you set the value on npiNlNet top.a and
npiNlPort top.b (marked as blue words) and you try to recursively get the active drivers
from npiNlNet top.o after evaluation, you have npiNlInstport before npiNlNet top.a
(pointed out by the black arrow) and npiNlPort top.b, if their values formed the value of
npiNlNet top.o.

Rules for npiNlSymbolLibInst
For npiNlSymbolLibInst, extract its npiNlFunc, npiNlXFunc, and npiNlThreeStateFunc.
According to these function-strings, the active drivers can be evaluated.
FN04D2 oai2 (ZN, A1, A2, B1, B2)

npiNlFunc:
!((A1&A2)|(B1&B2))

When A1=1, A2=0, B1=0, and B2=1, the active drivers of ZN are A2 and B1 because
the value of output ZN is caused by its input (A1&A2) = 0 and (B1&B2) = 0, which are
caused by A2 and B1 respectively.
Rules for npiNlUDPLibInst
For npiNlUDPInst, NPI VANL extracts its table entry, and then finds the first case matched
with the current input values. NPI VANL treats the UDP symbol "?" as a "don't care bit",

Schematic

This program recursively traces the driver with value and the value of each signal after
propagation is shown in the preceding Schematic.
At first stage, you want to trace active driver recursively from top.w1. The active driver of
top.w1 would be top.w2 and top.w3 is dropped because the value of top.w1 is X, and
the possible driver to cause this is only top.w2 with value X.
Due to similar reason, the active driver of top.w2 would be top.w7 and top.w9, since the
value X of top.w2 is caused by mux input top.w7 and the control pin top.w9, which are X
and 1, respectively.
Since the value on net is set in this example, on tracing you get
npiNlInstport top.top:Always0SigOp0:2:2:Mux.CH_w9 and
top.top:Always0SigOp0:2:2:Mux.IH_w7 before those net.
Secondly, user traces the active driver of top.w3, the output of an npiNlOrCell, with value
1.
The possible drivers that caused this 1 are signals whose value is also 1, thus get top.w5
and top.w6.
Since the value on net is set in this example, thus when tracing you
get npiNlInstPort top.top:Always1SigOp1:3:3:Or.IH_w5 and
top.top:Always1SigOp1:3:3:Or.IH_w6 before those net.

User Interface and Use Flow
The following figure shows the flow of using NPI Transaction Writer APIs:

Firstly, the new instance of the npi_tr_writer class needs to be created with the provided
instance path. The instance path specifies the scope to which all the objects created
through this instance belong.
Secondly, you can create any objects by the APIs of writer instance.
It is allowed to have multiple writer instances to dump the objects into the
same FSDB file, so the objects under different paths appear in one FSDB file
accordingly.
The relationship with another object can be set through the related relationship APIs. In
this model, there are two main relationships:
* Parent and child (children).
* Predecessor and successor (successors).

The two objects belonging to two different writer instances can be set as predecessor and
successor (successors) by calling the corresponding APIs and specifying the successor's
writer instance.
The attributes with different values and data types can be added. The allowed data types
are bit, bit vector, integer, real (double), time (64 bits unsigned integer), and string.
You can also set the expected attribute and if the attribute is not equal to the expected
attribute, it is highlighted in Protocol Analyzer.
To end an object creation, theend_object() method can be used for a specified object.
The ended object cannot be modified after it ends using this API.
To end all of the not ended objects, the flush_writer() API can be used, which ends all the
objects and dumps them into the FSDB file.

Illegal Cases for Object ID
The object ID is defined as const char*.
The following are some illegal cases for the provided object ID:
* The NULL pointer is provided.
* The object ID is not created by the create_object() API.
An error message is issued if these conditions are violated and the API that calls these
illegal cases becomes invalid.

The following is an example showing how to use npiSocketClient to connect to a server

In the program, a process is forked to invoke the Novas executable. Then a

<unistd.h>

void abortCB(void* cbData)
{
printf("Socket connection is broken\n");
}
{

// 1. get free port
int port = npi_socket_client_get_free_port();
if( !npi_socket_client_is_port_free(port) ) {
printf("Error. Fail to get a free port.\n");
}
// 2. invoke novas executable
pid_t pid = fork();
if( pid<0 ) {
printf("Error. Fail to fork a process to invoke Novas.\n");
}
if(pid == 0) { //child process
// the argument argc and argv is the options of Novas executable
// to invoke Novas with a port, we need to run Novas by the commands
below:
//
// novas -serverPort <free_port> <original_novas_load_design_options>
int new_argc = argc + 3;
char** new_argv = (char**) malloc(sizeof(char*)*new_argc);
// set the argument : novas -serverPort <free_port>
new_argv[0] = "novas";
new_argv[1] = "-serverPort";
static char buf[256];
sprintf(buf, "%d", port);
new_argv[2] = buf;
// keep original novas load design options except argv[0], which is
the executable name
for(int i=1; i<argc; i++) {

Argument Parser
The npiArg APIs are used to facilitate processing the arguments passed into a C program
(argv). In npiArg, argv arguments are defined as a set of attributes with their associated
values.
An attribute is a string beginning with a minus (-) or plus (+). Anything that follows an
attribute before another attribute begins are the values associated with the preceding
npiArg APIs provide routines to get, add, or remove attributes as well their associated
values.

Parse User-Defined Arguments in NPI C/C++ Programming
In the introduction to Use NPI Libraries in C/C++, the use of an NPI program is similar to
the following:
%> my_NPI_program.exe <novas import design options> <NPI options> <user
options>

To parse <user options> in the NPI program, npiArg can be a very convenient utility. For
example, assume an NPI program needs the user options "-input_signal signal_name".
%> my_npi_program.exe -f run.f -path ./Design -input_signal
"system.i_cpu.i_ALUB.carry_mode"

The following code snippet shows how to use npiArg to parse such a user option:

include "npi_util.h" // for npiArg
{
// parse the user options by npiUSN
int new_argc = 0;
char** new_argv = NULL;
string input_signal;
npiArg arg = npi_arg_construct(argc, argv);
if( npi_arg_has_attr(arg, "-input_signal") ) { // parse the attribute
"-input_signal"
// record the signal name specified in the "-input_signal" attribute
input_signal = npi_arg_attr_get_value(arg, "-input_signal",
1/*position*/);
// remove the "-input_signal" attribute and output new_argc and new_argv
for npi_init()
npi_arg_remove_attr(arg, "-input_signal");
new_argc = npi_arg_get_argc(arg);
new_argv = npi_arg_get_argv(arg);
}
printf("ERROR. Fail to find the argument \"-input_signal\"\n");
}
// now you can pass new_argc and new_argv to npi_init()
if( !npi_init(new_argc, new_argv) )

// close the npiArg
npi_arg_destroy(arg);
}

As shown in the above code snippets, npiArg can be used to retrieve the values of userdefined arguments while leaving the other arguments for npi_init() and npi_load_design()
alone.

Universal Scope Name
npiUSN is used to create a Universal Scope Name representation for hierarchical scopes
in SystemVerilog and VHDL.
As different tools have their own convention for SystemVerilog and VHDL scope names,
the npiUSN APIs convert different scope representations into a unified format thus making
it easier to use the scopes in NPI.
SystemVerilog and VHDL escape names are handled automatically.
typedef void* npiUSN

The npiUSN handle. (used in C/C++).

npi_usn_construct

Construct a npiUSN handle with a hierarchical string and a
delimiter.

npi_usn_destroy

Destroy a npiUSN handle.

npi_usn_push_back

Append a scope to the end of a npiUSN handle.

npi_usn_pop_back

Remove the last scope from a npiUSN handle.

npi_usn_back

Get the last scope name of a npiUSN handle.

npi_usn_set_delimiter

Change the delimiter of a npiUSN handle.

npi_usn_delimiter

Get the current delimiter of a npiUSN handle.

npi_usn_is_empty

Check whether any scopes exist for a npiUSN handle.

npi_usn_number

Get the total number of scopes of a npiUSN handle.

npi_usn_scope_name
_at

Get the scope name at the specified position of a npiUSN

npi_usn_middle_name Get the middle scope name of a npiUSN handle.
npi_usn_hierarchy_n
ame

Get the full hierarchical name of a npiUSN handle.

Use npiUSN in C/C++ Programming
Include "npi_util.h" in your C/C++ program when using npiUSN.

The following example demonstrates how to manipulate SystemVerilog and VHDL scopes
using npiUSN.

// header for npiUSN

{
// construct a npiUSN handle for a string : "System.TOP.i_CPU.i_ALUB"
char* hier_name = "System.TOP.i_CPU.i_ALUB";
char delimiter = '.';
npiUSN usn_hdl = npi_usn_construct(hier_name, delimiter);
// iterate every scopes and print to stdout
printf("== Dump the scope information ==\n");
int scope_num = npi_usn_number(usn_hdl);
for (int i=0; i<scope_num; i++) {
printf("Scope(%d) = \"%s\"\n", i, npi_usn_scope_name_at(usn_hdl, i));
}
// remove the last scope
npi_usn_pop_back(usn_hdl);

// Hierarchy becomes: "System.TOP.i_CPU"

// get the last scope
char* last_scope = npi_usn_back(usn_hdl);
printf("Last scope = %s\n", last_scope); //Last scope = i_CPU
// add the last scope "i_CCU.i_MODE"
npi_usn_push_back(usn_hdl, "i_CCU"); // Hierarchy becomes:
"System.TOP.i_CPU.i_CCU"
npi_usn_push_back(usn_hdl, "i_MODE"); // Hierarchy becomes:
"System.TOP.i_CPU.i_CCU.i_MODE"
// get the middle scope i_CPU.i_CCU : from scope 2 to scope 3
char* middle_name = npi_usn_middle_name(usn_hdl, 2, 3);
printf("Middle name = \"%s\"\n", middle_name); // Middle name:
"i_CPU.i_CCU"
// change the delimiter from '.' to '/'
npi_usn_set_delimiter(usn_hdl, '/');
printf("Current delimiter is %c\n", npi_usn_delimiter(usn_hdl));
// print the full hierarchy name
char* full_name = npi_usn_hierarchy_name(usn_hdl);
printf("After scope manipulation, now hierarchy is: \"%s\"\n",
full_name);
// remove all scopes

while( !npi_usn_is_empty(usn_hdl) ) {
npi_usn_pop_back(usn_hdl);
}
// destroy the npiUSN handle
npi_usn_destroy(usn_hdl);
}

Identify the connected high-connection signals from the ports of an instance.
Get the high-connected expression handle of each port of the specified instance, and find
all signals in each expression and collect them into a specified map (C++) or array (Tcl).
Refer to npi_ut_is_signal for the definition of a signal.

int npi_inst_port_2_high_conn_sig ( char* inst_hier_name,
hdl2hdlVecPairVec_t& port_2_sig_pair_vec );

port_2_sig_pair_vec

Specify a STL vector of the pair port handle and high connected signal handles.
The first element of each pair is the port handle of a target instance, and the second
element is a STL vector of handle.
The handle vector contains all the signal handles of high-connection.

{
hdl2hdlVecPairVec_t portSigPairVec;
hdl2hdlVecPairVec_t::iterator it;
npi_inst_port_2_high_conn_sig("TOP.inst", portSigPairVec);
for (it = portSigPairVec.begin(); it != portSigPairVec.end(); it++)
{
npi_sv_ut_dump_hdl_info((*it).first, stdout);
npi_release_handle((*it).first);
npi_sv_ut_dump_hdl_vec_info((*it).second/*IO*/, stdout);
}
}

Delay Control
Object Type: npiDmDelayControl

Delay control means that if a procedural assignment following the delay control is delayed
in its execution with respect to the procedural statement preceding the delay control by the
specified delay.
Delay control belongs to the class of the atomic statement.

reg reset, r1;
always /* process always */
100 /* delay control statement*/
begin: BLK /* named begin-end */
if(reset)
r1 = 0;
r1 = 1 1;
end

* Apply method "npiDmDelay" to the handle "#100 begin: BLK end", and the
npiDmConstant handle "100" is returned.
* Apply method "npiDmStmt" to the handle "#100 begin: BLK end", and the
npiDmNamedBegin handle "begin: BLK" is returned.

Disable
Object Type: npiDmDisable

Disable provides the ability to terminate the activity associated with concurrently active
processes, while maintaining the structured nature of procedural descriptions.
Disable belongs to the class of the atomic statement.

disable blk_n; /* npiDmDisable */
end

Apply method "npiDmExpr" to the handle "disable blk_n", and the npiDmNamedBegin
handle "blk_n" is returned.

Do-while
Object Type: npiDmDoWhile

Do-while is a kind of loop statement. It executes a statement first and tests its control
expression at the end of the loop.

The loop stops until do-while's control expression becomes false. Do-while belongs to the
class of the atomic statement.

do
// do while statement
begin : fff
x = x - 1;
if (x > 5) begin
end
end
while (x > 0);
return x + 10;
end

* Apply method "npiDmCondition" to the handle "do-while", and the npiDmOperation
handle "x > 0" is returned.
* Apply method "npiDmStmt" to the handle "do-while", and the npiDmNamedBegin
handle "begin: fff" is returned.

Object Type: npiDmEvent

Event means the SystemVerilog event construct.

event ev; /*npiDmEvent*/
event evAry1 [3:0]; /*npiDmEvent*/
event evAry2 [1:0][2:0]; /*npiDmEvent*/
task too( ref event task_e /*npiDmEvent*/ );

Apply property "npiDmTaskFuncArgument" to the handle "task_e", and "1" is returned.

Event Control
Object Type: npiDmEventControl

Event control means that the execution of a procedural statement is synchronized with a
value change on a net or variable or the occurrence of a declared event.
Event control belongs to the class of the atomic statement.

reg clk, reset, r1;
always @(posedge clk or negedge reset) /* event control */
begin: BLK
if(!reset)
r1 = 0;
r1 = 1 1;
end

* Apply method "npiDmCondition" to the handle "event control", and the npiDmOperation
handle "posedge clk or negedge reset" is returned.
* Apply method "npiDmStmt" to the handle "event control", and the npiDmNamedBegin
handle "begin: BLK" is returned.

Object Type: npiDmEventStmt

Event statement means an event triggering statement. The blocking event is triggered
using the -> operator, and the non-blocking event is triggered using the ->> operator.
Event statement belongs to the class of the atomic statement.

event e2;
->e1; /* npiDmEventStmt_1 */
->>e2; /* npiDmEventStmt_2 */
end

Simple expression is a class composed of net, variable, parameter, and interface

Constant means SystemVerilog constant literals or values such as "3'b001".
Operation is a construct that combines operands with operators such as "a[0]" or "{a, b}".
Property "npiDmConstType" returns npiDmConstType_e.
Property "npiDmOpType" returns npiDmOpType_e.
Property "npiDmDataType" returns npiDmDataType_e.

npiDmOpTypeStreamLR operations.

For
Object Type: npiDmFor

For is a kind of loop statement. It consists of one or more initial statements, a control
expression, one or more step statements, and a statement which is executed every time
the control expression return true.
For belongs to the class of the scope and the atomic statement.
Only for statements containing variable declarations as part of the for-initialization
assignment create implicit begin-end block around the for-loop.
The block creates a new hierarchy scope, making the variables local to the loop scope.
Therefore, the proerty npiDmLocalVarDecls is used to decide whether a for statement is a

parameter int SIZE = 256;
integer index=0;
function myfunc;
for(index=0; index<SIZE; index=index+1) /* for statement */
begin: ggg
$display("aaa");
end
myfunc = 1;

* Apply method "npiDmForInitStmt" to the handle "for", and the npiDmAssignment handle
"index=0" is returned.

"index<SIZE" is returned.

"index=index+1" is returned.

"begin: ggg" is returned.
* Apply property "npiDmLocalVarDecls" to handle "for", and "0" is returned.

Forever
Object Type: npiDmForever

Forever is a kind of loop statement. It continuously executes a statement. It belongs to the
class of the atomic statement.

forever CYCLE clk = ~clk; /* forever */
end

Apply method "npiDmStmt" to the handle "forever", and the npiDmDelayControl handle
"#CYCLE clk = ~clk is returned.

Generate Block
Object Type: npiDmGenBlock

Generate block is a collection of one or more module items. It is either conditionally or
multiply instantiated in generate constructs.

A generate block might not contain port declarations, parameter declarations, specify
blocks or specparam declarations. All other modules items, including other generate
constructs, are allowed in a generate block.
* A generate construct must contain a generate block in DM model.
* A generate block is not a scope only if (1) it is within a conditionally generate
construct, (2) it has no begin-end keyword, and (3) it only contains another
conditionally generate construct.
* If a generate block's name is explicitly named, the property
"npiDmImplicitDecl" returns 0. Otherwise, this property returns 1.

Object Types: Generate-case Construct (npiDmGenCase), Generate-case Item

Generate-case construct belongs to the conditional generate construct, which instantiates
at most one generate block from a set of alternative generate blocks.
Generate-case item is a handle that consists of a condition expression and a generate
block. The generate block within generate-case item represents a scenario of the
generate-case branches.
When generate-case item has no expression after applying method npiDmExpr,
it is a "default" generate-case item.

case(p) /* npiDmGenCase_1 */
1'b0: /* npiDmGenCaseItem_1 */

end

Generate Construct
Object Types: npiDmGenConstruct

Generate constructs are used to either conditionally or multiply instantiate generate blocks
into a model. They are if-generate, if-else-generate, case-generate and for-generate
constructs.
The if-generate, if-else-generate and case-generate constructs instantiate at most one
generate block from a set of alternative generate blocks. They belong to conditionally
generate constructs.
The for-generate construct allow a single generate block to be instantiated into a model
multiple times. It belongs to loop generate construct.

title: 1 01; /*npiDmContAssign*/
text:
for (i = 0; i < 2; i++ ) /* npiDmGenFor_1 */
begin : u1
end
if (p == 1) /* npiDmGenIf_1 */
end
if (p == 0) /* npiDmGenIfElse_1 */
end

Generate-for Construct
Object Types: npiDmGenFor

Generate-for construct belongs to the loop generate construct, which instantiates a single
generate block into a model multiple times.
It consists of one initial statement, a control expression, one step statement, and a
generate block which is instantiated every time the control expression return true.

title: 1 01; /*npiDmContAssign*/
text:
module top; /* npiDmModule_1 */
genvar i; /* npiDmGenVar_1 */
for (i = 0; i < 2; i++ ) /* npiDmGenFor_1 */
begin : u1 /* npiDmGenBlock_1 */
end
for(genvar j = 0; j < 2; j++ ) /*npiDmGenFor_2, npiDmGenVar_2*/

Object Types: Generate-if Construct (npiDmGenIf), Generate-if-else Item
(npiDmGenIfElse)

Generate-if and generate-if-else constructs belong to the conditional generate construct,
which instantiates at most one generate block from a set of alternative generate blocks.

if (p == 1) /* npiDmGenIf_1 */
begin : u1 /* npiDmGenBlock_1 */
end
if (p == 0) /* npiDmGenIfElse_1 */
begin : v1 /* npiDmGenBlock_2 */
end

end

Genvar
Object Types: npiDmGenVar

Genvar is an integer during elaboration to evaluate the generate loop but it does not exist
at simulation time. It is not referenced anywhere other than in a loop generate scheme.
If a genvar has already been used as an index variable in an outer loop, it cannot be used
as an index variable in an inner loop.

module top; /* npiDmModule_1 */
genvar i; /* npiDmGenVar_1 */
for (i = 0; i < 2; i++ ) /*npiDmGenFor_1, npiDmGenBlock_1*/
for (genvar j = 0; j < 4; j++) /* npiDmGenFor_2, npiDmGenVar_2 */

Object Type: Hierarchical Reference (npiDmHierRef), Reference (npiDmRef)

There are several meaning for Hierarchical Reference in the DM model as follows:
* SystemVerilog hierarchial reference which accesses external scope object.
* SystemVerilog struct or union member access.
* SystemVerilog interface member access by interface port reference.
* SystemVerilog built-in method call of object.
The Reference is the segment of Hierarachical Reference. It contains the information of bit
select of part select and the actual object.

If, If-else
Object Type: If (npiDmIf), If-else (npiDmIfElse)

If and if-else are conditional statements. They are used to make a decision about whether
a statement is executed.
If and if-else belong to the class of the atomic statement.

reg a, b, x, y, z;
if ( a & b ) /*npiDmIf*/
x = y;
if ( a | b ) /*npiDmIfElse*/
x = ~y;
x = z;
end

* Apply method "npiDmElseStmt" to the handle "if-else", and the npiDmAssignment

Instance, Port Instance, Parameter Instance
Object Type: Instance (npiDmInstance), Port Instance (npiDmPortInst), Parameter
Instance (npiDmParamInst)

Instance means the SystemVerilog instance construct of a module or an interface.
Port Instance is the connection to the port. Parameter Instance is the connection to the
parameter.
The left index of the instance array is accessed by the method "npiDmLeft".
The right index of the instance array is accessed by the method "npiDmRight".
If the instance array has only one index such as "m i0 [1] ();", the index is accessed by the
method "npiDmLeft".
The instance in the bind construct which is not a real instance. The instance has no
real parameter and port connections. Apply the property "npiDmBindInst" to check if the
instance is in the bind. Any manipulation on the bind instance is not allowed.

bind top mm ( 3/*npiDmParamInst*/, 4 /*npiDmParamInst*/ )
b1 /*npiDmInstance*/
( w5/*npiDmPortInst*/, w6/*npiDmPortInst*/ );
module m();

parameter P1, P2;

Wait is a statement that can delay a procedural statement until a condition become true.

text:
* On applying the "npiDmVhExpr" method to the npiDmVhConst handle "OP_CODES3",
the npiDmVhAggregate handle is returned.
* On applying the "npiDmVhAssocElem" method to the npiDmVhAggregate handle,
three npiDmVhAssocElem handles are returned:
* On applying the "npiDmVhChoices" method to the first npiDmVhAssocElem handle,
the npiDmVhIntLiteral handles "2" and "1" is returned.
* On applying the "npiDmVhExpr" method to the first npiDmVhAssocElem handle, the
npiDmVhEnumLiteral handle '1' is returned.
* On applying the "npiDmVhChoices" method to the second npiDmVhAssocElem
handle, the npiDmVhIntLiteral handle "5" is returned.
* On applying the "npiDmVhExpr" method to the second npiDmVhAssocElem handle,
the npiDmVhEnumLiteral handle '1' is returned.
* On applying the "npiDmVhChoices" method to the third npiDmVhAssocElem handle,
the npiDmVhOthers handle is returned.
* On applying the "npiDmVhExpr" method to the second npiDmVhAssocElem handle,
the npiDmVhEnumLiteral handle '0' is returned.

The "npiDmVhIsNamed" property returns 1 if the choices are specified.

Vh Expr
Object Type: Vh Name, Vh Literal, npiDmVhQualExpr, npiDmVhTypeConv,
npiDmVhAggregate, npiDmVhLoopIndex, npiDmVhFuncCall, npiDmVhOperation

Vh Expr is a class composed of Vh Name, Vh Literal, Type
Qualification(npiDmVhQualExpr), Type Conversion(npiDmVhTypeConv),
Aggregate(npiDmVhAggregate), Loop Index(npiDmVhLoopIndex), Function
Call(npiDmVhFuncCall), and Operation(npiDmVhOperation).

entity sub is
port (oo: out BIT);
architecture arch_sub of sub is

use IEEE.std_logic_arith.all;
port (oo: out bit_vector(0 to 3));
-- type qualification (npiDmVhQualExpr) is used in default expression
of C9
constant C9: std_logic_vector(0 to 4) := std_logic_vector'("XU-1H");
-- type conversion (npiDmVhTypeConv) is used in default expression of
C10
constant C10: std_ulogic_vector(5 to 9) := std_ulogic_vector(C9);
constant Delay1: TIME := 1 ms;
-- default expression of Delay2 is npiDmVhOperation
constant Delay2: TIME := 2 * Delay1;
function init_func(x: std_logic_vector) return integer is
return x'length;
-- default expression of CNT is npiDmVhFuncCall
constant CNT: integer := init_func("1100");
component sub
port (oo: out BIT);
-- I is npiDmVhLoopIndex
gfor:for I in 0 to 3 generate
gfsub: sub generic map(I)
port map(oo(I));

* On applying the "npiDmVhExpr" method to the npiDmVhConst handle "C9", and the
npiDmVhQualExpr handle is returned.
* On applying the "npiDmVhType" method to the npiDmVhQualExpr handle, the
npiDmVhArrayType handle "std_logic_vector" is returned.
* On applying the "npiDmVhExpr" method to the npiDmVhQualExpr handle, the
npiDmVhAggregate handle, where the expression of element association is "XU-1H",
* On applying the "npiDmVhExpr" method to the npiDmVhConst handle "C10", the
npiDmVhTypeConv handle is returned.
* On applying the "npiDmVhType" method to the npiDmVhTypeConv handle, the
npiDmVhSubType handle, which is the type of "C9", is returned.

* On applying the "npiDmVhExpr" method to the npiDmVhTypeConv handle, the
npiDmVhConst handle "C9" is returned.
* On applying the "npiDmVhExpr" method to the npiDmVhConst handle "Delay2", the
npiDmVhOperation handle with npiDmVhOpMul property is returned.
* On applying the "npiDmVhExpr" method to the npiDmVhOperation handle, the
npiDmVhIntLiteral handle "2" and the npiDmVhConst handle "Delay1" is returned.
* On applying the "npiDmVhExpr" method to the npiDmVhConst handle "CNT", the
npiDmVhFuncCall handle "init_func" is returned.
* On applying the "npiDmVhLoopIndex" method to the npiDmVhGenFor handle "gfor",
the npiDmVhLoopIndex handle "I" is returned.

The "npiDmOpType" property returns npiDmOpType_e.

Vh Attr
Object Type: npiDmVhAttrDecl, npiDmVhAttrSpec

An attribute is a value, function, type, range, signal, or constant that might be associated
with one or more named entities in a description. There are two categories of attributes:
predefined and user-defined.
An attribute specification associates a user-defined attribute with one or more named
entities and defines the value of that attribute for those entities. The attribute specification
is said to decorate the named entity.

constant Delay: TIME := 1 ms;
attribute Pin_code of Delay: constant is 1; -- npiDmVhAttrSpec

* On applying the "npiDmVhType" method to the npiDmVhAttrDecl handle "Pin_code",
the npiDmVhSubType handle "POSITIVE" is returned.
* On applying the "npiDmVhExpr" method to the npiDmVhAttrSpec handle "PIN_CODE",
the npiDmVhIntLiteral handle "1" is returned.
* On applying the "npiDmVhEntDesignator" method to the npiDmVhAttrSpec handle
"PIN_CODE", the npiDmVhConst handle "Delay" is returned.

Vh Stmt
Object Type: npiDmVhStmt

Vh Stmt is a class composed of Concurrent Statement (Vh Conc Stmt) and Sequential
Statement (Vh Seq Stmt).

function init_func(x: integer) return integer is
variable ret: integer;
if_stmt: if (x > 256) then -- npiDmVhIf
ret := 1;
else -- npiDmVhElse
ret := 0;
ret_stmt: return ret; -- npiDmVhReturn
ssa: oo <= '1'; -- npiDmVhSimpleSigAssign

* On applying the "npiDmVhStmt" method to the npiDmVhArchitecture handle "rtl", the
npiDmVhSimpleSigAssign handle "ssa" is returned.
* On applying the "npiDmVhUpperStmt" to the npiDmVhSimpleSigAssign handle "ssa",
the npiDmVhArchitecture handle "rtl" is returned.
* On applying the "npiDmVhScope" method to the npiDmVhSimpleSigAssign handle
"ssa", the npiDmVhArchitecture handle "rtl" is returned.
* On applying the "npiDmVhStmt" method to the npiDmVhFunction handle "init_func",
the npiDmVhIf handle "if_stmt" and the npiDmVhReturn handle "ret_stmt" are
* On applying the "npiDmVhUpperStmt" method to the npiDmVhReturn handle
"ret_stmt", the npiDmVhFunction handle "init_func" is returned.
* On applying the "npiDmVhScope" method to the npiDmVhReturn handle "ret_stmt",
the npiDmVhFunction handle "init_func" is returned.
* On applying the "npiDmVhBranch" method to the npiDmVhIf handle "if_stmt", the
npiDmVhElse handle is returned.

Object Type: npiDmVhBlock, npiDmVhProcess, npiDmVhConcProcCall,

Vh Conc Stmt is a class composed of Block(npiDmVhBlock), Process(npiDmVhProcess),

Instance(npiDmVhInstance), and Generate Statement (Vh Generate).

oo: out std_logic_vector(1 downto 0));

signal op_code: std_logic_vector(3 downto 0) := "0000";
component sub
procedure check(signal P1, P2: BIT) is
ssa: P1 <= '1'; -- npiDmVhSimpleSigAssign
constant size: integer := 256;
bk: block (cin = '1') -- npiDmVhBlock
end block bk;
inst: sub generic map(16) -- npiDmVhInstance
port map(oo => oo(0));
-- npiDmVhGenIf (npiDmVhGenerate)
gif_inst: sub generic map(cv)
port map(oo(1));
conc_proc_call: check(P1, P2); -- npiDmVhConcProcCall
fail: assert op_code = "0000" -- npiDmVhConcAssert
report "Illegal Code of Operation" -- report is not supported
severity FAILURE; -- severity is not supported

On applying the "npiDmVhStmt" method to the npiDmVhArchitecture handle "arch_top",
the following handles are returned:
* npiDmVhSimpleSigAssign handle "ssa"
* npiDmVhProcess handle "prcs"
* npiDmVhBlock handle "bk"
* npiDmVhInstance handle "inst"
* npiDmVhGenIf handle "gif"

* npiDmVhConcProcCall handle "check"
* npiDmVhConcAssert handle "fail"

The "npiDmVhLabelName" property returns the label name of a statement.
* "ssa", "prcs", "bk", "inst", "gif", "conc_proc_call" and "fail" are label names.

variable cnt: integer := 2;
variable quota: integer := 0;
variable day: WEEK_DAY := MON;
-- npiDmVhIf
cond1: if (cnt > 1) and (cnt < 5) then
va0: cnt := cnt + 2; -- npiDmVhVarAssign
elsif cnt = 0 then -- npiDmVhElsif
va1: cnt := cnt + 1; -- npiDmVhVarAssign
else -- npiDmVhElse
va2: cnt := 0; -- npiDmVhVarAssign
-- npiDmVhCase
cond2: case day is
when TUE to WED | FRI => quota := 50; -- npiDmVhCaseItem
when others => quota := 75; -- npiDmVhDefaultCaseItem

On applying the "npiDmVhStmt" method to the npiDmVhProcess handle "prcs", the
npiDmVhIf handle "cond1" and the npiDmVhCase handle "cond2" are returned.
* npiDmVhIf handle "cond1"
On applying the "npiDmVhCondition" method to the npiDmVhIf handle "cond1", the
npiDmVhOperation handle, which is "(cnt > 1) and (cnt < 5)" is returned.
On applying the "npiDmVhStmt" method to the npiDmVhIf handle "cond1", the
npiDmVhVarAssign handle "va0" is returned.
On applying the "npiDmVhBranch" method to the npiDmVhIf handle "cond1", the
following handles are returned:

On applying the "npiDmVhUpperStmt" method to the npiDmVhElsif handle, the
npiDmVhIf handle "cond1" is returned.
On applying the "npiDmVhCondition" method to the npiDmVhElsif handle, the
npiDmVhOperation handle, which is "cnt = 0" is returned.

On applying the "npiDmVhStmt" method to the npiDmVhElsif handle, the
npiDmVhVarAssign handle "va1" is returned.
npiDmVhElse handle
On applying the "npiDmVhUpperStmt" method to the npiDmVhElse handle, the
npiDmVhIf handle "cond1" is returned.
On applying the "npiDmVhStmt" method to the npiDmVhElse handle, the
npiDmVhVarAssign handle "va2" is returned.
* npiDmVhCase handle "cond2"
On applying the "npiDmVhCondition" method to the npiDmVhCase handle "cond2",
the npiDmVhVar handle "day" is returned.
On applying the "npiDmVhBranch" method to the npiDmVhCase handle "cond2", the
following handles are returned:
npiDmVhCaseItem handle
On applying the "npiDmVhUpperStmt" method to the npiDmVhCaseItem handle,
the npiDmVhCase handle "cond2" is returned.
On applying the "npiDmVhChoices" method to the npiDmVhCaseItem handle, the
npiDmVhRange handle "[TUE to WED]" is returned.
On applying the "npiDmVhStmt" method to the npiDmVhCaseItem handle, the
npiDmVhVarAssign handle, which is "quota := 50" is returned.
npiDmVhDefaultCaseItem handle
On applying the "npiDmVhUpperStmt" method to the npiDmVhDefaultCaseItem
handle, the npiDmVhCase handle "cond2" is returned.
On applying the "npiDmVhStmt" method to the npiDmVhDefaultCaseItem handle,
the npiDmVhVarAssign handle, which is "quota := 70" is returned.

Vh Loop
Object Type: npiDmVhWhile, npiDmVhFor

Vh Loop is a class composed of Loop(npiDmVhWhile) and For Loop(npiDmVhFor). A loop
statement includes a sequence of statements that is to be executed repeatedly, zero or
more times.

variable cnt: integer := 2;
-- npiDmVhWhile
loop1: loop
if_stmt1: if(cnt = 0) then -- npiDmVhIf
exit;
cnt := 0;
end loop loop1;
-- npiDmVhWhile
loop2: while (cnt > 0) loop
if_stmt2: if(cnt > 0) then -- npiDmVhIf

cnt := cnt - 1;
cnt := cnt + 1;
end loop loop2;
-- npiDmVhFor
loop3: for ii in 3 downto 0 loop
va: cnt := cnt + ii; -- npiDmVhVarAssign
end loop loop3;

npiDmVhWhile handles "loop1" and "loop2" and the npiDmVhFor handle "loop3" are
* npiDmVhWhile handle "loop1"
On applying the "npiDmVhStmt" method to the npiDmVhWhile handle "loop1", the
npiDmVhIf handle "if_stmt1" is returned.
* npiDmVhWhile handle "loop2"
On applying the "npiDmVhCondition" method to the npiDmVhWhile handle "loop2",
the npiDmVhOperation handle, which is "cnt > 0" is returned.
On applying the "npiDmVhStmt" method to the npiDmVhWhile handle "loop2", the
npiDmVhIf handle "if_stmt2" is returned.
* npiDmVhFor handle "loop3"
On applying the "npiDmVhLoopIndex" method to the npiDmVhFor handle "loop3", the
npiDmVhLoopIndex handle "ii" is returned.
On applying the "npiDmVhConstraint" method to the npiDmVhFor handle "loop3", the
npiDmVhRange handle "[3 downto 0]" is returned.
On applying the "npiDmVhStmt" method to the npiDmVhFor handle "loop3", the
npiDmVhVarAssign handle "va" is returned.

* "loop1", "loop2", "loop3", "if_stmt1", "if_stmt2" and "va" are label names.

Vh Exit, Vh Next
Object Type: npiDmVhExit, npiDmVhNext

A next statement is used to complete the execution of one of the iterations of an enclosing
loop statement.
An exit statement is used to complete the execution of an enclosing loop statement.

variable cnt: integer := 2;
-- npiDmVhWhile
loop1: loop
va: cnt := cnt + 1; -- npiDmVhVarAssign
nl: next loop1 when (cnt = 3); -- npiDmVhNext
el: exit loop1 when (cnt > 10); -- npiDmVhExit
end loop loop1;

* On applying the "npiDmVhStmt" method to the npiDmVhWhile handle "loop1",
the npiDmVhVarAssign handle "va", the npiDmVhNext handle "nl", and the
npiDmVhExit handle "el" are returned.
* npiDmVhNext handle "nl"
On applying the "npiDmVhCondition" method to the npiDmVhNext handle "nl", the
npiDmVhOperation handle, which is "cnt = 3" is returned.
* npiDmVhExit handle "el"
On applying the "npiDmVhCondition" method to the npiDmVhExit handle "el", the
npiDmVhOperation handle, which is "cnt > 10" is returned.

* "loop1", "va", "nl" and "el" are label names.

Vh Return
Object Type: npiDmVhReturn

A return statement is used to complete the execution of the innermost enclosing function
or procedure body.

title: 1 01; /*npiDmContAssign*/
text:
function init_func(x: std_logic_vector) return integer is -npiDmVhFunction
ret: return x'length; -- npiDmVhReturn

title: 1 01; /*npiDmContAssign*/
text:
* On applying the "npiDmVhStmt" method to the npiDmVhFunction handle "init_func", the
npiDmVhReturn handle "ret" is returned.
* On applying the "npiDmVhExpr" method to the npiDmVhReturn handle "ret", the
npiDmVhAttrName handle "x'length" is returned.

* "ret" is a label name.

Vh Wait
Object Type: npiDmVhWait

The wait statement causes the suspension of a process statement or a procedure.

prcs: process
ws: wait on a(0), b(1 downto 0) until a(0)='0' for 1 ns; -npiDmVhWait

npiDmVhWait handle "ws" is returned.
* On applying the "npiDmVhCondition" method to the npiDmVhWait handle "ws", the
npiDmVhOperation handle, which is a(0)='0' is returned.
* On applying the "npiDmVhTimeExpr" method to the npiDmVhWait handle "ws", the
npiDmVhPhysLiteral handle "1ns" is returned.
* On applying the "npiDmVhSensitivities" method to the npiDmVhWait handle "ws",
the npiDmVhIndex handle "a(0)" and the npiDmVhSlice handle "b(1 downto 0)" is

* "ws" is a label name.

Vh Conc Assert, Vh Seq Assert
Object Type: npiDmVhConcAssert, npiDmVhSeqAssert

An assertion statement (including npiDmVhConcAssert and npiDmVhSeqAssert) checks
that a specified condition is true and reports an error if it is not.

signal a: std_logic;
signal op_code: std_logic_vector(3 downto 0) := "0000";
fail1: assert op_code = "0000" -- npiDmVhConcAssert
report "Illegal Code of Operation" -- report is not supported
severity FAILURE; -- severity is not supported
prcs: process (a)
fail2: assert op_code = "0000" -- npiDmVhSeqAssert
report "Illegal Code of Operation" -- report is not supported
severity FAILURE; -- severity is not supported

"arch_top", the npiDmVhConcAssert handle "fail1" is returned.
* On applying the "npiDmVhCondition" method to the npiDmVhConcAssert handle
"fail1", the npiDmVhOperation handle, which is op_code = "0000" is returned.
npiDmVhSeqAssert handle "fail2" is returned.
* On applying the "npiDmVhCondition" method to the npiDmVhSeqAssert handle
"fail2", the npiDmVhOperation handle, which is op_code = "0000" is returned.

* "fail1" and "fail2" are label names.

Assert Coverage
Object Types: Assert Metric (npiCovAssertMetric), Assert (npiCovAssert), Cover
Property (npiCovCoverProperty), Cover Sequence (npiCovCoverSequence),
Success Bin (npiCovSuccessBin), Attempt Bin (npiCovAttemptBin), Failure
Bin (npiCovFailureBin), Vacuous Bin (npiCovVacuousBin), Incomplete Bin
(npiCovIncompleteBin) and Firstmatch Bin (npiCovFirstmatchBin).

Assert Metric collects all the assert, cover property and cover sequence handles.
Success bin means the hit count for assert, match count for cover property and all
matches count for cover sequence.

Attempt bin means the attempt count. Failure bin means the failure count for assert.
Vacuous bin means the vacuous success count for cover property. Incomplete bin means
the incomplete count.
Firstmatch bin means the first match count for cover sequence.

* Assert generates child bins: Success, attempt, failure and incomplete.
Cover property generates child bins: Success, attempt, vacuous and incomplete.
Cover sequence generates child bins: Success, attempt, firstmatch and incomplete.
* Cover information only shows in assert, cover property and cover sequence. The
property npiCoverable of them is 1.
The property npiCovCount of success bin determines its scope handle (assert, cover
property or cover sequence) covered or not. (the value of npiCovCovered).
* The property npiCovCount can be set for success bin, attempt bin, failure bin,
incomplete bin and firstmatch bin. Similarly, the count of success bin could affect the
property npiCovered and npiCovStatus of its scope handle.

N.A

Branch Coverage
Object Types: Branch Metric (npiCovBranchMetric), Branch (npiCovBranch), Branch
Bin (npiCovBranchBin), Branch Term (npiCovBranchTerm)

Branch Metric tracks the execution of conditional statements in the design code. Branch is
a section of block which contains the combination of conditional statements.
Branch Bin is a vector value taken on the branch term of the branch. Branch Term is the
composition of the branch.

Condition Coverage
Object Types: Condition Metric (npiCovConditionMetric), Condition
(npiCovCondition), Condition Bin (npiCovConditionBin), Condition Term
(npiCovConditionTerm)

Condition Metric monitors whether certain expressions and sub expressions in the design
code evaluate to true or false. Condition is a logical or bitwise expression.

Condition Bin is a vector value taken on the condition term of the expression. Condition
Term is the composition of the expression.

Coverage Database
Object Type: Database (npiCovDatabase), Test (npiCovTest), Test Info
(npiCovTestInfo)

Database represents the object loaded from a coverage database. It contains the
available tests and the top-level instances of the design.
Test represents the result of a single execution of a tool or the merged results of two or
more executions. It contains the coverage data which determine a coverage object is
covered or not.
Test Info represents the test information got from merged test.
To get the top-level instance, apply the method "npiCovInstance" to the database handle.
Only one database could be opened in a single process. If the application wants
to open another database, the original database should be closed first.

Covered Test
Object Type: Covered Test (npiCovCoveredTest)

Covered Test represents the test that covers the bin handle.

There are three tests: "t0", "t1", and "t2". The merged test of these three tests is "tm".
Cover bin "cbA" named "auto[0]" is covered by "t0" twice and "t2" three times. The pseudo
code for getting the covered tests would be like:
printf("Cover bin: %s is covered by\n", npi_cov_get_str(npiCovName,
cbA));
npiCovHandle ctItr = npi_cov_iter_start(npiCovCoveredTest, cbA, tm/*test

title: 1 01; /*npiDmContAssign*/
text:
ered by "t0" twice and "t2" three times. The pseudo
code for getting the covered tests would be like:
printf("Cover bin: %s is covered by\n", npi_cov_get_str(npiCovName,
cbA));
npiCovHandle ctItr = npi_cov_iter_start(npiCovCoveredTest, cbA, tm/*test
must be given*/);
npiCovHandle ct = NULL;
while ((ct = npi_cov_iter_next(ctItr))) {
printf(" %s (%d times)\n", npi_cov_get_str(npiCovName, ct),
npi_cov_get(npiCovCount, ct, tm));
}
npi_cov_iter_stop(ctItr);

Cover bin: auto[0] is covered by
t0 (2 times)
t1 (3 times)

1. One-to-many method npiCovCoveredTest must be applied to test handle when getting
iterator.
2. npiCovCount for covered test means the covered times for the associated bin handle.

Finite State Machine Coverage
Object Types: Fsm Metric (npiCovFsmMetric), Fsm (npiCovFsm), States
(npiCovStates), Transitions (npiCovTransitions), Sequences (npiCovSequences),
State Bin (npiCovStateBin), Transition Bin (npiCovTransBin), Sequence Bin
(npiCovSeqBin)

Fsm Metric tracks the states and transitions of the finite state machines recognized by
verification tools. Fsm represents a finite state machine logic.
States represents the possible states of the FSM. Transitions represents the possible
transitions of the FSM.
Sequences represents the possible sequence of the FSM. State Bin represents the
coverage object of a state.
Transition Bin represents the coverage object of a transition. Sequence Bin represents the
coverage object of a sequence.

Object Type: npiCovInstance

Instance represents the hierarchical structure of the design. Instance contains a variety of
metrics. The metric defines the method of the measurement.
To get the parent instance, apply the method "npiCovScope" to the instance handle. To get
the child instances, apply the method "npiCovInstance" to the instance handle.

npiCovDefInfo shows the instance's definition name plus the information of assigned

parameter value.

Line Coverage
Object Types: Line Metric (npiCovLineMetric), Block (npiCovBlock), Statement Bin
(npiCovStmtBin)

Line Metric tracks which statements in the design source code were executed during
simulation.
Block represents the section of code, contains statements. Statement Bin represents the
coverage object of a statement.

Power Coverage
Object Types: Power Domain (npiCovPowerDomain), Power Measure
(npiCovPowerMeasure), Power Metric (npiCovPowerMetric) and Covergroup
(npiCovCovergroup)

Power Domain is the power network defined by upf or cpf.

Power Measure is the measure unit under power domain to connect the covergroups for
power coverage estimation. Power Metric collects all the covergroups for power coverage
estimation.
Covergroup here mentions the covergroup whose purpose is to estimate power coverage.
These covergroups only appears under power metrics.

1. If coverage database generated by simulator contains low-power hierarchical
verification plan, power domains is generated from test. Otherwise, power metric is
generated from test directly.
2. For VCS, the option -power=coverage+dump_hvp needs to be applied to generate lowpower hierarchical verification plan.

N.A.

Toggle Coverage
Object Types: Toggle Metric (npiCovToggleMetric), Signal (npiCovSignal), Signal Bit
(npiCovSignalBit), Toggle Bin (npiCovToggleBin)

Toggle Metric monitors value changes on signal bits in the design. Signal represents a
multiple bit signal. The npiCovSize property is great than 1.
Signal Bit represents a bit signal. The npiCovSize property is great 1. Toggle Bin
represents a value change state of a signal bit. The npiCovToggleType property can be
"0a1" or "1a0".

Testbench Coverage
Object Types: Testbench Metric (npiCovTestbenchMetric), Covergroup
(npiCovCovergroup), Cover Instance (npiCovCoverInstance), Cross (npiCovCross),
Cover Point (npiCovCoverPoint) and Cover Bin (npiCovCoverBin)

Testbench Metric tracks the execution of covergroups. Covergroup is a section of block
which contains the combination of coverpoint and cross.
Cover Instance is an instance-based covergroup information when covergroup's option
"per_instance" is set 1. Coverpoint is a point to check if the specified integral expression is
covered.
Cross can check the cross coverage between multiple coverpoints or crosses. Cover bin is
the basic unit to analyze the coverage data.

text:
* If the option property npiCovPerInstance of covergroup is 1, cover instances can be
generated from covergroup.
* The property npiCovCount can be set for cover bin, and it also affects the cover bin's
property npiCovered and npiCovStatus.
* The cover bin mentioned in 2) must be generated from cover instance or covergroup
whose property npiCovPerInstance is equal to 0.
* Options like npiCovGoal, npiCovAtLeast, npiCovComment, and so on. can be obtained
only under npiCovCoverInstance objects.

* Cover bin's property npiCovBinName and npiCovBinType are supported for the cover
bins from cross.
* The property npiCovBinType returns npiCovAutoBin for auto-bin, npiCovUserBin for
user-defined bin, and npiCovIgnoreBin for ignored bin.

A simulation test means running simulation once.
The number of simv runs without cleaning the database equals the number of simulation
tests.

* The database handle is obtained by the npi_vcs_open API.
* npiVcsToolName is always "VCS".

Compilation
The compilation handle shows the compilation information from the database generated
by the VCS simulator.

* npiVcsResult returns 1 if the compilation result is successful; otherwise, returns 0.

Design Statistics
The Design statistics handle shows the basic design information like the module number
and all the module information.

* Module signifies the module definition in the design.

Simulation
The simulation handle contains the simulation information like simulation begin-time and
end-time. Combined with simulation test handle, the information in every simulation test
can also be obtained.

* Waveform signifies the waveform dumped by a specific system task.

Test
Test signifies the simulation test by simv. The execution times of simv is equal to the test
number. This information (test number) can be obtained by the npiVcsTestNo property
from design statistics (npiVcsDesignStats) handle.

N/A

Time is the handle to represent the time information from compilation or simulation. The
time format could be time_t or double.

* npiVcsFormat indicates what kind of value format npi_vcs_get_value should use.
Start time, finish time, and gen time use the npiVcsTimeVal format.
Elapsed time and cpu time use the npiVcsDoubleVal format.

Module represents the module definition in the design.

* npiVcsLength signifies the number of code lines for the module definition.

Waveform
Waveform represents the waveform dumping system task. The number of waveforms is
equal to the number of dumping system tasks.

* npiVcsSize signifies the size of the waveform file and the unit is KB.

Iterator is the container to save the handles obtained by one-to-many method.

* npiVcsSize signifies the number of handles that is iterated by this iterator.

Isolation Control
Object Type: npiPwIsoControl

The npiPwIsoControl object contains the specification of the isolation control signal and
sense.
Related UPF commands include set_isolation, set_isolation_control. Property
"npiPwClampValue" returns npiPwClampType_e.
Property "npiPwSense" returns npiPwSenseType_e. Refer to Isolation Strategy.

Isolation Strategy
Object Type: npiPwIsoStrategy

The npiPwIsoStrategy object contains the specification of isolation strategy which is
applied at specified ports on the interface of the specified power domain.
Property "npiPwLocation" returns npiPwLocType_e.
Property "npiPwDirection" returns npiPwDirType_e.
Property "npiPwClamp" returns npiPwClampType_e.
Property "npiPwSinkOffClamp" returns npiPwClampType_e.
Property "npiPwSourceOffClamp" returns npiPwClampType_e.
Refer to Isolation Control.

* Apply one-to-one relationship "npiPwPowerDomain" to the npiPwIsoStrategy handle
"ISO_V1", the npiPwPowerDomain handle "top/PD_V1" is returned.
* Apply one-to-one relationship "npiPwSource" to the npiPwIsoStrategy handle
"ISO_V1", the npiPwSupplySet handle "top/V1_SET" is returned.

* Apply one-to-one relationship "npiPwSink" to the npiPwIsoStrategy handle "ISO_V1",
the npiPwSupplySetHandle handle "top/PD_V2.primary" is returned.
* Apply one-to-many relationship "npiPwIsoControl" to the npiPwIsoStrategy handle
"ISO_V1", the npiPwIsoControl handle "top/ISO_V1" is returned.
* Apply one-to-many relationship "npiPwImpactSignal" to the npiPwIsoStrategy handle
"ISO_V1", the npiPwLogicNet handle "top/inst1/out" is returned.
* Apply one-to-many relationship "npiPwElement" to the npiPwIsoStrategy handle
"ISO_V1", the npiPwLogicPort handle "top/inst1/out" is returned.
* Apply one-to-many relationship "npiPwElement" to the npiPwIsoStrategy handle
"ISO_V1", the npiPwInstance handle "top/inst1/m1" is returned.
* Apply one-to-many relationship "npiPwIsoControl" to the npiPwIsoStrategy handle
"ISO_V2", the npiPwIsoControl handle "top/ISO_V2" is returned.
* Apply property "npiPwLocation" to the npiPwIsoStrategy handle "ISO_V1", and
"npiPwLocSelf" is returned.
* Apply property string "npiPwNamePrefix" to the npiPwIsoStrategy handle "ISO_V1",
and ""CELL"" is returned.
* Apply property string "npiPwNameSuffix" to the npiPwIsoStrategy handle "ISO_V1",
and ""ISO"" is returned.
* Apply property "npiPwClamp" to the npiPwIsoStrategy handle "ISO_V1", and
"npiPwClamp1" is returned.
* Apply property "npiPwSinkOffClamp" to the npiPwIsoStrategy handle "ISO_V1", and
"npiPwClampUserDef" is returned.
* Apply property string "npiPwSinkOffClampStr" to the npiPwIsoStrategy handle
"ISO_V1", and "1.20" is returned.
* Apply property "npiPwSourceOffClamp" to the npiPwIsoStrategy handle "ISO_V1", and
"npiPwClampUserDef" is returned.
* Apply property string "npiPwSourceOffClampStr" to the npiPwIsoStrategy handle
"ISO_V1", and "1.20" is returned.
* Apply property "npiPwForceIsolation" to the npiPwIsoStrategy handle "ISO_V1", and
"1" is returned.
* Apply property "npiPwDiffSupplyOnly" to the npiPwIsoStrategy handle "ISO_V2", and
"1" is returned.
* Apply property "npiPwDirection" to the npiPwIsoStrategy handle "ISO_V2", and
"npiPwDirBoth" is returned.

* The default value of property "npiPwDirection" is "npiPwDirOutputs".
* The default value of property "npiPwLocation" is "npiPwLocAutomatic".
* The default value of property "npiPwDiffSupplyOnly" is "0".

ls_strategy_example.upf, ls_strategy_example.v

Level-shifter Strategy
Object Type: npiPwLsStrategy

The npiPwLsStrategy object contains the specification of level-shifter strategy which is
applied at specified ports on the interface of the specified power domain.
Property "npiPwLocation" returns npiPwLocType_e.

* Apply property string "npiPwNamePrefix" to the npiPwLsStrategy handle "LS_V1", and
