create_supply_set SS_VDD
create_power_domain PD_CHIP -supply { primary SS_VDD } -update
create_power_switch SUB_VDD_SW -domain PD_CHIP \
-ack_port {ack_port ack 1} \
-ack_delay {ack_port 1} \
-off_state {off {!ctrl_port}}
create_power_domain PD_INST

-elements inst

set_port_attributes -ports {inst/in} \
-clamp_value 0 \
-driver_supply SS_VDD \
-related_power_port CHIP_VDD \
-related_ground_port CHIP_VSS
set_port_attributes -ports {inst/ctrl} \
-receiver_supply SS_VDD
set_related_supply_net -object_list inst/out -power CHIP_VDD -ground
CHIP_VSS
set_level_shifter ls -domain PD_INST -elements {inst/in inst/out
inst/ctrl}

title: 1 01; /*npiDmContAssign*/
text:
* Apply property "npiPwDirection" to the npiPwLogicPort handle "ack_port", and
"npiPwDirOut" is returned.
* Apply property "npiPwPortType" to the npiPwLogicPort handle "ack_port", and
"npiPwPortSwAck" is returned.
* Apply property "npiPwAckDelay" to the npiPwLogicPort handle "ack_port", and "1" is
* Apply property "npiPwAckLogic" to the npiPwLogicPort handle "ack_port", and "1" is
* Apply one-to-one relationship "npiPwLogicNet" to the npiPwLogicPort handle
"ack_port", the npiPwLogicNet handle "top/u_chip/ack" is returned.
* Apply one-to-one relationship "npiPwDrvSupply" to the npiPwLogicPort handle "inst/in",
the npiPwSupplySet handle "top/u_chip/SS_VDD" is returned.
* Apply one-to-one relationship "npiPwRelatedPower" to the npiPwLogicPort handle
"inst/in", the npiPwSupplyPort handle "top/u_chip/CHIP_VDD" is returned.

* Apply one-to-one relationship "npiPwRelatedGnd" to the npiPwLogicPort handle "inst/
in", the npiPwSupplyPort handle "top/u_chip/CHIP_VSS" is returned.
the npiPwAttribute handle "UPF_clamp_value" is returned.
the npiPwAttribute handle "UPF_driver_supply" is returned.
the npiPwAttribute handle "UPF_related_ground_port" is returned.
the npiPwAttribute handle "UPF_related_power_port" is returned.
* Apply one-to-one relationship "npiPwRecSupply" to the npiPwLogicPort handle "inst/
ctrl", the npiPwSupplySet handle "top/u_chip/SS_VDD" is returned.
* Apply one-to-many relationship "npiPwAttribute" to the npiPwLogicPort handle "inst/
ctrl", the npiPwAttribute handle "UPF_receiver_supply" is returned.
* Apply one-to-one relationship "npiPwRelatedPower" to the npiPwLogicPort handle
"inst/out", the npiPwSupplyNet handle "top/u_chip/CHIP_VDD" is returned.
* Apply one-to-one relationship "npiPwRelatedGnd" to the npiPwLogicPort handle "inst/
out", the npiPwSupplyNet handle "top/u_chip/CHIP_VSS" is returned.

* For a logic port that is not defined in UPF (that is, HDL port), property "npiPwDirection"
returns npiPwDirInvalid.
* For command set_port_attributes, it only supports ports within HDL design.
* For command set_related_supply_net:
Build relation between <logic port> and <supply net ref> which is within <relation>
class.

Operation
Object Type: npiPwOperation

The npiPwOperation object is a construct that combines operands with operators.

Property "npiPwOpType" returns npiPwOpType_e. Refer to Expression.

* Apply one-to-many relationship "npiPwExpr" to the npiPwOperation handle
"((CHIP_SS.power=={FULL_ON 0.8})&&(CHIP_SS.ground=={FULL_ON 0}))",
* The npiPwOperation handle "(CHIP_SS.power=={FULL_ON 0.8})" and the
npiPwOperation handle "(CHIP_SS.ground=={FULL_ON 0})" is returned.
* Apply one-to-many relationship "npiPwExpr" to the npiPwOperation handle
"(CHIP_SS.power=={FULL_ON 0.8})",
* The npiPwSupplySetFunction handle "CHIP_SS.power" and the npiPwSupplyState
handle "{FULL_ON 0.8}" is returned.

* Apply property "npiPwOpType" to the npiPwOperation handle
"((CHIP_SS.power=={FULL_ON 0.8})&&(CHIP_SS.ground=={FULL_ON 0}))", and
"npiPwOpLogAnd" is returned.
* Apply property "npiPwOpType" to the npiPwOperation handle
"(CHIP_SS.power=={FULL_ON 0.8})", and "npiPwOpLogEq" is returned.

N/A

Object Type: npiPwAttribute

The npiPwAttribute object represents the attribute information of ports.
Refer to Logic Port and Supply Port.

* Apply one-to-one relationship "npiPwRelatedPower" to the npiPwLogicPort handle
"inst/in", the npiPwSupplyPort handle "top/u_chip/CHIP_VDD" is returned.
* Apply one-to-one relationship "npiPwRelatedGnd" to the npiPwLogicPort handle "inst/
in", the npiPwSupplyPort handle "top/u_chip/CHIP_VSS" is returned.
the npiPwAttribute handle "UPF_clamp_value" is returned.
the npiPwAttribute handle "UPF_related_ground_port" is returned.
the npiPwAttribute handle "UPF_related_power_port" is returned.
* Apply property "npiPwFullName" to the npiPwAttribute handle "UPF_clamp_value", and
"UPF_clamp_value" is returned.
* Apply property "npiPwAttrValue" to the npiPwAttribute handle "UPF_clamp_value", and
"0" is returned.
* Apply property "npiPwFullName" to the npiPwAttribute handle
"UPF_related_ground_port", and "UPF_related_ground_port" is returned.
* Apply property "npiPwAttrValue" to the npiPwAttribute handle
"UPF_related_ground_port", and "CHIP_VSS" is returned.
* Apply property "npiPwFullName" to the npiPwAttribute handle
"UPF_related_power_port", and "UPF_related_power_port" is returned.
* Apply property "npiPwAttrValue" to the npiPwAttribute handle
"UPF_related_power_port", and "CHIP_VDD" is returned.

For command set_port_attributes, it only supports ports within HDL design.

attribute_example.upf, attribute_example.v

Port State
Object Type: npiPwPortState

The npiPwPortState object represents the possible state of the specified supply port.
Refer to Supply State, Supply Port, and Power State Table State.

* Apply one-to-many relationship "npiPwPortState" to the npiPwSupplyPort handle
"VDD", the npiPwPortState handle "top/VDD.HV" is returned.
* Apply one-to-many relationship "npiPwPortState" to the npiPwPstState handle
"HighMode", the npiPwPortState handle "top/VDD.HV" is returned.
* Apply one-to-one relationship "npiPwSupplyPort" to the npiPwPortState handle "HV",
the npiPwSupplyPort handle "top/VDD" is returned.
* Apply one-to-one relationship "npiPwSupplyState" to the npiPwPortState handle "HV",
the npiPwSupplyState handle "{FULL_ON 1.08}" is returned.

The port state is not returned, if the port state is not used in power state table.
add_port_state port -state {HV 1} -state {LV 0.9} -state {OFF off}
create_pst PST -supplies {port}
add_pst_state HighMode -pst PST -state {HV}
add_pst_state SleepMode -pst PST -state {OFF}

Apply one-to-many relationship "npiPwPortState" to the npiPwSupplyPort handle "port",
the npiPwPortState handle "top/VDD.LV" is not returned.

sense.

Retention Strategy
Object Type: npiPwRetStrategy

The npiPwRetControl object contains the specification of the retention control signal and
The npiPwRetStrategy object contains the specification of retention strategy which is
applied at specified registers in the specified power domain.
The retention strategy identifies the save behavior and restore behavior of retention
registers.
Refer to Retention Control.

Property Note

The database name is a full path.
For example, if dut.crdb is under /home/uu/,
npi_crdb_get_str(npiCrdbName, handle_of_DUT_CRDB) returns
"/home/uu/dut.crdb".

Property Note
Language type

The language of a scope is the module language.

For scope objects of instances, the returned language type is the
module language, not the instance language.
For example, u1 is instantiated under top, which is Verilog. Module
u1 is written in VHDL. Therefore, npi_crdb_get(npiCrdbLangType,
handle_of_u1) returns npiCrdbVHDL instead of npiCrdbVerilog.

Traversal Note

A composite signal reference handle can use npiCrdbVolChild to get all its member
handles. Example: struct {logic f1; logic [1:0] f2;} st1;
//-- check st1Handle is a struct

NPI_INT32 is_struct = 0;
NPI_INT32 has_prop_ = npi_crdb_get(npiCrdbSigType, st1Handle,
is_struct/*O*/);
if((0 == has_prop) || (0==is_struct))
//-- iterate childs of struct st1
npiCrdbHandle memIter = npi_crdb_vol_iter_start (npiCrdbVolChild,
st1Handle);
if( memIter == NPI_CRDB_INVALID_HANDL) {
}
npiCrdbHandle memberH = npi_crdb_vol_iter_next (memIter); //get f1
memberH = npi_crdb_vol_iter_next (topScopeIter); //get f2
NPI_INT32 code = npi_crdb_vol_iter_stop (memIter);

Only Bit signal can iterate equivalent signals and correlate signals

Does not allow sig iterate equivalent or correlate signals
Allows sig[1] and sig[0] iterate equivalent or correlate signals
Note that you need to use npi_crdb_vol_iter_start, npi_crdb_vol_iter_next, and
npi_crdb_vol_iter_stop to iterate equivalent, correlation, and child signals.
The return handles are volatile handles.
CRDB only extracts equivalent nets of signal whose dimension <= 1. NPI CRDB model
follows what CRDB has, that is, only signal of npiCrdbBit or npiCrdbBus might have
equivalent nets.

Property Note
Port direction

The direction is based on CRDB model instead of language model.
Some other ports such as ref port might be modeled as input port in
CRDB.

Signal type

The signal type is based on CRDB model instead of language model.
In CRDB model, packed and unpacked information is not reserved, so
packed array and unpacked array are modeled the same in CRDB.

Size and range

Size is the number of 1st level elements of composite signals.
Example: wire [6:4][2:0] mdap2;

Left and right

Because CRDB does not have information about a range of a struct
array is increased or decreased, decrease range is used.
Example: struct packed {reg f1;} [0:7] st1;

HVP Plan
Plan represents the object loaded from hierarchical verification plan. The hierarchy
is composed of features. Plan defines some attributes, annotations and metrics for
estimating the coverage status.

Plan handle is obtained by API npi_hvp_load_plan.

Spec
Spec file for the hierarchical verification plan.

NA.

Attribute Declaration
Attribute declaration is declared under plan and used by features. Attribute declaration
contains four data type: integer, real, string and enum. The difference between attribute
and annotation is that attribute propagates the assigned value down to the child hierarchy
unless it is explicitly overridden at the plan or feature level.

attribute real fraction = 1.0; // attribute decl; npi_hvp_get_value
gets 1.0
annotationreal fractionAnn = 2.0;

npi_hvp_get_value for attribute decl gets the value assigned in its right-hand-side.

Annotation Declaration
Annotation declaration is declared under plan and used by features. Annotation
declaration contains four data type: integer, real, string and enum. The difference between
attribute and annotation is that attribute propagates the assigned value down to the child
hierarchy unless it is explicitly overridden at the plan or feature level.

annotation real fractionAnn = 2.0; //annotation decl;
npi_hvp_get_value gets 2.0

npi_hvp_get_value for attribute decl gets the value assigned in its right-hand-side.

Attribute Assign
Attribute assign represents the attribute value assign statement under plan.

fraction = 3.0; // attribute assign
fractionAnn= 5.0;

NA

Annotation Assign
Annotation assign represents the annotation value assign statement under plan.

attribute enum{orange, apple, banana} fruitName = orange;

fractionAnn = 5.0; //annotation assign

NA

Attribute represents the usable attribute under plan or feature.

fraction = 3.0; // attribute: fraction; npi_hvp_get_value
respectively returns 1.0 when "isGetDefaultVal" is true
// and 3.0 when "isGetDefaultVal" is false

npi_hvp_get_value for attribute returns the default value (pre-defined value or value
assigned in declaration) if setting flag "isGetDefaultVal" as true; otherwise, return the
current assigned value.

Annotation
Annotation represents the usable annotation under plan or feature.

fractionAnn = 5.0; //annotation: fractionAnn;
npi_hvp_get_value respectively returns 2.0 when "isGetDefaultVal" is
// true and 5.0 when "isGetDefaultVal" is false

npi_hvp_get_value for annotation returns the default value (pre-defined value or value
assigned in declaration) if setting flag "isGetDefaultVal" as true; otherwise, return the
current assigned value.

Metric
Metric represents the usable metric under plan.

metric integer bugs; // integer metric: bugs

fractionAnn =5.0;

npiHvpAggType could return npiHvpMaxAgg, npiHvpMinAgg, npiHvpSumAgg,

Feature represents the component that construct the hierarchy under plan.

NPI Libraries
* Use NPI Libraries

NPI Libraries is a set of libraries that extend the functionality of NPI Models. The goal is to
improve the NPI programmers' productivity by reducing reinvention-of-the-wheel.
The libraries are aimed at a wide range of NPI users and application domains. They
range from common design traversal applications like hierarchy tree dumping, module
annotation, signal driver/load tracing, to specific design flow enhancements like design
rule validation, design manipulation, and so on. Some special NPI Models programming
tricks are also included.
NPI Libraries covers both C/C++ APIs and Tcl commands. All of them are written using
NPI Models. They are open source. Users can download NPI Libraries and make
modifications as desired.
The API Reference section gives an introduction to the NPI Libraries categories.

The Signal Library provides the APIs that are related to the design information of a signal
(variable or net). In general, the APIs can be classified into the following groups:
1. Trace the driver or load of a signal based on the NPI Language Model and NPI Netlist
2. Get the equivalent signals of a target signal.
3. Get the signal definition typespec of a target signal.
Driver/Load Tracing
The APIs with the prefix "npi_sv_trace" mean they function as tracing the driver or load of
a signal based on the NPI Language (SystemVerilog) Model.
The APIs with the prefix "npi_nl_trace" mean they function as tracing the driver or load of a
signal based on the NPI Netlist Model.
Equivalent Signals
The API "npi_get_equivalent_signal" obtains the net handles that are equivalent to the
target signal.
The two signals are defined as "equivalent" if they are only connected by the port/instport
of the module instances (for example, an instance whose cell type is npiNlModuleCell).
Signal Definition Typespec
The API "npi_get_signal_define_typespec" obtains the typespec handle that represents
the definition of the signal.
The API is written based on the NPI Language Model.

Limitations
1. All the APIs for tracing the drivers or loads of a signal based on NPI Language Model
does not work when the specified signal is located at the index or slice of a reference
module mm(ref bit ma);
bit [1:0] a;
mm m0(a[p]); // m0 port ma's higher connection a[p] that is a
ref-obj,

Trace Network APIs are based on Netlist models. It contains three parts:
1. Trace network and generate network graph under user-specified criteria.
2. Report path according to current graph.

port or a signal.

Detail Mode Setting

There are a bunch of stop conditions for this system. You can specify the cell type of
instance that can be passed through, either with positive listing or negative listing. You can
also specify the module names that you want to stop tracing.
To prevent loop and complexity of the graph, it does not pass through flip-flops, and a
maximum tracing depth is also specified.
Further, a module ports mapping can be given to prevent tracing too deep into modules. It
simply jumps from input port to the corresponding output port while tracing.
The following section covers the map file mapping rules:
Basic Mapping Rules
Map file:
modName portA portB
1. If trace to portA, it maps to portB.
2. If trace to a bit portA[idx], it maps to portB[idx].
3. If trace to slice portA[lidx,ridx], it maps to slice portB[lidx:ridx]. (For example, portA [1:0]
maps to portB[1:0]).
4. If output port not existed, it stops tracing at input port and the port is listed in the result
5. If portB has size = 1, then any part of portA maps to portB. (for example, both portA[1]
and portA[1:0] maps to portB).

Extended Mapping Rules
Map file:
modName portA portB
modName portA[0] portB[2]
If trace to portA, it maps to portB.
If trace to portA[0], it maps to portB[2]. Since the map relation is specified.
If trace to portA[1], maps to portB[1] according to basic mapping rules.
Map file:
modName portA portB
modName portA[0] portB
If trace to portA, it maps to portB.
If trace to port portA[0], maps to portB. Since the map relation is specified.
If trace to port portA[1], maps to portB[1] according to basic mapping rules.
Map file:
modName portA portB[1]
If trace to portA, it maps to portB[1].
If trace to portA[idx], maps to portB[1].
If trace to portA[lidx:ridx], maps to portB[1].
The map is bidirectional. portB maps to portA, and the spec is also applicable.
Special environment variable setting for trace network as follows:
setenv NPI_NL_TRACE_DUMP_STATUS 1 - Dump tracing status information.
setenv NPI_NL_TRACE_REG_PASS_DQ 1

Pass register from D to Q and reverse. You must be careful with this option because this
might increase the graph complexity significantly.

The Netlist Library provides some commonly used APIs written based on the NPI Netlist
Obtain Handles (npiNlHandle) by nl_name
Since the NPI Netlist Model regards the design as a netlist after inference, the objects
in the Netlist model might have its specific name, which might not be their names in the
design source code.
In the Netlist model, the object name "nl_name" is called. The "nl_name" can be obtained
from the property npiNlName for that handle.
However, if you dump the nl_name into a file, it is difficult to recover the handle directly
from the nl_name.
To overcome the difficulties described above, the Netlist Library provides the following
APIs to get the handles from the nl_name:
* npi_nl_inst_handle_by_nl_name
* npi_nl_port_handle_by_nl_name
* npi_nl_instport_handle_by_nl_name
* npi_nl_net_handle_by_nl_name
As the names suggest, these APIs can obtain the handles from the nl_name and therefore
users can continue with their applications with the handles.

The NPI VANL Library provides some C-APIs and Tcl interfaces written based on the NPI
Netlist Model and the NPI Netlist Library.
The NPI VANL Library can be seen as Netlist Model + Value on ports and inst ports. Thus,
despite those basic APIs which focus on value propagation, it also provides APIs related
to the design information of a signal like Signal Library and APIs that can identify the
connected components from a signal like Connection Library.
The difference between Netlist and VANL tracing is that the VANL Library traces driver or
load or fan-in or fan-out in an active way, so called "Active Trace".

You can trace driver or load with value, and find the possible signals that cause the value
change of the target signal, or conversely find the signals affected by the target signal. For
more information about Active Trace, see Rules for Active Trace.

Rules for Active Trace
When tracing an active driver/load from output/input pins of instances, different rules are
applied for different npiNlInstType
This section introduces the rules for Active Trace of every supported instance.

NPI VANL provides "Active Trace" functionality, which is a way to trace driver or load with
value. Active trace only happens when tracing driver from an instance output or tracing
load from an instance input.
It considers its npiNlCellType and the values of its inputs and outputs. You can trace
active drivers and then conveniently find the possible signals which are the root cause to
the value change of the target signal.
On the contrary, you can trace active loads whose values are mainly or partially affected
by the target signal.
The relationship between active driver and active load is mutual. If A and B are the active
drivers of O, then O must be the active load of A and B.
Rules for User Set Signals
Since VANL Library is based on NPI Netlist Model, user can set or define values on
npiNlNet, npiNlInstPort, and npiNlPort.
The user-defined or user-set signals are "value-tied" and they do not change their values
until user cleans or resets them. More importantly, they do NOT have any active driver.
For example, as shown in the figure below, if you set the value on npiNlNet top.a and
npiNlPort top.b (marked as blue words) and you try to recursively get the active drivers
from npiNlNet top.o after evaluation, you have npiNlInstport before npiNlNet top.a
(pointed out by the black arrow) and npiNlPort top.b, if their values formed the value of
npiNlNet top.o.

Rules for npiNlSymbolLibInst
For npiNlSymbolLibInst, extract its npiNlFunc, npiNlXFunc, and npiNlThreeStateFunc.
According to these function-strings, the active drivers can be evaluated.
FN04D2 oai2 (ZN, A1, A2, B1, B2)

npiNlFunc:
!((A1&A2)|(B1&B2))

When A1=1, A2=0, B1=0, and B2=1, the active drivers of ZN are A2 and B1 because
the value of output ZN is caused by its input (A1&A2) = 0 and (B1&B2) = 0, which are
caused by A2 and B1 respectively.
Rules for npiNlUDPLibInst
For npiNlUDPInst, NPI VANL extracts its table entry, and then finds the first case matched
with the current input values. NPI VANL treats the UDP symbol "?" as a "don't care bit",
which is not included as an active driver.

-> npiNlInstPort, top.top:Always0SigOp0:2:2:Mux.IH_w7, (null), (1'bx)
trace driver recursively 2: npiNlDeclNet, top.w3, (null)
-> npiNlInstPort, top.top:Always1SigOp1:3:3:Or.IH_w5, (null), (1'b1)

text:
Schematic

This program recursively traces the driver with value and the value of each signal after
propagation is shown in the preceding Schematic.
At first stage, you want to trace active driver recursively from top.w1. The active driver of
top.w1 would be top.w2 and top.w3 is dropped because the value of top.w1 is X, and
the possible driver to cause this is only top.w2 with value X.
Due to similar reason, the active driver of top.w2 would be top.w7 and top.w9, since the
value X of top.w2 is caused by mux input top.w7 and the control pin top.w9, which are X
and 1, respectively.
Since the value on net is set in this example, on tracing you get
npiNlInstport top.top:Always0SigOp0:2:2:Mux.CH_w9 and
top.top:Always0SigOp0:2:2:Mux.IH_w7 before those net.
Secondly, user traces the active driver of top.w3, the output of an npiNlOrCell, with value
1.
The possible drivers that caused this 1 are signals whose value is also 1, thus get top.w5
and top.w6.
Since the value on net is set in this example, thus when tracing you
get npiNlInstPort top.top:Always1SigOp1:3:3:Or.IH_w5 and
top.top:Always1SigOp1:3:3:Or.IH_w6 before those net.
List of Supported Types and Propagate Rules
In this section, supported cell types to evaluate value and active trace are listed.
npiNlSymbolLibInst and npiNlUDPLibInst are supported.
npiNlRTLInst and npiNlHierInst are only supported for some specific npiNlCellType.

Refer to npi_nl.h.
The value goes straight through npiNlModuleCell. The value does NOT propagate
through registers. NPI VANL is only applicable for propagating values between
combinational cells.
Thus, the register output is not evaluated during propagation.

User Interface and Use Flow
The following figure shows the flow of using NPI Transaction Writer APIs:

title: 1 01; /*npiDmContAssign*/
text:
Firstly, the new instance of the npi_tr_writer class needs to be created with the provided
instance path. The instance path specifies the scope to which all the objects created
through this instance belong.
Secondly, you can create any objects by the APIs of writer instance.
It is allowed to have multiple writer instances to dump the objects into the
same FSDB file, so the objects under different paths appear in one FSDB file
accordingly.
The relationship with another object can be set through the related relationship APIs. In
this model, there are two main relationships:
* Parent and child (children).
* Predecessor and successor (successors).

The two objects belonging to two different writer instances can be set as predecessor and
successor (successors) by calling the corresponding APIs and specifying the successor's
writer instance.
The attributes with different values and data types can be added. The allowed data types
are bit, bit vector, integer, real (double), time (64 bits unsigned integer), and string.
You can also set the expected attribute and if the attribute is not equal to the expected
attribute, it is highlighted in Protocol Analyzer.
To end an object creation, theend_object() method can be used for a specified object.
The ended object cannot be modified after it ends using this API.
To end all of the not ended objects, the flush_writer() API can be used, which ends all the
objects and dumps them into the FSDB file.

Illegal Cases for Object ID
The object ID is defined as const char*.
The following are some illegal cases for the provided object ID:
* The NULL pointer is provided.
* The object ID is not created by the create_object() API.
An error message is issued if these conditions are violated and the API that calls these
illegal cases becomes invalid.

npi_nl_sig_hdl_2_sig_hdl_conn
Find a connective path between two signals using the NPI Netlist model.
One of the paths from the net with handle from_hdl to the destination net, specified by its
handle to_hdl, is computed.
Then, the handles of nets along the path are saved into a specified vector (C++) or array

int npi_nl_sig_hdl_2_sig_hdl_conn (npiNlHandle from_hdl, npiNlHandle
to_hdl, nlHdlVec_t& conn_nl_hdl_vec, int assignCell = 0 );

from_hdl

Specify the Netlist model handle of the source net.
to_hdl

Specify the Netlist model handle of the destination net.
conn_nl_hdl_vec

Specify the reference of the STL vector where the connected net handles (npiNlHandle) is

A Boolean value specifying whether or not a npiNlAssignCell is treated as a primitive cell.
0: the npiNlAssignCell object is treated as a net without its information of direction and is
1: the npiNlAssignCell object is treated as a primitive cell with information of its direction
and is not simply passed through when traversing the model.

end

npi_nl_trace_network_port_2_inst
Report tracing result and the network between start ports and end instances based
on NPI Netlist model.
A general trace connection app is provided. The function starts tracing from the ports listed
in the startFile.
When tracing to a module listed in the modMap, it does not go into the module. Instead, it
jumps to the correspondent port and keep tracing.
There are some conditions for the program to stop tracing:
* First, it meets the floating ports/instports or constant-tied signal.
* Second, it meets the ports of end instance listed in the endFile.
* Third, it meets the instports of flip-flop cell.
* Fourth, it meets the instports of an instance whose npiNlCellType is not npiNlModule
nor listed in the passCellFile.
* Fifth, it meets ports of the top boundary module of the whole design.
* Sixth, it meets the instports of an instance whose module name is listed in the
stopModFile.
And last, if the tracing level exceed the depth user specified, it stops tracing.
In the end, the tracing result of each ports is dumped to the resultFile and the whole graph
network of the points mentioned above (start points, jump points, end points and stop
points) is dumped to the networkFile.

Tcl
proc ::npi_L1::npi_nl_trace_network_port_2_inst { startFile endFile
resultFile networkFile
{ passCellFile "" } { isPassCellPosList 1 }
{ mapFile "" } {linkFile "" }
{ isToBit 0 } { isEndAtModule 0 }
{ detailMode 0 } { networkStyle 0 } { depth 20 }
{ stopModFile "" } }

* startFile: Specify the file name containing the full actual name / npiNlFullName of
start ports, and the trace direction of each port.
Trace direction is optional. If trace direction is not specified, for output it traces load,
others trace the driver.
Format:
port_full_actual_name npiNlDriver/npiNlLoad

Wildcard supported for the ports' name for the following case:
- top.u1.p*
- top.u1.p*[1]
- top.u1.* // all ports under top.u1

* endFile: Specify the file name containing the end instances. It can be module
name, or the full actual name / npiNlFullName of end instances, according to the flag
isEndAtModule.
isEndAtModule = 0: full actual name / npiNlFullName of instances
isEndAtModule = 1: module name

Wildcard supported.
* resultFile: Specify the file name where the trace results of each start port is shown.
* networkFile: Specify the file name where the network relationship is shown. To
specify the complexity of the network, refer to detailMode.

* passCellFile: Specify the file name containing the npiNlCellType that passes through
and keep tracing. No-specified type: tracing only passes through module boundaries by
default. (npiNlCellType == npiNlModuleCell)
isPassCellPosList = 1, only the npiNlCellType listing in the file + npiNlModuleCell pass,
while others do not.
isPassCellPosList = 0, then npiNlCellType listing in the file does not pass through,
while others do.
* isPassCellPosList: Specify whether the passCellFile is in positive listing. Default is
1.
* mapFile: Specify the file name containing the module port mapping that jumps
through while tracing. The mapping should be 1-1 or 1-N or N-1 relationship. N-N is
not supported. Wildcard supported. If one line has first character `#', it is treated as
comment line.
* Style:
1-1: modName in1 out1
N-1: modName { in1 in2 } out1
1-N: modName in1 { out1 out2 }
linkFile

Specify the file name containing the full actual name / npiNlFullName of link points.
A link point is a npiNlPort or a npiNlInstPort that user particularly want to observe in the
network graph. The graph recognizes the link point as a node, thus also reported in the
network result.
Wildcard is supported. If one line has first character `#', it is treated as comment line.
* isToBit: Specify whether the start port should split to bits before tracing. Default is 0.
If the start ports is itself a npiNlPseudoPort name. For example, top.a[2:3]
from a npiNlPort top.a[0:3], it is always automatically split to bits.
* isEndAtModule: Specify whether the end file is stated in the "full actual name /
npiNlFullName" style (0), or the "module name" style (1) or mixed style(2). Default is 0.
* detailMode: Specify how detail the network is, and how it affects the result of report
path or network. By default, 0, the network graph contains:
The start ports and end ports
Both sides of ports of mapping module.

Link ports that you want to observe.
The stop ports or instports and literal net that meet the stop conditions.
0: The instports from the passCellFile is not a node in the network
graph for less complexity.
1: Adding all past ports of module into the graph.
2: Adding all instports of instance from symbol library.
3: Adding all past ports of module, and the past instports from the
passCellFile into the graph.

* networkStyle: Specify which style the network file should be dumped.
0: Text view (default).
1: json style.
Text view and json style shows the actual name of each node in graph, along with
its type, direction if it is a port or instport, connected net if it is an instport, and value
if it is a literal net.
It shows its instance information, including instance name, module name, cell type,
file name and begin line number. It also shows the driver or load relationship of
each node.
2: Tree view.
Each tree starts from a no-driver node.
3: Tree view readable.
Similar to 2. However for instport with non-intuitive netlist-gen name, it shows its
connected net's name instead for readability.

* depth: Specify the maximum tracing level. Default is 20.
* stopModFile: Specify the file name containing the module names that stops tracing.
If the tracing program ended gracefully, the total number of start ports is returned.
Otherwise, return 0.

npi_nl_trace_network_sig_2_sig
Report tracing result and the network between start nets and end nets based on NPI
Netlist model.
A general trace connection app is provided. The function starts tracing from the nets listed
in the startFile. When tracing to a module listed in the modMap, it does not go into the
module. Instead, it goes to the corresponding port and keeps tracing.
There are some conditions for the program to stop tracing:
1. It meets the floating ports/instports or constant-tied signal.
2. It meets the nets listed in the endFile.
3. It meets the instports of flip-flop cell.
4. It meets the instports of an instance whose npiNlCellType is not npiNlModule nor
listed in the passCellFile.
5. It meets ports of the top boundary module of the whole design.
6. It meets the instports of an instance whose module name is listed in the stopModFile.
7. Finally, if the tracing level exceed the depth user specified, it stops tracing. Then, the
tracing result of each ports is dumped to the resultFile.
The whole graph network of the points mentioned above (start points, jump points, end
points and stop points) are dumped to the networkFile.

Tcl
proc ::npi_L1::npi_nl_trace_network_sig_2_sig { startFile endFile
resultFile
networkFile
{ passCellFile "" } { isPassCellPosList 1 }
{ mapFile "" } {linkFile "" }
{ isToBit 0 }
{ detailMode 0 } { networkStyle 0 } { depth 20 }
{ stopModFile "" }}

startFile

Specify the file name containing the full actual name / npiNlFullName of start nets, and the
trace direction of each net.

Format:
net_full_actual_name npiNlDriver/npiNlLoad Does not support wildcard.
endFile

Specify the file name containing the full actual name / npiNlFullName of end nets.
Wildcard supported. If one line has first character `#', it is treated as comment line.
resultFile

Specify the file name where the trace results of each start net is shown.
networkFile

Specify the file name where the network relationship is shown. To specify the complexity of
the network please refer to: detailMode.
passCellFile

Specify the file name containing the npiNlCellType that pass through and keep tracing. Nospecified type: tracing passes through module boundaries by default(npiNlCellType ==
npiNlModuleCell). If one line has first character `#', it is treated as comment line.
isPassCellPosList = 1, only the npiNlCellType listing in the file + npiNlModuleCell passes,
while others do not.
isPassCellPosList = 0, then npiNlCellType listing in the file does not pass through, while
others do.
isPassCellPosList

Specify whether the passCellFile is in positive listing. Default is 1.
mapFile

Specify the file name containing the module port mapping that jumps through while
tracing. The mapping should be 1-1 or 1-N or N-1 relationship. N-N is not supported.
Wildcard is supported. If one line has first character `#', it is treated as comment line.
Style:
1-1: modName in1 out1
N-1: modName { in1 in2 } out1
1-N: modName in1 { out1 out2 }
linkFile

Specify the file name containing the full actual name /npiNlFullNameof link points. A
link point is a npiNlPort or a npiNlInstPort that you want to observe in the network
graph. The graph recognizes the link point as a node, and therefore is also reported in
the network result. Wildcard is supported. If one line has first character `#', it is treated as
comment line.
isToBit

Specify whether the start net should split to bits before tracing. Default is 0.
detailMode

Specify how detail the network is, and how it affects the result of report path or network. By
default, 0, the network graph contains:
* the start ports and end ports,
* both sides of ports of mapping module,
* link ports that user wants to observe,
* the stop ports/instports and literal net that meet the stop conditions.
Note: The instports from the passCellFile are not a node in the network
graph for less complexity.
1. 1: adding all past ports of module into the graph.
2. 2: adding all instports of instance from symbol library.
3. 3: adding all past ports of module, and the past instports from the passCellFile into the
graph.

networkStyle

Specify which style the network file should be dumped. Default is 0, Text view.
1: json style

Text view and json style shows the actual name of each node in graph, along with its type,
direction if it is a port or instport, connected net if it is an instport, and value if it is a literal
net. It shows its instance information, including instance name, module name, cell type, file
name and begin line number. Also, it shows the driver/ load relationship of each node.
2: Tree view
Each tree starts from a no-driver node.
3: Tree view readable
Similar to 2. However for instport with non-intuitive netlist-gen name, it shows its
connected net's name instead for readability.

Specify the maximum tracing level. Default is 20.
stopModFile

Specify the file name containing the module names that stops tracing.
If the tracing program ended gracefully, the total number of start nets is returned.
Otherwise, returns 0.

All NPI VANL routines must be enclosed by npi_vanl_begin() and npi_vanl_end().

npiVanlBitValue_e defaultValue = NPI_VANL_X, npiVanlBeginType_e
beginType = npiVanlDefaultBegin);

scopeHierName

Specifies the full hierarchical name of the top boundary scope. When a specific scope is
set, any signal outside the scope is not considered. If it's NULL, all scopes are included.
defaultValue

Enum npiVanlBitValue_e is a four-state value set, especially used in NPI VANL Library.

Logical zero

NPI_VANL_1

NPI_VANL_X

NPI_VANL_Z

npiVanlBeginType_e is stated below:
npiVanlDefaultBegin

Default

Iterate whole design and search for literal nets
under top boundary scope, get their values and
call npi_vanl_set_value_by_hdl internally.

npi_nl_trace_network_port_2_inst
Report tracing result and the network between start ports and end instances based
on NPI Netlist model.
A general trace connection app is provided. The function starts tracing from the ports listed
in the startFile.
When tracing to a module listed in the modMap, it does not go into the module. Instead, it
jumps to the correspondent port and keep tracing.
There are some conditions for the program to stop tracing:
* First, it meets the floating ports/instports or constant-tied signal.
* Second, it meets the ports of end instance listed in the endFile.
* Third, it meets the instports of flip-flop cell.
* Fourth, it meets the instports of an instance whose npiNlCellType is not npiNlModule
nor listed in the passCellFile.
* Fifth, it meets ports of the top boundary module of the whole design.
* Sixth, it meets the instports of an instance whose module name is listed in the
stopModFile.
And last, if the tracing level exceed the depth user specified, it stops tracing.
In the end, the tracing result of each ports is dumped to the resultFile and the whole graph
network of the points mentioned above (start points, jump points, end points and stop
points) is dumped to the networkFile.

Tcl
proc ::npi_L1::npi_nl_trace_network_port_2_inst { startFile endFile
resultFile networkFile
{ passCellFile "" } { isPassCellPosList 1 }
{ mapFile "" } {linkFile "" }
{ isToBit 0 } { isEndAtModule 0 }
{ detailMode 0 } { networkStyle 0 } { depth 20 }
{ stopModFile "" } }

* startFile: Specify the file name containing the full actual name / npiNlFullName of
start ports, and the trace direction of each port.
Trace direction is optional. If trace direction is not specified, for output it traces load,
others trace the driver.
Format:
port_full_actual_name npiNlDriver/npiNlLoad

Wildcard supported for the ports' name for the following case:
- top.u1.p*
- top.u1.p*[1]
- top.u1.* // all ports under top.u1

* endFile: Specify the file name containing the end instances. It can be module
name, or the full actual name / npiNlFullName of end instances, according to the flag
isEndAtModule.
isEndAtModule = 0: full actual name / npiNlFullName of instances
isEndAtModule = 1: module name

Wildcard supported.
* resultFile: Specify the file name where the trace results of each start port is shown.
* networkFile: Specify the file name where the network relationship is shown. To
specify the complexity of the network, refer to detailMode.

* passCellFile: Specify the file name containing the npiNlCellType that passes through
and keep tracing. No-specified type: tracing only passes through module boundaries by
default. (npiNlCellType == npiNlModuleCell)
isPassCellPosList = 1, only the npiNlCellType listing in the file + npiNlModuleCell pass,
while others do not.
isPassCellPosList = 0, then npiNlCellType listing in the file does not pass through,
while others do.
* isPassCellPosList: Specify whether the passCellFile is in positive listing. Default is
1.
* mapFile: Specify the file name containing the module port mapping that jumps
through while tracing. The mapping should be 1-1 or 1-N or N-1 relationship. N-N is
not supported. Wildcard supported. If one line has first character `#', it is treated as
comment line.
* Style:
1-1: modName in1 out1
N-1: modName { in1 in2 } out1
1-N: modName in1 { out1 out2 }
linkFile

Specify the file name containing the full actual name / npiNlFullName of link points.
A link point is a npiNlPort or a npiNlInstPort that user particularly want to observe in the
network graph. The graph recognizes the link point as a node, thus also reported in the
network result.
Wildcard is supported. If one line has first character `#', it is treated as comment line.
* isToBit: Specify whether the start port should split to bits before tracing. Default is 0.
If the start ports is itself a npiNlPseudoPort name. For example, top.a[2:3]
from a npiNlPort top.a[0:3], it is always automatically split to bits.
* isEndAtModule: Specify whether the end file is stated in the "full actual name /
npiNlFullName" style (0), or the "module name" style (1) or mixed style(2). Default is 0.
* detailMode: Specify how detail the network is, and how it affects the result of report
path or network. By default, 0, the network graph contains:
The start ports and end ports
Both sides of ports of mapping module.

Link ports that you want to observe.
The stop ports or instports and literal net that meet the stop conditions.
0: The instports from the passCellFile is not a node in the network
graph for less complexity.
1: Adding all past ports of module into the graph.
2: Adding all instports of instance from symbol library.
3: Adding all past ports of module, and the past instports from the
passCellFile into the graph.

* networkStyle: Specify which style the network file should be dumped.
0: Text view (default).
1: json style.
Text view and json style shows the actual name of each node in graph, along with
its type, direction if it is a port or instport, connected net if it is an instport, and value
if it is a literal net.
It shows its instance information, including instance name, module name, cell type,
file name and begin line number. It also shows the driver or load relationship of
each node.
2: Tree view.
Each tree starts from a no-driver node.
3: Tree view readable.
Similar to 2. However for instport with non-intuitive netlist-gen name, it shows its
connected net's name instead for readability.

npi_nl_trace_network_sig_2_sig
Report tracing result and the network between start nets and end nets based on NPI
Netlist model.
A general trace connection app is provided. The function starts tracing from the nets listed
in the startFile. When tracing to a module listed in the modMap, it does not go into the
module. Instead, it goes to the corresponding port and keeps tracing.
There are some conditions for the program to stop tracing:
1. It meets the floating ports/instports or constant-tied signal.
2. It meets the nets listed in the endFile.
3. It meets the instports of flip-flop cell.
4. It meets the instports of an instance whose npiNlCellType is not npiNlModule nor
listed in the passCellFile.
5. It meets ports of the top boundary module of the whole design.
6. It meets the instports of an instance whose module name is listed in the stopModFile.
7. Finally, if the tracing level exceed the depth user specified, it stops tracing. Then, the
tracing result of each ports is dumped to the resultFile.
The whole graph network of the points mentioned above (start points, jump points, end
points and stop points) are dumped to the networkFile.

Tcl
proc ::npi_L1::npi_nl_trace_network_sig_2_sig { startFile endFile
resultFile
networkFile
{ passCellFile "" } { isPassCellPosList 1 }
{ mapFile "" } {linkFile "" }
{ isToBit 0 }
{ detailMode 0 } { networkStyle 0 } { depth 20 }
{ stopModFile "" }}

startFile

Specify the file name containing the full actual name / npiNlFullName of start nets, and the
trace direction of each net.

Format:
net_full_actual_name npiNlDriver/npiNlLoad Does not support wildcard.
endFile

Specify the file name containing the full actual name / npiNlFullName of end nets.
Wildcard supported. If one line has first character `#', it is treated as comment line.
resultFile

Specify the file name where the trace results of each start net is shown.
networkFile

Specify the file name where the network relationship is shown. To specify the complexity of
the network please refer to: detailMode.
passCellFile

Specify the file name containing the npiNlCellType that pass through and keep tracing. Nospecified type: tracing passes through module boundaries by default(npiNlCellType ==
npiNlModuleCell). If one line has first character `#', it is treated as comment line.
isPassCellPosList = 1, only the npiNlCellType listing in the file + npiNlModuleCell passes,
while others do not.
isPassCellPosList = 0, then npiNlCellType listing in the file does not pass through, while
others do.
isPassCellPosList

Specify whether the passCellFile is in positive listing. Default is 1.
mapFile

Specify the file name containing the module port mapping that jumps through while
tracing. The mapping should be 1-1 or 1-N or N-1 relationship. N-N is not supported.
Wildcard is supported. If one line has first character `#', it is treated as comment line.
Style:
1-1: modName in1 out1
N-1: modName { in1 in2 } out1
1-N: modName in1 { out1 out2 }
linkFile

Specify the file name containing the full actual name /npiNlFullNameof link points. A
link point is a npiNlPort or a npiNlInstPort that you want to observe in the network
graph. The graph recognizes the link point as a node, and therefore is also reported in
the network result. Wildcard is supported. If one line has first character `#', it is treated as
comment line.
isToBit

Specify whether the start net should split to bits before tracing. Default is 0.
detailMode

Specify how detail the network is, and how it affects the result of report path or network. By
default, 0, the network graph contains:
* the start ports and end ports,
* both sides of ports of mapping module,
* link ports that user wants to observe,
* the stop ports/instports and literal net that meet the stop conditions.
Note: The instports from the passCellFile are not a node in the network
graph for less complexity.
1. 1: adding all past ports of module into the graph.
2. 2: adding all instports of instance from symbol library.
3. 3: adding all past ports of module, and the past instports from the passCellFile into the
graph.

networkStyle

Specify which style the network file should be dumped. Default is 0, Text view.
1: json style

Text view and json style shows the actual name of each node in graph, along with its type,
direction if it is a port or instport, connected net if it is an instport, and value if it is a literal
net. It shows its instance information, including instance name, module name, cell type, file
name and begin line number. Also, it shows the driver/ load relationship of each node.
2: Tree view
Each tree starts from a no-driver node.
3: Tree view readable
Similar to 2. However for instport with non-intuitive netlist-gen name, it shows its
connected net's name instead for readability.

Specify the maximum tracing level. Default is 20.

npi_nl_trace_network_sig_2_inst
Report tracing result and the network between start nets and end instances based
on NPI Netlist model.
A general trace connection app is provided. The function starts tracing from the nets listed
in the startFile. When tracing to a module listed in the modMap, it does not go into the
module. Instead, it goes to the corresponding port and keeps tracing.
There are some conditions for the program to stop tracing:
1. It meets the floating ports or instports or constant-tied signal.
2. It meets the ports of end instance listed in the endFile.
3. It meets the instports of flip-flop cell.
4. It meets the instports of an instance whose npiNlCellType is not npiNlModule nor
listed in the passCellFile.
5. It meets ports of the top boundary module of the whole design.
6. It meets the instports of an instance whose module name is listed in the stopModFile.
7. Finally, if the tracing level exceed the depth user specified, it stops tracing. Then, the
tracing result of each ports is dumped to the resultFile.
The whole graph network of the points mentioned above (start points, jump points, end
points and stop points) are dumped to the networkFile.

Tcl
proc ::npi_L1::npi_nl_trace_network_sig_2_inst { startFile endFile
resultFile
networkFile
{ passCellFile "" } { isPassCellPosList 1 }
{ mapFile "" } {linkFile "" }
{ isToBit 0 } { isEndAtModule 0 }
{ detailMode 0 } { networkStyle 0 } { depth 20 } }
{ stopModFile "" } }

* startFile: Specify the file name containing the full actual name or npiNlFullName of
start nets, and the trace direction of each net.
Format:
net_full_actual_name npiNlDriver/npiNlLoad

Does not support wildcard.
* endFile: Specify the file name containing the end instances. It can be module name,
or the full actual name or npiNlFullName of end instances, according to the flag
isEndAtModule.
isEndAtModule = 0: full actual name / npiNlFullName of instances
isEndAtModule = 1: module name

Wildcard supported.
* resultFile: Specify the file name where the trace results of each start port is shown.
* networkFile: Specify the file name where the network relationship is shown. To
specify the complexity of the network, refer to detailMode.
* passCellFile: Specify the file name containing the npiNlCellType that passes through
and keep tracing.

No-specified type: tracing passes through module boundaries by default.
(npiNlCellType == npiNlModuleCell). If one line has first character `#', it is treated
as comment line.
isPassCellPosList = 1, only the npiNlCellType listing in the file + npiNlModuleCell
passes, while others do not.
isPassCellPosList = 0, then npiNlCellType listing in the file does not pass through,
while others do.
* isPassCellPosList: Specify whether the passCellFile is in positive listing. Default is
1.
* mapFile: Specify the file name containing the module port mapping that jumps through
while tracing.
The mapping should be 1-1 or 1-N or N-1 relationship. N-N is not supported. Wildcard
is supported. If one line has first character `#', it is treated as comment line.
* Style:
1-1: modName in1 out1
N-1: modName { in1 in2 } out1
1-N: modName in1 { out1 out2 }

* linkFile: Specify the file name containing the full actual name /npiNlFullName of
link points.
A link point is a npiNlPort or a npiNlInstPort that you want to observe in the
network graph.
The graph recognizes the link point as a node, and therefore is also reported in the
network result. Wildcard is supported. If one line has first character `#', it is treated as
comment line.
* isToBit: Specify whether the start net should split to bits before tracing. Default is 0.

fileName
Specifies the name of the file to be read.
File Format
"signal full hierarchy name" => "value string";
Each statement is separated by a line break. A value string is a string of value in
expression as a simple decimal number, or a based literal constant specified in decimal,
hexadecimal, octal, or binary format (example: 4'b1001), or structurally both with size
and base (example: {2'b10,2'b01}). Note that the full name exists in the netlist model, and
some signal in FSDB might be flattened in the netlist model that cannot set value.

while { [array anymore vc_array $tok] } {

proc npi_fsdb_sig_value_between { fsdb_file_hdl sig_name begin_time
end_time format vc_array }

vc_array

(Output) Array of value changes. Key is time; data is value.
Each time value is unique in this array.
When multiple value changes occur at one time snapshot, only the latest value is
recorded.
On success, return 1 and output vc_array.
FL_case10.tcl
set
set
set
set

sig_name "tb_CPUsystem.i_CPUsystem.i_CPU.i_CCU.MAselect"

if {[::npi_L1::npi_fsdb_sig_value_between $fsdb_file_hdl $sig_name
$begin_time $end_time npiFsdbBinStrVal "vc_array"] == 1 } {
puts "$sig_name between $begin_time ~ $end_time:"
set tok [array startsearch vc_array]
while { [array anymore vc_array $tok] } {
set key [array nextelement vc_array $tok]
lappend key_list $key
}
set key_list [lsort -integer $key_list]
foreach key $key_list {
puts "At time $key, Value = $vc_array($key)"
}
}

npi_l1_fsdb_sig_by_property
Query the signals by given property with specified FSDB file.

Predefine Data Type
There are several new data types related to this API.
1. typedef enum npiFsdbL1Bool
typedef enum npiFsdbL1Bool {
npiFsdbL1Unset = 0,
npiFsdbL1True,
npiFsdbL1False
npiFsdbL1Bool;
2. typedef struct npiFsdbL1PropertyStruct
This is the struct type for users to set querying constraints.
typedef struct npiFsdbL1Property_s{
const char* sigName = "";
npiFsdbL1Bool real = npiFsdbL1Unset;
npiFsdbL1Bool MDA = npiFsdbL1Unset;
const char* leftRange = "";
const char* rightRange = "";
const char* rangeSize = "";
const char* direction = "";
const char* assertionType = "";
const char* compositeType = "";
} npiFsdbL1PropertyStruct;

For all the constraints except sigIsReal, they are defined as constant character pointer
type and the simple expression is supported.
For example, if the querying constraints are as below.
1. Signal name is "i_BJsource" or "MAselect".
2. Range size is between 10 and 20.
3. Direction type is input or inout.

To set these constraints, the following is a partial extract of sample code.
npiFsdbL1Property_spropStruct;
propStruct.sigName = " sig == \"i_BJsource\" || sig == \" MAselect \" ";
propStruct.rangeSize = "sig>10 && sig< 20";
propStruct.direction = "sig == \"input\" || sig == \"inout\"";

There are several rules that need to be noticed.
1. Except sigName, all constraints are not case sensitive which means both lowercase
and capital are acceptable. For example, propStruct.direction = "input" and
propStruct.direction = "INPUT" are with same meaning, which is to set the
direction as input.
2. For the non-numeral identifier , it should be marked by "\" ". As the example above, the
signal name expression is
propStruct.sigName = " sig == \"i_BJsource\" || sig == \" MAselect \"
";

The two identifier, i_BJsource and MAselect are marked as \"i_BJsource\" and \"
MAselect \".
3. For each equivalence, the operand name should be "sig". Any other operand name is
invalid and makes this API calling invalid.
For example, propStruct.rangeSize = "a>10 && a< 20" ; is an invalid expression
since the operand name is a instead of sig.
Signal Name Constraint
For querying array signal, the expression should be declaration name without the
dimension. For example, if there is a signal array named "Card[3:0]", to querying this
signal, the given constraint should be as below.
propStruct.sigName = " sig == \"Card\" ";

The following expressions are not legal for this case.
propStruct.sigName = " sig == \"Card[3:0]\" "; // invalid. Should not
include dimension
propStruct.sigName = " sig == \"Card[1]\" "; // invalid. Should not
include dimension

MDA Constraint
For the querying constraint MDA, it means if the signal has the array with more than two
dimension or not. If this constraint is true, all the signals which have the array with more
than two dimension is queried. Note that the any two dimension or multi-dimension arrays
inside composite signals (struct, union, ) are not considered in this constraint.

Direction Constraint
For the constraint direction, the allowable const char* is as below.
* Input
* Output
* Inout
These are not case sensitive but it is failed if any other const char* is given.
There is an example for this constraint.
npiFsdbL1Property_spropStruct;
propStruct.direction = "sig == \"INOUT\""; // legal, since it is not case
sensitive

Assertion Type Constraint
For the constraint assertion type, the allowable const char* is as below.
* Assert

These are not case sensitive but it is failed if any other const char* is given.
Composite Type Constraint
* Array
* Struct
* Union
* TaggedUnion
* Record
These are not case-sensitive but it is failed if any other const char* is given.

Supported Logic Symbols
For this API, there are several symbols supported in expression, such as the following:
1. && (AND)
2. || (OR)
3. == (equal)
4. <= (Less than or equal to)
5. < (Less than)
6. >= (Greater than or equal to)
7. > (Greater than)
8. * (wildcard, signal name constraint only)

npi_pw_get_supply_network_path
Find paths in the power supply network.
Trace drivers and loads of the given from/through/to supply port handle vectors.
Uses the Power Model.
The supply network path consists of supply port and supply net.
It is collected into a specified vector (C++) or list (Tcl).

int npi_pw_get_supply_network_path(const pwHdlVec& fromPortHdlVec, const
pwHdlVec& throughPortHdlVec, const pwHdlVec& toPortHdlVec, psnPathVec_t&
psnPathVec);

fromPortHdlVec / throughPortHdlVec / toPortHdlVec

Specify the reference of the vector for supply port handles and "pwHdlVec_t" is a typedefine for "vector <npiPwHandle>".
psnPathVec

Specify the reference of the vector where supply network paths is collected. The typedefine "psnPathVec_t" is list as follows:
struct psnNode_s {

npiPwHandle supplyPortHdl; // supply port handle
npiPwHandle supplyNetHdl; // supply net handle connect to the load supply port
This field identifies the supply net connected to the load supply port.
bool isPowerSwitchPort; // true if supplyPortHdl is power switch port
Set this field to true when supplyPortHdl is a power switch port.
bool isPrimaryPowerNet; // true if supplyNetHdl is primary power net
bool isPrimaryGroundNet; // true if supplyNetHdl is primary ground net
} psnNode_t;
typedef vector <psnNode_t> psnPath_t;
typedef vector <psnPath_t> psnPathVec_t;

}
{
npiPwHandle hdl = NULL;
pwHdlVec_t fromPortHdlVec, throughPortHdlVec, toPortHdlVec;
psnPathVec_t psnPathVec;
hdl = npi_pw_handle_by_name( "TOP/VDD", npiPwSupplyPort );
fromPortHdlVec.push_back(hdl);
hdl = npi_pw_handle_by_name( "TOP/SW/sout", npiPwSupplyPort );
throughPortHdlVec.push_back(hdl);
int num = npi_pw_get_supply_network_path(fromPortHdlVec,
throughPortHdlVec, toPortHdlVec, psnPathVec);
printf("%d supply network path found:\n", num);
npi_pw_supply_network_path_dump(psnPathVec[i]);
}
}

Specifies the ID of the object to be modified. For illegal case, see Illegal Cases for Object
ID.

The attribute value represented by multiple bits. For each bit, its value can be
0,1,x(X),z(Z). If the attribute value length is not equal to expected value length, this API is
failed and returns 0. Note that the attribute length more than 64 bits is supported.

set_object_attribute_value_int
This method specifies the value of an integer attribute for an object. This method can be
called up until the point at which the object is ended; however, only the last specified value
is associated with the attribute.

NPI_INT32 set_object_attribute_value_int(
cosnt char* attribute_name,
NPI_INT64
NPI_INT64
expected_value,
npiTrIntBits num_bits,
npiFsdbwRadix radix = npiFsdbwDec);

Specifies the UID of the object to be modified. For illegal case, see Illegal Cases for Object
ID.

Specifies the attribute value. The data types are as following.
NPI_INT64: it represents long integer type.
NPI_UINT64: it represents unsigned long integer type.

Specifies the expected attribute value. If this value differs from "attribute_value", the object
num_bits (NPI_INT64 only)

Number of bits of integer attribute.
The enumerate type is as below.
typedef enum npiTrIntBits {
npiTrInt8B, // 8 bits integer
npiTrInt16B, // 16 bits integer
npiTrInt32B, // 32 bits integer
npiTrInt64B // 64 bits integer
}npiTrIntBits;
Note that for unsigned integer (NPI_UINT64), the bit size is 64 bits only.

npi_tr_writer_create_bit_vector_value
This method is to create a multiple bits vector. You can use it to create a bit vector as
argument of method set_object_attribute_value_bit_vector().
string bitVector = npi_tr_writer_create_bit_vector_value
// bitVector: "00000000101"
tr_writer-> set_object_attribute_value_bit_vector(obj_id,
"attr_bit_vec", bitVector);
(5, 11);

const char* bitVector =
npi_tr_writer_create_bit_vector_value (bitVector, "x1z1", 11);
//
bitVector: "0000000x1z1"
tr_writer-> set_object_attribute_value_bit_vector(obj_id,
"attr_bit_vec", bitVector);

string npi_tr_writer_create_bit_vector_value(
NPI_INT64 value, unsigned int num_bits);
const char* value, unsigned int num_bits);

value (NPI_INT64 or const char*)

The target value. It can be either 64-bits integer or string.
For example, if this argument is set to integer "7" and the num_bits is set to 4, the
vector_value is "0111". If it is set to string "01xz" and the num_bits is set to 6, the
vector_value is "0001xz".
num_bits

The number of bits in vector_value.
If num_bits is less than value length, the value is truncated to fit the exact size.
On success, the bit vector string is returned.

For example, if this argument is set to "7" and the num_bits is set to 4, the vector_value is
"0111". If it is set to string "01xz" and the num_bits is set to 6, the vector_value is "0001xz".
num_bits

The number of bits in vector_value.
value_type

1. STRING
2. NPI_INT64

NPI_INT32 npi_tr_writer_FSDB_open(
const char* name,
const char* unit,
npiFsdbTime time = 0);

Specifies the name of the FSDB file. If it is NULL, an error is issued and this API fails.
Each FSDB file must have a unique name. If the name is same as any of the existing
FSDB files, this API fails and returns a NULL pointer.
unit (C-based)
Specifies the scale unit of this file. For example, if the scale unit should be set as 10 ns,
you can provide a string "10 ns" as a unit for this API. The legal scale unit should be as [1,
10, 100] [s, ms, us, ns, ps, fs] (these are case sensitive and only lower cases are allowed).
An error is issued and it is set as 1 ns if any other value is provided.
time (C-based)
Specifies the begin time of simulation for this FSDB file. If the provided time is a negative
value, a warning is issued and it is set as 0.

npi_hier_tree_trv_chk_skip_cb
Register callback function to skip traverse for npi_hier_tree_trv

The API npi_hier_tree_trv_chk_skip_cb provides a solution to determine whether
the traverse can be stopped during execution of npi_hier_tree_trv. The API
npi_hier_tree_trv_chk_skip_cb creates the association between npi_hier_tree_trv
and user-defined callback function/data for specified object types. When a handle
is retrieved by npi_hier_tree_trv, the registered callback function is called. The
callback function must return a boolean value. Once the returned value returns 'true',
npi_hier_tree_trv stops exploring any relationship of the handle; likewise, if the
callback function returns false, the traverse continues and the callback function of
npi_hier_tree_trv_register_cb is executed. The registered callback function/data is
reset by the API npi_hier_tree_trv_reset_cb.
Also refer to npi_hier_tree_trv, npi_hier_tree_trv_register_cb, and
npi_hier_tree_trv_reset_cb.
The object (npiHandle) is passed as an argument to the callback function and
be released when the execution of callback function is done. If users want to
preserve the object, npi_set_permanent_handle can be used to set the object
as "permanent".
Object types recognized by npi_hier_tree_trv_chk_skip_cb are identical with
npi_hier_tree_trv_register_cb.

npi_nl_set_black_box
Set a module as black box.
This API affects the trace results of APIs: npi_nl_trace_driver/load series,
npi_nl_sig_2_reg_conn series including fanIn/fanOut, and npi_nl_trace_network series.

npi_nl_set_black_box ( const char* modName );

modname

Specify the module name.
If success, return true.

Tcl
proc ::npi_L1:: npi_nl_set_black_box { modName }

modname

Specify the module name.
If success, return 1.
If a module is set to be black box, then its instances (cell should be npiNlModuleCell) are
treated as black boxes.
When tracing from outside of those black box instances, it does not trace into the instance.
Instead, it passes through the instance according to the direction of its instports.
Basically the behavior is the same as npiNlMacroCell:
1. When tracing load of an input instport (pi), it gets all the output (po) and inout (pio)
instports of the instance.
2. When tracing driver of an output instport (po), it gets all the input (pi) and inout (pio)
instports of the instance.
3. When tracing load of an inout (pio) instport, it gets all the output (po) and inout instports
of the instance despite itself, and the load of the other side (p).
4. When tracing driver of an inout (pio) instport, it gets all the input (pi) and inout instports
of the instance despite itself, and the driver of the other side.

This method is to create a multiple bits vector. You can use it to create a bit vector as
argument of method set_object_attribute_value_bit_vector().
string bitVector = npi_tr_writer_create_bit_vector_value
// bitVector: "00000000101"

"attr_bit_vec", bitVector);
(5, 11);

const char* bitVector =
npi_tr_writer_create_bit_vector_value (bitVector, "x1z1", 11);
//
bitVector: "0000000x1z1"
tr_writer-> set_object_attribute_value_bit_vector(obj_id,
"attr_bit_vec", bitVector);

string npi_tr_writer_create_bit_vector_value(
NPI_INT64 value, unsigned int num_bits);
const char* value, unsigned int num_bits);

value (NPI_INT64 or const char*)

The target value. It can be either 64-bits integer or string.
For example, if this argument is set to integer "7" and the num_bits is set to 4, the
vector_value is "0111". If it is set to string "01xz" and the num_bits is set to 6, the
vector_value is "0001xz".
num_bits

The number of bits in vector_value.
If num_bits is less than value length, the value is truncated to fit the exact size.
On success, the bit vector string is returned.

"0111". If it is set to string "01xz" and the num_bits is set to 6, the vector_value is "0001xz".

npi_tr_writer_FSDB_open

NPI_INT32 npi_tr_writer_FSDB_open(
const char* name,
const char* unit,
npiFsdbTime time = 0);

Specifies the name of the FSDB file. If it is NULL, an error is issued and this API fails.
Each FSDB file must have a unique name. If the name is same as any of the existing
FSDB files, this API fails and returns a NULL pointer.
unit (C-based)
Specifies the scale unit of this file. For example, if the scale unit should be set as 10 ns,
you can provide a string "10 ns" as a unit for this API. The legal scale unit should be as [1,
10, 100] [s, ms, us, ns, ps, fs] (these are case sensitive and only lower cases are allowed).
An error is issued and it is set as 1 ns if any other value is provided.
time (C-based)
Specifies the begin time of simulation for this FSDB file. If the provided time is a negative
value, a warning is issued and it is set as 0.

scale_unit

you can provide a string "10 ns" as a unit for this API. The legal scale unit must be as [1,

10, 100] [s, ms, us, ns, ps, fs] (these are case sensitive and only lower cases are allowed).
An error is issued and scale unit is set as 1 ns if any other value is provided.

Specifies the begin time of simulation for this FSDB file. If time is omitted, the begin time

npi_hier_tree_trv_register_cb
Register callback function for npi_hier_tree_trv.
The npi_hier_tree_trv_register_cb API associates a user-defined callback function and
data with npi_hier_tree_trv.
You can register callbacks for object types that can be iterated from a scope.
npi_hier_tree_trv calls the registered callback when it traverses the corresponding object
type.
Also refer to npi_hier_tree_trv, npi_hier_tree_trv_chk_skip_cb and
npi_hier_tree_trv_reset_cb.
The object (npiHandle) is passed as an argument to the callback function and
be released when the execution of callback function is done. If users want to
preserve the object, npi_set_permanent_handle can be used to set the object
as "permanent".

Object types recognized by npi_hier_tree_trv_register_cb:
npiAlways
npiAssignStmt
npiFor
npiFuncCall
npiPackedArrayVar
npiShortRealTypes

npi_nl_set_black_box
Set a module as black box.
This API affects the trace results of APIs: npi_nl_trace_driver/load series,
npi_nl_sig_2_reg_conn series including fanIn/fanOut, and npi_nl_trace_network series.

npi_nl_set_black_box ( const char* modName );

modname

Specify the module name.
If success, return true.

Tcl
proc ::npi_L1:: npi_nl_set_black_box { modName }

modname

Specify the module name.
If success, return 1.
If a module is set to be black box, then its instances (cell should be npiNlModuleCell) are
treated as black boxes.
When tracing from outside of those black box instances, it does not trace into the instance.
Instead, it passes through the instance according to the direction of its instports.
Basically the behavior is the same as npiNlMacroCell:
1. When tracing load of an input instport (pi), it gets all the output (po) and inout (pio)
instports of the instance.
2. When tracing driver of an output instport (po), it gets all the input (pi) and inout (pio)
instports of the instance.

of the instance despite itself, and the load of the other side (p).
4. When tracing driver of an inout (pio) instport, it gets all the input (pi) and inout instports
of the instance despite itself, and the driver of the other side.

npi_expr_decompile
Decompile the target expression. The expression includes SV expression and VHDL
expression.
The API npi_expr_decompile decompiles the npiHandle object and return a string
functionally equivalent to the original source code.

const char* npi_expr_decompile ( npiHandle exprHdl, bool constSize=false,
resConstOpr=false );

constSize

If this variable is true, the value of size appends before constant. The default value is
false.
resConstOpr

Option to resolve value of operations that are composed by constants or generate
variables. The default value is false. This option is only available in SystemVerilog.
A string representing the decompiled result of the given expression handle. If the input
handle is not an expression, an empty string ("") is returned.

include"npi.h"
include"npi_L1.h"
int main(int argc,char** argv)
{

// Usage of constSize
npiHandle paramHdl = npi_handle_by_name("top.P2",NULL);
npiHandle paramRhsHdl = npi_handle(npiExpr, paramHdl);
printf("RHS of P2: %s\n", npi_expr_decompile(paramRhsHdl));
printf("RHS of P2 with constant size: %s\n",
npi_expr_decompile(paramRhsHdl, true/*constSize*/));
// Usage of resConstOpr
npiHandle varHdl = npi_handle_by_name("top.a", NULL);
npiHandle varRhsHdl = npi_handle(npiExpr, varHdl);
printf("RHS of a: %s\n", npi_expr_decompile(varRhsHdl));
printf("RHS of a and resolve operation: %s\n",
npi_expr_decompile(varRhsHdl, false/*constSize*/, true/*resConstOpr*/));

}

The NPI Netlist API npi_nl_ut_filter_port_instport filters the npiNlPortType of all handles in

Filtering uses either a positive or negative list.
The filtered result is collected into another specified vector (C++) or array (Tcl).

Resolve an expression handle to a bit vector.
The API npi_get_bit_blasted_expr resolves an expression to a bit vector. The bit
vector contains full name of a signal handle or 1-bit constant value.

typedef std::vector<string> stringVec_t;

bitVec/*O*/ );

bitVec

A vector of bit information. The bit information is one of the following types:
(1) A constant: 1'b1, 1'b0, 1'bx, or 1'bz
(2) Full name of a signal, for example, top.mod.sig
The vector stores information from MSB to LSB. bitVec[0] is MSB and
bitVec[bitVec.size()-1] is LSB.
Bit length of the expression. If the expression is not supported, the API returns -1.

design files. In the NPI Text model, you can use two APIs -- npi_text_property() and
npi_text_property_str() to query the attribute's integer value or string value.

typedef void* npiIC;
npiIC npi_ic_construct (int leftAry[],
int rightAry[],
unsigned int size,
int isInc);
/*
@description
Construct an npiIC handle.
@parameter leftAry
Specify an integer array containing the left ends of intervals.
@parameter rightAry
Specify an integer array containing the right ends of intervals.
@parameter size
Specify the size of leftAry/rightAry.
@parameter isInc
Specify the interval type.
If isInc == 1, leftAry[i] <= rightAry[i],
otherwise, leftAry[i] >= rightAry[i].
@return value
The npiIC handle.
@note
For the following cases, the API returns NULL.
- if isInc == 1 and there is any i such that leftAry[i] >
rightAry[i].
- if isInc != 1 and there is any i such that leftAry[i] <
rightAry[i].

Appendix E: KP&L
* Text Model Limitations

Text Model Limitations
1. The same file name cannot exist in design files. Always try to use the full file name to
specify a file.
In the current NPI Text Model, the simple file name is unique.
If two files in different directories share the same file name and you pass the simple
name to npi_text_file_by_name, only one file handle is returned.
The returned handle belongs to the first loaded file with that simple name.
In this case, use npi_text_file_by_name.
Pass a full name as the input argument to get the correct file handle object.
2. The change of macro text of a macro does not take effect until the changed macro text
file is written out and the files that use this macro in Verdi system are imported again.
This also means that if you change macro text and call npi_text_expand_macro, text
substitution may be unexpected.
The substitution still uses the original macro text for macro_name.
3. The nested macro is expanded at once. Partial expand is not supported.
4. The manipulation APIs do not concurrently change the element order in a
npiIterHandle object unless using traversal API to update the change.
Some manipulation APIs change the order between lines and words.
These changes do not affect existing npiIterHandle objects.
To update the change, get a new npiIterHandle by calling npi_text_iter_start().
If you use an old npiIterHandle after npi_text_delete_line or
npi_text_delete_word, you might access a NULL handle.

model does not support adding a line handle in this file.
6. If there is only a line handle and this line handle does not have any word handle, using
npi_text_replace_line() to add content creates the corresponding word handles.

Introduction
As designs incorporate more (and more complex) standard protocols, the engineers
tasked with verifying the behavior of those designs find themselves faced with a variety
of new challenges. Not only must they understand the domain-specific aspects of the
design they are verifying, they must also understand the operation of the incorporated
protocols and how those protocol interfaces interact with the design. Learning about a
new protocol, or coming up to speed on updates to a well-established protocol might
represent significant effort for design verification teams. Large SOCs that incorporate
multiple protocol blocks further exacerbate these issues.
The complexity of modern protocols also creates a significant challenge for many
traditional debug methodologies.
Some methodologies use a bottom-up approach. This approach extracts information from
simulation log or waveform dump files. It then attempts to transform this low-level data into
more easily analyzed higher-level representations. But this approach assumes not only
that all of the required high-level information can be inferred from the low-level data. It also
assumes that this approach is reasonably efficient.
Alternatively, the debug process might use a top-down approach. That is, this approach
might be forced, particularly when a test environment focuses primarily on higher-level
transactions. But top-down methodologies rarely offer adequate insight into the underlying
simulation details. These details are often required to uncover the ultimate cause of
unexpected behavior.

The scope of complex protocol definitions is broad. It extends from the lowest physical
details (such as the analog behavior exhibited by a PHY) up to the edge of (and
sometimes into) the software domain. This highlights the challenges faced by verification
teams who want to add home-grown support for a particular protocol to a verification
environment.
This also illustrates two important requirements for a protocol-oriented analysis tool.
First, a protocol-oriented analysis tool must be able to represent and view protocol data
at multiple levels of abstraction. Second, the tool must be extensible, such that these
protocol-oriented analysis capabilities can be made available for in-house, internallydeveloped or proprietary protocol VIPs.
The Verdi Protocol Analyzer is designed to address these challenges. The Verdi Protocol
Analyzer accelerates the investigation of protocol behavior by providing protocol-oriented

analysis and debugging capabilities in verification environments that use Synopsys
Verification IP.
These capabilities not only reduce the time required to identify the source of bugs that
can be directly attributed to protocol behavior, but also provide insight into aspects of the
operation of a design that might otherwise be overlooked. With the addition of VC Apps
Protocol Analyzer, these same benefits can be extended to in-house, internally-developed
or proprietary protocol VIPs.
Starting with the Verdi L-2016.06 release, the VC Apps Protocol Analyzer APIs were
enhanced to support the recording of memory data of in-house, internally-developed
or proprietary protocol VIPs. The use of these APIs allow you to visualize memory data
using the Verdi Memory Browser. This is fully integrated with other transaction-based and
general Verdi capabilities.
This document describes the overall VC Apps Protocol Analyzer integration process
as well as the specific steps that are required to integrate a protocol VIP into the Verdi
Protocol Analyzer environment.

Tool Flow
In the hardware world, bus analyzers and packet analyzers are widely used to debug
hardware issues. These analyzers display information at a higher level of abstraction than
more traditional logic analyzers that work at the signal level.
The Verdi Protocol Analyzer provides similar capabilities for verification engineers who
are working with RTL and face many of the same debug challenges. The Verdi Protocol
Analyzer brings all of the design and test environment debug information into one place
and provides a protocol aware environment to simplify root-cause analysis.
During simulation, the VIP captures protocol-specific data using code that is either
designed into the Synopsys VIP or added to an in-house or custom VIP as part of the VC
Apps Protocol Analyzer integration process. As the VIP interacts with the design, it creates
a high-level record of transactions and other interesting protocol-specific activity such as
the values of internal state machines. This protocol-specific (and simulation-specific) data

Integration Process Overview

is stored in a common FSDB database along with the other design information, such as
waveforms, source code, stack traces, and so on.
The Verdi Protocol Analyzer uses this data in conjunction with protocol knowledge
provided by the Synopsys VIP (or created as part of the VC Apps Protocol Analyzer
integration process) to create a higher-level, interactive display of the protocol-related
activity and provide comprehensive protocol-oriented analysis and debug capabilities.
The protocol-related activity can also be synchronized with other design-related debug
information (such as signal activity and simulation log messages) to enable easy
correlation of errors (or other unexpected behavior) with protocol activity.
